description: Crop and animal production, hunting and related service activities
detailled_description:
This division encompasses the two primary pillars of the agricultural sector: the production of crop products and the production of animal products. It covers the entire spectrum of primary agricultural activities, including soilless cultivation such as hydroponics and aquaponics, as well as essential service activities incidental to agriculture, hunting, trapping, and related operations.

This includes, among others:

*   **Crop Production:** The cultivation of non-perennial crops including cereals, legumes, oil seeds, vegetables, industrial fiber crops, and ornamental plants (011), as well as the cultivation of perennial crops such as fruits, nuts, berries, beverage crops (coffee, tea, cocoa), and spices (012). It also includes the production of vegetative plant materials and nursery operations for propagation (013).
*   **Animal Production:** The farming, husbandry, and breeding of all terrestrial animals (014). This covers the management of livestock—including cattle, buffaloes, equines, camelids, sheep, goats, and swine—as well as poultry, beekeeping, and the raising of specialty animals such as insects and pets.
*   **Mixed Farming:** The integrated, non-specialized production of both crops and animals within the same agricultural unit (015).
*   **Support and Post-Harvest Services:** Professional support activities provided on a fee or contract basis for both crop and animal production (016). This includes soil preparation, planting, spraying, and harvesting services, as well as animal husbandry services like artificial insemination and sheep shearing. It further encompasses post-harvest activities such as cleaning, grading, drying, and disinfecting to prepare agricultural products for primary markets (016).
*   **Hunting and Trapping:** The commercial taking of wild animals, whether dead or alive, for food, fur, skins, research, or population control (017).

This does not include the subsequent industrial processing of agricultural products into finished goods (classified under divisions 10, 11, and 12), nor does it include the construction of agricultural land (e.g., drainage or terracing, classified in section F). Additionally, this division excludes the marketing of farm products by third-party buyers or cooperative associations (section G) and landscape service activities (class 81.30).

details.includes:
This division includes two basic activities, namely the production of crop products and the production of animal products. 

Mixed farming (group 01.5) breaks with the usual principles for identifying the main activity. It accepts that many agricultural units have a reasonably balanced production of crops and animals, and that it would be arbitrary to classify them in one category or the other.

This division includes the soilless cultivation of crops, such as using hydroponic and aquaponic methods.
details.alsoIcludes: This division also includes service activities incidental to agriculture, as well as hunting, trapping and related activities.
details.excludes:
Agricultural activities exclude any subsequent processing of the agricultural products (classified under divisions 10, 11 and 12), beyond that needed to prepare them for the primary markets. The preparation of products for the primary markets is included here.

This division excludes field construction (for example, agricultural land terracing, drainage, preparing rice paddies) classified in section F and buyers and cooperative associations engaged in the marketing of farm products classified in section G. Also excluded are landscape service activities, which are classified in class 81.30.

detailled_description:
This group encompasses the cultivation of non-perennial crops, defined as plants that do not persist beyond two growing seasons, including the cultivation of these plants for the specific purpose of seed production. This category covers a broad spectrum of agricultural activities ranging from food staples and industrial raw materials to ornamental plants.

This includes, among others:

*   **Cereals, Legumes, and Oil Seeds:** The cultivation of wheat, grain maize, sorghum, barley, rye, oats, millet, and pseudocereals (quinoa, amaranth, chia), as well as leguminous crops (beans, lentils, peas, lupines) and oil seeds (soya beans, groundnuts, mustard, rapeseed, sunflower) (0111). This also includes the cultivation of rice (0112).
*   **Vegetables, Roots, and Tubers:** The growing of leafy, stem, fruit-bearing, and root vegetables, including potatoes, sweet potatoes, cassava, yams, mushrooms, truffles, melons, and sweetcorn (0113).
*   **Industrial and Fiber Crops:** The cultivation of sugar cane (0114), unmanufactured tobacco (including preliminary on-site processing) (0115), and various fiber crops such as cotton, jute, flax, hemp, and sisal (0116).
*   **Other Non-Perennial Crops:** The growing of forage crops (e.g., clover, alfalfa, maize for fodder), flower seeds, and ornamental plants, including the cultivation and cutting of flowers (0119).

This does not include the growing of rice (0112), sweetcorn (0113), or maize, lupines, and kale for fodder (0119) when classified specifically within other classes, nor does it include the cultivation of oleaginous fruits (0126), spices, aromatic, drug and pharmaceutical crops (0128), or mushroom spawn (0130). Furthermore, it excludes the preparation of tobacco leaves by third parties (0163) and the industrial manufacture of tobacco products (1200).

detailled_description:
This group encompasses the cultivation of perennial crops, defined as plants that persist for more than two growing seasons, either by surviving continuously or by dying back and regrowing each season. The scope includes the production of these crops for consumption, industrial processing, and seed production.

The activities within this category are organized into the following clusters:

*   **Fruit and Nut Cultivation:** This includes the growing of grapes for fresh consumption or processing into wine, juice, and dried fruit (0121); tropical and subtropical fruits such as bananas, avocados, and mangoes (0122); citrus fruits including oranges and lemons (0123); pome and stone fruits such as apples, cherries, and plums (0124); and a wide variety of berries, edible nuts (e.g., almonds, walnuts), and other tree or bush fruits like locust beans (0125). It also includes the cultivation of oleaginous fruits, specifically coconuts, olives, and oil palms (0126).
*   **Beverage and Spice Crops:** This comprises the cultivation of beverage crops including coffee, tea, maté, and cocoa (0127), as well as perennial and non-perennial spices, aromatic plants (e.g., pepper, cinnamon, vanilla, hops, ginger), and drug or narcotic crops. This cluster also includes the sun-drying of these crops when performed in association with the growing process (0128).
*   **Other Perennial Plant Production:** This includes the cultivation of rubber trees for latex, Christmas trees, trees for sap extraction, and vegetable materials used primarily for plaiting (0129).

This group does not include the growing of perennial flowers or other ornamental plants (0119); the gathering of wild sap or gums (0230); the processing of crops into finished goods such as wine (1102) or fruit juice (1032); the industrial drying of spices by third parties (0163); or the cultivation of oil seeds like soya beans and groundnuts (0111).

This category encompasses the production of all vegetative plant materials intended for propagation, ornamental use, or further cultivation. It focuses on the professional nursery operations required to supply live plants, grafting stock, and specialized biological materials for agricultural and horticultural purposes.

This includes, among others:
*   **Vegetative Planting Materials:** The production of cuttings, suckers, and seedlings for direct propagation or for creating grafting stock (0130).
*   **Nursery Operations:** The cultivation of live plants for bulbs, tubers, roots, slips, and mushroom spawn, as well as the operation of non-forestry tree nurseries (0130).
*   **Ornamental and Landscaping Materials:** The growing of plants specifically for ornamental purposes, including the cultivation of turf for transplanting (0130).

This does not include the growing of plants for the purpose of seed production (classified under 01.1 and 01.2) or the operation of forest tree nurseries (classified under 02.10).

This category encompasses the farming, husbandry, and breeding of all terrestrial animals, excluding aquatic species. It covers the management of livestock for meat, dairy, fiber, and reproductive materials, as well as the farming of specialized animals such as poultry, insects, and pets.

This includes, among others:
*   **Cattle and Buffaloes:** The raising and breeding of dairy cattle and buffaloes, including the production of raw milk and bovine semen (0141), as well as the raising of cattle and buffaloes for meat, draft purposes, or fighting (0142).
*   **Equines and Camelids:** The breeding and raising of horses, asses, mules, and hinnies (0143), as well as camels and other camelids (0144).
*   **Small Livestock:** The raising of sheep and goats, including the production of raw milk and raw wool (0145), and the raising and breeding of swine and pigs (0146).
*   **Poultry:** The farming of various poultry species (such as chickens, turkeys, ducks, geese, quails, ostriches, and guineafowls), the operation of poultry hatcheries, and the production of eggs (0147).
*   **Other Animals:** The raising and breeding of semi-domesticated and specialty animals, including rabbits, fur animals, and reindeer (0148). This also includes beekeeping and the production of honey and wax; the raising of silkworms; the farming of insects, land molluscs, and land snails; the raising of reptiles (excluding crocodiles); and the breeding of pets (e.g., cats, dogs, and birds).

This does not include: farm animal boarding and care (01.62); sheep shearing on a contract basis (01.62); the production of hides and skins from slaughterhouses (10.11) or from hunting and trapping (01.70); the production of pulled wool (10.11) or feathers and down (10.12); the processing of milk (10.51); the operation of racing and riding stables without breeding activities (93.19); the operation of shelters or boarding/training facilities for pets (96.99); or any activities related to aquatic animals, including fish farming, ornamental fish, or the farming of frogs, crocodiles, and marine worms (03.2, 03.21, 03.22).

description: Support activities to agriculture and post-harvest crop activities
detailled_description:
This category encompasses a wide range of specialized services provided to the agricultural sector, including support activities for crop and animal production performed on a fee or contract basis, as well as essential post-harvest processing of agricultural products. It covers the entire lifecycle of professional assistance required to maintain production systems, optimize yields, and prepare harvests for the primary market.

The scope of this category includes the following functional areas:

*   **Crop Production Support:** This covers activities related to the cultivation cycle, such as field preparation, planting, irrigation equipment operation, crop spraying, pruning, and harvesting. It also includes the provision of agricultural machinery with operators and the maintenance of land to keep it in good condition without active production (0161).
*   **Animal Production Support:** This encompasses services designed to promote animal propagation, growth, and output. Key activities include herd testing, artificial insemination, stud services, sheep shearing, farm animal boarding and care, coop cleaning, and the services of farriers (0162).
*   **Post-Harvest and Seed Processing:** This includes activities aimed at preparing products for primary markets or propagation. This consists of cleaning, grading, trimming, disinfecting, waxing, and drying various crops (including fruits, vegetables, tobacco, and cocoa). It further includes specialized processes like cotton ginning, plant retting, artificial fruit ripening, and the processing and treatment of seeds to ensure quality for storage and marketing (0163).

This category does not include the preparation of agricultural products by the producer themselves; agricultural research and development; veterinary and animal vaccination services; pet boarding; landscape architecture and gardening; drainage of agricultural land; or the wholesale and marketing of agricultural raw materials.

description: Hunting, trapping and related service activities
detailled_description:
This category covers the commercial hunting and trapping of wild animals, as well as the related service activities involved in these operations. It encompasses the systematic taking of wildlife for various economic purposes, including food production, commercial skin and fur processing, and scientific or recreational exhibition.

This category includes, among others:
*   **Commercial hunting and trapping:** The taking of wild animals (dead or alive) for food, fur, skins, or hides, as well as for use in research, zoos, or as pets (0170).
*   **Specific animal collection:** The catching of frogs and the collection of snails in the wild (0170).
*   **Land-based marine and predator management:** The land-based catching of sea mammals, such as walruses or seals, as well as the hunting of foxes, minks, and wolves for livestock protection and general animal population control (0170).

This does not include the raising of game animals on ranching operations (01.4); the production of bird or reptile skins from farming/ranching (01.48); pest control services related to agriculture (01.61); whaling (03.11); the production of hides and skins from slaughterhouses (10.11); hunting for sport, recreation, or associated service activities (93.19); or service activities specifically aimed at promoting hunting and trapping (94.99).

This division encompasses the complete lifecycle of forest resource management, ranging from the cultivation and maintenance of timber tracts to the commercial harvesting of wood and the extraction of various wild-growing, non-wood forest products. It also includes the provision of specialized support services performed on a fee or contract basis to facilitate forestry and logging operations.

This division includes, among others:

*   **Silviculture and Forest Management:** The cultivation, conservation, and management of natural, semi-natural, and planted forests, including the operation of forest tree nurseries for forestry purposes, the planting and thinning of timber, and the growing of specific wood types like poplar and willow (021).
*   **Logging and Timber Production:** The harvesting and production of roundwood, including timber intended for industrial processing or for use in an unprocessed form, such as pit-props, fence posts, and utility poles. This also covers the production of traditional forest by-products, such as charcoal produced within the forest, and the gathering of forest residues like brushwood, stumps, and wood chips (022).
*   **Extraction of Non-Wood Forest Products:** The commercial gathering of naturally occurring, wild-growing forest resources, including edible products (mushrooms, truffles, berries, nuts), botanical substances (cork, resins, balsams, gums, mosses, lichens), and wild-harvested herbs (023).
*   **Forestry Support Services:** Professional services performed on a fee or contract basis, such as forest inventory, management consulting, timber valuation, forest fire and pest control, and the transport of logs within the forest environment (024).

This division does not include the further industrial processing of wood, such as sawmilling and planing (division 16); the agricultural cultivation of products (division 01); the operation of tree nurseries not intended for forest trees (01.30); the growing of Christmas trees (01.29); landscaping and arboriculture services (81.30); the draining of forestry land or site clearing (43.12); or the conservation and maintenance of national parks and nature reserves (91.42).

This division encompasses the commercial harvesting of wild aquatic organisms and the organized production of aquatic species through aquaculture. It covers the full spectrum of activities involved in capturing, culturing, and farming marine, brackish, and freshwater life, as well as the specialized support services required to maintain these operations.

This division includes the following clusters of activity:

*   **Capture Fishery:** This involves the commercial harvesting, collecting, and gathering of wild aquatic organisms from oceanic, coastal, and inland waters. Activities range from the taking of finfish, crustaceans, and molluscs to the gathering of marine and freshwater materials, including pearls, sponges, corals, and algae (Fishing, 031).
*   **Aquaculture (Aquafarming):** This includes the production processes designed to increase the yield of aquatic organisms beyond natural environmental capacities through regular stocking, feeding, and protection. This covers the breeding, rearing, and farming of fish, molluscs, crustaceans, amphibians, and aquatic plants in marine, brackish, or freshwater environments (Aquaculture, 032).
*   **Support Activities:** This covers services incidental to both fishing and aquaculture, including technical and administrative support, such as diving services for aquaculture management, the maintenance of specialized cultivation equipment (e.g., fish cages), and professional fishery control and guard services (Support activities for fishing and aquaculture, 033).

This division does not include the processing of fish, crustaceans, or molluscs, whether performed at land-based plants or on factory ships (10.20); the building and repairing of ships and boats (30.11, 30.13, 33.15, 33.18); or any activities related to sport or recreational fishing, including the operation of sport fishing preserves (93.19).

These activities involve the removal of species for human consumption or other purposes using diverse methods ranging from manual collection to specialized fishing gear.

The scope of this category is organized into the following areas:

*   **Marine Capture:** This includes commercial fishing operations in ocean and coastal waters, such as the taking of marine crustaceans, molluscs, and various marine aquatic animals (e.g., turtles, sea squirts, tunicates, and sea urchins). It also encompasses the hunting of whales and the gathering of marine materials and organisms, including pearls, sponges, coral, and marine algae (Marine fishing, 0311).
*   **Inland Water Capture:** This includes commercial fishing activities conducted in inland water bodies, as well as the collection of freshwater crustaceans, molluscs, and other freshwater aquatic animals, along with the gathering of freshwater materials like seaweed and algae (Freshwater fishing, 0312).

This category does not include the processing of fish, crustaceans, molluscs, or whales on factory ships or in factories ashore (10.11, 10.20), nor does it include the capturing of marine mammals other than whales, such as seals and walruses (01.70). Furthermore, it excludes the catching of frogs and collection of snails in the wild (01.70), the collection of wild plants such as reeds and sedges (02.30), the rental of pleasure boats with crew for fishing trips (50.10), fishing inspection and patrol services (84.24), and any fishing practiced for sport or recreation, including the operation of sport fishing preserves (93.19).

This category encompasses the production process of aquaculture, which involves the culturing, farming, and harvesting of aquatic organisms using techniques designed to increase production beyond natural environmental capacities. It covers the rearing of organisms—such as fish, molluscs, crustaceans, plants, and amphibians—through juvenile or adult phases under captive or artificial conditions, including individual, corporate, or state ownership throughout the rearing stage.

This category includes the following key operational areas:

*   **Marine and Brackish Water Aquaculture (0321):** This includes the farming of marine fish, including ornamental varieties, and the culture of crustaceans, bivalves, and other molluscs in seawater or brackish water. It also covers land-based aquaculture in salt-water tanks, the operation of marine fish hatcheries, the production of bivalve spat and shrimp post-larvae, the cultivation of marine microalgae, and the growing of seaweed.
*   **Freshwater Aquaculture (0322):** This includes the farming of freshwater fish and ornamental freshwater species, as well as the culture of freshwater crustaceans, bivalves, and other aquatic animals. It also encompasses the operation of freshwater fish hatcheries, the farming of frogs, the growing of seaweed and algae, and the cultivation of freshwater microalgae.

Mining and quarrying include the extraction of minerals occurring naturally as solids (coal and ores), liquids (petroleum) or gases (natural gas). Extraction can be achieved by different methods (for example, underground or surface mining, well operation, seabed mining).

This section includes supplementary activities aimed at preparing the crude materials for marketing (for example, crushing, grinding, cleaning, drying, sorting, concentrating ores and liquefaction of natural gas). 

Mining activities are classified into divisions, groups and classes on the basis of the principal mineral produced. Divisions 05 and 06 are concerned with mining and quarrying of fossil fuels (coal, lignite, petroleum, gas); divisions 07 and 08 concern metal ores, various minerals and quarry products. 

Some of the technical operations of this section, particularly related to the extraction of hydrocarbons, may also be carried out for third parties by specialised units as an industrial service activity which is reflected in division 09.

description: Extraction of crude petroleum and natural gas
detailled_description:
This division encompasses the industrial activities involved in the extraction of crude petroleum and natural gas from the earth, including the operation and development of oil and gas fields. It covers the production of primary hydrocarbons, the mining of oil-bearing materials, and the necessary field-level processing required to prepare these resources for transport.

This division includes, among others, the following clusters of activity:

*   **Extraction of Crude Petroleum:** This includes the primary extraction of crude petroleum oils and the production of crude oil from unconventional sources, such as oil shale and tar sands (0610). It also encompasses initial processing activities essential for the preparation of crude oil, such as decantation, desalting, dehydration, stabilization, and the operation of emulsion breakers and separators (0610).
*   **Extraction of Natural Gas:** This covers the production of crude gaseous hydrocarbons (natural gas) and the extraction of condensates (0620). It includes technical processes to prepare gas for distribution, such as gas desulphurisation, the separation of liquid hydrocarbon fractions, and the extraction of coal mine methane and coal seam gas (0620).
*   **Field Operations:** The division includes the general operation and development of oil and gas fields, including drilling, completing, and equipping wells, as well as the maintenance of field-gathering lines up to the point of shipment from the producing property (0610, 0620).

This division does not include:
- Support activities for oil and gas extraction performed on a fee or contract basis, including exploration, test drilling, and site preparation (09.10).
- The refining of petroleum products and the recovery of liquefied petroleum gases during the refining process (19.20).
- The manufacture of industrial gases (20.11).
- The operation of long-distance transport pipelines (49.50).
- Geophysical, geologic, and seismic surveying services (71.12).

This division encompasses the extraction and preparation of metallic minerals (ores) through underground or open-cast mining methods, as well as seabed mining. It includes the essential ore dressing and beneficiating operations, such as crushing, grinding, washing, drying, sintering, calcining, leaching, gravity separation, and flotation.

The division is structured into two primary thematic areas:

*   **Iron Ore Mining:** This includes the extraction and preparation of ores valued primarily for their iron content (071).
*   **Non-Ferrous Metal Ore Mining:** This includes the mining and concentration of various metallic ores, categorized as follows:
    *   **Radioactive metal ores:** The mining of ores valued for their uranium and thorium content, including pitchblende and the production of yellowcake (0721).
    *   **Base, industrial, and precious metal ores:** The mining and preparation of ores for aluminium (bauxite), copper, lead, zinc, tin, manganese, chrome, nickel, cobalt, molybdenum, tantalum, vanadium, lithium (spodumene), as well as precious metals such as gold, silver, and platinum (0729).

This division does not include the roasting of iron pyrites (20.13), the enrichment of uranium and thorium ores (20.13), the production of aluminium oxide (24.42), the operation of blast furnaces (division 24), the production of uranium metal (24.46), or the production of copper or nickel mattes (24.44/24.45). Furthermore, it excludes the extraction and preparation of pyrites and pyrrhotite (except for roasting processes), which are classified under class 08.91.

This division encompasses the extraction of minerals from mines, quarries, and alluvial deposits, as well as the utilization of salt marshes and dredging operations. It focuses on the primary extraction and initial preparation of raw materials essential for the construction, chemical, and manufacturing industries.

This includes, among others:

*   **Construction and Industrial Minerals:** The quarrying of monumental and building stones (such as marble, granite, and sandstone), as well as the extraction of limestone, gypsum, anhydrite, chalk, and uncalcined dolomite (081). This also includes the extraction and dredging of industrial and construction sand, gravel, and various types of clay, including refractory clays and kaolin (081).
*   **Chemical, Fertilizer, and Specialized Minerals:** The extraction of minerals utilized as chemical raw materials, such as natural phosphates, potassium salts, native sulphur, pyrites, barytes, fluorspar, and lithium produced from brine (089). This cluster also covers the extraction of salt via underground mining or the evaporation of saline waters, the harvesting and preparation of peat, and the extraction of specialized materials including gemstones, asbestos, graphite, talc, feldspar, mica, quartz, and various abrasive materials (089).
*   **Primary Processing:** Essential on-site activities such as crushing, grinding, cutting, cleaning, drying, sorting, and mixing of the extracted minerals (081, 089).

This division does not include the subsequent processing or manufacturing of mineral products (such as the manufacture of calcined dolomite, the production of synthetic fertilizers, or the processing of salt for food-grade retail), which are classified under section C. Additionally, it excludes the mining of bituminous sand, the cutting or shaping of stone performed outside of quarry sites, the manufacture of peat-based products, and service activities incidental to mining.

This division encompasses specialized support services incidental to mining, quarrying, and the extraction of petroleum and natural gas, provided strictly on a fee or contract basis. It covers the technical and operational tasks required throughout the exploration, development, and production phases for a wide range of mineral and energy resources.

This includes, among others:

*   **Exploration and Prospecting:** Services related to the assessment of prospective sites, including traditional prospecting methods, geological observations, the collection of core samples, and test drilling or hole boring for both oil and gas wells and other mineral deposits (091, 099).
*   **Drilling and Well-Site Services:** Specialized operations such as directional drilling and redrilling, derrick erection and dismantling, cementing well casings, and well-site maintenance activities including "spudding in," cleaning, bailing, and swabbing (091).
*   **Operational Support and Infrastructure Maintenance:** Essential field operations such as draining and pumping of mines and oilfields, as well as the demolition, dismantling, and securing of mine shafts, tunnels, and underground facilities (091, 099).
*   **Specialized Field Services:** On-site services for oil and gas fields, such as fire prevention and firefighting, as well as the liquefaction and regasification of natural gas when conducted directly at the mine site for transport purposes (091).

This does not include the actual operation of mines, quarries, or oil and gas fields on a contract or fee basis (divisions 05, 06, 07, and 08); specialized repair and maintenance of drilling and extraction machinery and equipment (33.12); specialized offshore installation, repair, and maintenance of equipment integral to floating platforms (division 43); geophysical surveying services provided on a contract or fee basis (71.12); or the liquefaction and regasification of natural gas for transport purposes when not performed at the mine site (52.21, 52.22).

details.includes:
This section includes the physical, mechanical, chemical or biological transformation of materials, substances, or components into new products, although this cannot be used as the single universal criterion for defining manufacturing (see remark on processing of waste below). The materials, substances, or components undergoing transformation are either raw materials or products of agriculture, forestry, fishing, mining or quarrying as well as products of other manufacturing activities. Substantial alteration, renovation or reconstruction of goods is generally considered to be manufacturing.

The output of a manufacturing process may be finished in the sense that it is ready for use or consumption, or it may be semi-finished in the sense that it is to become an input for further manufacturing. For example, the output of alumina refining is the input used in the primary production of aluminium; primary aluminium is the input to aluminium wire drawing; aluminium wire is the input for the manufacture of fabricated wire products.

Manufacture of specialised components and parts of, and accessories and attachments to machinery and equipment is, as a general rule, classified in the same class as the manufacture of the machinery and equipment for which the parts and accessories are intended. Manufacture of unspecialised components and parts of machinery and equipment (for example, engines, pistons, electric motors, electrical assemblies, valves, gears, roller bearings, is classified in the appropriate class of manufacturing, without regard to the machinery and equipment in which these items may be included.

Making specialised components and accessories by moulding or extruding plastics materials is usually included in group 22.2.

Assembly of the component parts of manufactured products is considered manufacturing. This includes the assembly of manufactured products from either self-produced or purchased components. 

The recovery of waste, in other words, the processing of waste into secondary raw materials* is classified in group 38.2. While this may involve physical, mechanical, biological or chemical transformations, this is not considered to be a part of manufacturing activities. The primary purpose of these activities is considered to be the treatment or processing of waste and they are therefore classified in section E. However, the manufacture of new products from secondary raw materials is classified in manufacturing, even if these processes use waste as an input (for example, the production of silver from film waste is considered to be a manufacturing process).

Specialised maintenance and repair of industrial, commercial and similar machinery and equipment is, in general, classified in division 33. However, the repair and maintenance of computers, personal and household goods, motor vehicles and motorcycles is classified in division 95.

The installation of machinery and equipment, when carried out as a specialised activity, is classified in class 33.20.

Maintenance, repair and installation of equipment that forms an integral part of buildings or similar structures (for example, maintenance, repair and installation of escalators or of air-conditioning systems, is classified as construction in section F, if carried out at the construction site). 

This section also contains the activities of factoryless goods producers (FGPs) in manufacturing (see introductory guidelines, paragraph xx).

As a general rule, the activities in the manufacturing section involve the transformation of materials into new, rebuilt and remanufactured products. Their output is a new product. As clarification, the following activities are considered manufacturing in NACE:
- fresh fish processing (oyster shucking, fish filleting), not done on a fishing boat, see 10.20
- milk pasteurising and bottling, see 10.51
- leather converting, see 15.11
- wood preserving, see 16.12
- printing and related activities, excluding published goods, see 18.1
- tyre retreading, see 22.11
- ready-mixed concrete production, see 23.63
- galvanising, electroplating, plating, etc., and other metallic or non-metallic coating of metals, see 25.51
- heat treatment of metals, see 25.52
- refilling of ink cartridges, see 26.20
- refilling or recharging of fire extinguishers, see 28.29
- rebuilding or remanufacture of machinery (e.g. automobile engines), see 29.10
- assembly provided by a seller or blending of several products to be sold. If assembly is provided by a contractor, this activity should be classified in manufacturing.

Conversely, there are activities that, although sometimes involving transformation processes, are classified in other sections of NACE; in other words, they are not considered as manufacturing. They include:
- logging, classified in section A
- beneficiating of agricultural products, classified in section A
- preparation of food for immediate consumption on the premises, classified in division 56
- beneficiating of ores and other minerals, classified in section B
- production of gaseous fuels for energy supply through a permanent network, classified in section D
- production of compost from organic waste, classified in section E
- assembly provided as part of a delivery or by a seller; however, if assembly is the main activity provided by a contractor, it is classified in manufacturing
- activities of breaking bulk and redistribution in smaller lots, including packaging, repackaging, or bottling products (e.g. as liquors or chemicals); sorting and reselling of scrap; mixing paints to customer order; cutting metals to customer order; treatment not resulting in a different good, classified in section G
- publishing and the combined activities of publishing and printing, classified in section J

Note: * secondary raw materials are materials and products which can be used as raw materials by simple reuse, or via recycling and recovery.

This division encompasses the industrial processing of products derived from agriculture, forestry, and fishing into food and beverages for human consumption, as well as the production of prepared feeds for animals. The scope covers the entire transformation process—ranging from primary slaughtering and milling to the manufacturing of complex, value-added food products—and includes production for own account as well as custom processing for third parties.

This division includes, among others, the following clusters of activities:

*   **Meat and Seafood Processing:** The slaughtering and dressing of animals and poultry, including the rendering of fats and the production of fresh, chilled, or frozen meat products (101). This also includes the industrial processing and preservation of fish, crustaceans, and molluscs through freezing, drying, smoking, or canning, as well as the production of fishmeal (102).
*   **Plant-based Food Processing:** The preservation of fruits, vegetables, and potatoes (103), the extraction and refining of vegetable and animal oils and fats, including the production of spreads and margarine (104), and the milling of grains and cereals into flour, starches, and related ingredients (106).
*   **Dairy and Bakery Production:** The manufacturing of a wide array of dairy products, such as liquid milk, cheese, and yoghurt, as well as the production of edible ice (105). Additionally, it covers the production of bread, fresh and dry pastry goods, biscuits, and farinaceous products like pasta and couscous (107).
*   **Specialized Food and Animal Feed:** The manufacture of various sugar and confectionery products, coffee, tea, condiments, sauces, and specialized nutritional foods such as infant formula and ready-made meals (108). This also includes the production of prepared animal feeds and pet food, including the conversion of food industry by-products into nutritional formulations (109).

This division does not include the preparation of meals for immediate consumption (division 56), the production of plant-based milk substitutes (11.07), the manufacture of essential oils and specialized chemical treatment of fats (20.59), or the gathering of raw agricultural products (division 01). Furthermore, it excludes the manufacturing of spirits, beer, wine, and soft drinks (division 11) and the primary processing performed on active fishing vessels (03.11).

details.includes:
This division includes the processing of products of agriculture, forestry and fishing into food for humans or animals, and includes the production of various intermediate products that are not directly food products. The activity often generates associated products of greater or lesser value (for example, hides from slaughtering, or oilcake from oil production).

This division is organised by activities dealing with different kinds of products: meat, fish, fruits and vegetables, fats and oils, milk products, grain mill products, animal feed and other food products. Production can be carried out for own account, as well as for third parties, as in custom slaughtering.

Some activities are considered manufacturing even though there is retail sale of the products in the producers’ own shop (for example, those activities performed in bakeries, pastry shops and prepared meat shops which sell their own production). However, where the processing is minimal and does not lead to a real transformation, the unit is classified to section G.
details.alsoIcludes: This division also includes the manufacture of liquids considered food or that use similar manufacturing processes (for example, milk and fruit juice/ concentrate).
details.excludes: This division excludes the preparation of meals for immediate consumption, see division 56.

description: Processing and preserving of meat and production of meat products
detailled_description:
This category encompasses the industrial activities involved in the slaughtering, processing, and preservation of meat and poultry, as well as the manufacturing of various meat-based products. It covers the entire value chain from the initial dressing of carcasses to the production of specialized, value-added meat preparations.

The scope of this category includes the following areas:

*   **Slaughtering and Primary Processing:** This includes the operation of slaughterhouses for the killing, dressing, and packing of meat, including beef, pork, lamb, rabbit, mutton, and camel (1011), as well as poultry (1012). It also covers the production of fresh, chilled, or frozen meat in carcasses or cuts (1011) and individual poultry portions (1012). 
*   **By-product Processing and Specialized Treatments:** Activities include the processing of animal offal, the rendering and refining of edible animal fats (including poultry fats) (1011, 1012), and the handling of by-products such as the production of hides and skins originating from slaughterhouses, and the processing of pulled wool (1011). Furthermore, it includes the cleaning, disinfecting, and treatment of feathers and down (1012).
*   **Meat Products Manufacturing:** This involves the production of preserved meat through methods such as cooking, drying, salting, or smoking (1013). It also encompasses the creation of various meat products, including sausages, salami, puddings, andouillettes, saveloys, bolognas, pâtés, rillettes, and boiled ham (1013).

This category does not include the manufacture of prepared meat and poultry dishes (1085), the manufacture of soups containing meat (1089), or the wholesale trade of meat (4632).

description: Processing and preserving of fish, crustaceans and molluscs
detailled_description:
This category encompasses the industrial processing and preservation of aquatic organisms, specifically fish, crustaceans, and molluscs, for both human consumption and animal feed. It covers a wide range of preservation techniques, including freezing, drying, smoking, canning, and other methods of curing, as well as the initial preparation of raw aquatic products.

This includes, among others:
*   **Preservation and Processing Methods:** The preparation and preservation of fish, crustaceans, and molluscs through freezing, deep-freezing, drying, cooking, smoking, salting, and immersion in brine (1020).
*   **Product Manufacturing:** The production of various fish, crustacean, and mollusc products, such as fish fillets, roes, caviar, and caviar substitutes (1020).
*   **Industrial By-products and Specialized Processing:** The production of fishmeal for human or animal consumption, as well as meals and solubles derived from fish and other aquatic animals unfit for human consumption (1020). This category also encompasses the processing of seaweed and specialized mechanical preparation, such as removing fish heads, gutting, and filleting for freezing (1020).
*   **Factory Vessel Operations:** The activities of factory vessels that are not engaged in active fishing but are dedicated exclusively to the processing and preserving of aquatic organisms (1020).

This does not include the processing and preserving of fish performed on vessels that are actively engaged in fishing (03.11), the processing of whales (10.11), or the production of oils and fats derived from fish and marine mammals (10.41). Furthermore, it excludes the manufacture of prepared fish dishes (10.85) and the production of fish soups (10.89).

description: Processing and preserving of fruit and vegetables
detailled_description:
This category covers industrial activities related to the processing and long-term preservation of fruits, vegetables, and potatoes. It encompasses a wide range of transformation techniques, including freezing, drying, canning, and various mechanical preparation methods such as peeling and cutting.

The scope of this category includes the following areas:

*   **Potato Processing:** The industrial preparation of potato-based products, including the manufacture of prepared frozen potatoes, dehydrated mashed potatoes, potato snacks, crisps, flour, and meal, as well as the peeling and cutting of fresh potatoes (10.31).
*   **Fruit and Vegetable Juices:** The manufacture of fruit and vegetable juices, including the production of concentrates from fresh produce (10.32).
*   **Other Fruit, Vegetable, and Nut Processing:** The preservation of fruits, nuts, and vegetables via freezing, drying (including freeze-drying and infrared), canning, or immersion in oil or vinegar. This also includes the manufacture of jams, marmalades, table jellies, nut pastes, and processed nut foods. Furthermore, this category covers the production of perishable prepared vegetable products, such as packaged salads, peeled or cut vegetables, and tofu (10.39).

This category does not include the manufacture of beverages produced with fruit nectars (11.07), the manufacture of flour or meal of dried leguminous vegetables (10.61), the preservation of fruits and nuts in sugar (10.82), the manufacture of prepared vegetable dishes (10.85), or the manufacture of artificial concentrates (10.89).

description: Manufacture of vegetable and animal oils and fats
detailled_description:
This category covers the industrial production, processing, and refining of vegetable and animal oils and fats for both edible and non-edible use. It encompasses the transformation of raw materials into base oils, fats, and specialized spreads intended for human consumption or industrial application.

This category includes the following areas:

*   **Production of Vegetable and Animal Oils:** This involves the manufacturing of crude and refined vegetable oils (e.g., olive, soya-bean, hemp, sunflower seed, and rape oil) and the extraction of fish and marine mammal oils (10.41). It also covers the processing of vegetable oils through techniques such as blowing, boiling, dehydration, and hydrogenation, as well as the production of non-defatted flour or meal from oilseeds, nuts, and kernels, and the manufacture of non-edible animal oils and fats (10.41).
*   **Edible Fats and Spreads:** This includes the manufacture of margarine, melanges, and similar spreads, as well as the production of compound cooking fats (10.42).
*   **Residual Products:** The category includes the production of cotton linters, oilcakes, and other residual products resulting from oil production processes (10.41).

This category does not include the rendering or refining of lard and other edible fats derived from bovine animals, sheep, goats, or pigs (10.11), the rendering of edible poultry fats (10.12), or the production of corn oil and wet corn milling (10.62). Furthermore, it excludes the manufacture of essential oils and the treatment of oils and fats through specialized chemical processes (20.59).

description: Manufacture of dairy products and edible ice
detailled_description:
This category covers the industrial production of various dairy-based products and the manufacture of edible ice products intended for consumption. It encompasses the processing of raw milk into a wide range of dairy staples, as well as the specialized production of frozen desserts.

This category includes the following key areas:

*   **Dairy Processing:** This includes the production of fresh, pasteurized, sterilized, homogenized, or ultra-heat treated liquid milk and cream (1051), as well as the manufacture of concentrated or dried milk, whether sweetened or unsweetened (1051). It also covers fermented and processed dairy products such as yoghurt, milk-based drinks, kefir, cheese, curd, whey, casein, and lactose (including lactose-free variants and syrups) (1051).
*   **Edible Ice:** This includes the manufacturing of ice cream and various forms of edible ice, such as sorbets (1052).

This group excludes the production of raw milk from cattle (01.41) or other animals such as sheep, goats, or camels (01.43, 01.44, 01.45), and the production of dairy-based infant formulae or dietary drinks (10.86). Furthermore, it does not include the manufacture of cheese substitutes (10.89), plant-based milk substitutes (11.07), or fruit and water kefirs (11.03). Finally, it excludes the production of ice from natural water intended for cooling purposes (35.30) and the retail service activities of ice cream parlours (56.1).

description: Manufacture of grain mill products, starches and starch products
detailled_description:
This category encompasses the processing of agricultural raw materials into essential food ingredients, specifically covering the milling of various grains and vegetables, and the industrial production of starches and their derivatives. It includes activities ranging from traditional grain processing and rice milling to the sophisticated chemical and physical extraction of starch products.

This category includes, among others:

*   **Grain and Vegetable Milling:** The production of flour, semolina, groats, meal, or pellets from wheat, rye, oats, maize, and other cereals (1061). This also includes rice milling (husked, polished, or parboiled), the milling of dried leguminous vegetables, roots, tubers, or nuts (1061), and the manufacture of cereal breakfast foods (1061).
*   **Flour-based Preparations:** The production of flour mixes, as well as prepared blended flour and dough for bakery products such as bread, cakes, biscuits, and pancakes (1061).
*   **Starch Production:** The manufacture of starches from rice, potatoes, maize, and other sources, as well as specialized processes like wet corn milling (1062).
*   **Starch Derivatives and Related Products:** The manufacture of glucose, glucose syrup, maltose, inulin, gluten, tapioca and tapioca substitutes, and corn oil (1062).

This does not include the preparation of crops for primary markets (e.g., cleaning, trimming, or grading) or grain drying performed on a fee or contract basis (01.63). It also excludes the manufacture of potato flour and meal (10.31), the production of cane or beet sugar (10.81), and the manufacture of lactose (milk sugar) (10.51).

description: Manufacture of bakery and farinaceous products
detailled_description:
This category encompasses the industrial production of a wide range of bakery and farinaceous food products, including both fresh and shelf-stable goods. It covers the transformation of flour and other ingredients into staple baked items, dry snacks, and various pasta-based foods.

This category includes the following logical clusters:

*   **Fresh Bakery Products:** The manufacture of bread, rolls, and fresh pastry goods such as cakes, pies, tarts, pancakes, and waffles, including pre-baked bread products (1071).
*   **Dry Bakery and Preserved Products:** The production of rusks, biscuits, and other dry bakery items, as well as preserved pastry goods and waffles. This cluster also includes the manufacture of sweet or salted snack products like cookies, crackers, and pretzels, along with the production of breadcrumbs from toasted bread (1072).
*   **Farinaceous Products:** The manufacture of various pasta products (e.g., macaroni and noodles), whether cooked, stuffed, or in their raw state, as well as the production of couscous (1073).

This category also encompasses the specialized production of gluten-free bakery and farinaceous goods across these segments.

This does not include:
*   The manufacture of potato-based snacks (1031).
*   The retail sale of bread and rolls baked on-premises from pre-baked products (4724).
*   The manufacture of prepared meals or dishes based on pasta or couscous (1085).
*   The manufacture of soups containing pasta (1089).

This category encompasses the manufacture of a diverse range of food products not classified elsewhere, including sugar, confectionery, coffee, tea, seasonings, prepared meals, and specialized nutritional food products. It focuses on processed and manufactured food items intended for resale rather than immediate preparation or consumption.

This category includes the following logical clusters:

*   **Sugar and Confectionery:** The refining and manufacture of sugar (sucrose) and syrups (10.81), as well as cocoa products, chocolate, sugar confectionery, chewing gum, and sugar-preserved fruits or nuts (10.82).
*   **Beverage Bases:** The processing of coffee (roasting, decaffeinating, extracts) and tea/maté (blending, extracts, herb infusions), including products packaged in pods or capsules (10.83).
*   **Condiments and Seasonings:** The manufacture of spices, sauces, condiments (such as mayonnaise and mustard), vinegar, and the processing of food-grade salt (10.84).
*   **Prepared Meals and Dishes:** The production of frozen or canned ready-made meals containing at least two distinct main ingredients, such as meat, fish, pasta, or vegetable dishes (10.85).
*   **Specialized Nutrition:** The manufacture of homogenised food preparations, infant formulae, baby foods, weight-control foods, and products for medical dietary purposes (10.86).
*   **Other Food Products (n.e.c.):** A wide variety of products, including soups and broths, fresh (perishable) prepared foods like sandwiches, yeast, egg products, meat/cheese substitutes, processed honey, and insect-based food preparations (10.89).

This category does not include the gathering of wild maple syrup (02.30); the manufacture of glucose, lactose, or inulin (10.62); the production of spirits, beer, wine, or soft drinks (division 11); the preparation of meals in restaurants or catering services (56.2); the wholesale or retail trade of food products (46.38, 47.11, 47.27); the preparation of botanical products for pharmaceutical use (21.20); or the production of fresh fruit and vegetable-based prepared foods (10.39).

This category encompasses the industrial production of prepared animal feeds and feed supplements intended for both farm animals and household pets. It covers the processing, formulation, and manufacturing of balanced nutritional products tailored to specific animal dietary requirements.

This category includes the manufacture of prepared feed for farm animals, such as concentrated animal feed and feed supplements, as well as the preparation of unmixed single feed for livestock (1091). It also includes the production of prepared feed for pets, including dogs, cats, birds, and fish (1092). Furthermore, these activities comprise the processing of food industry waste and slaughterhouse by-products into formulated animal feeds (1091, 1092).

This does not include the manufacture of meat products (10.13), the production of fishmeal for animal feed (10.20), or the manufacture of oilseed cake (10.41). Additionally, it excludes activities that result in by-products usable as animal feed without further special treatment, such as certain oilseeds (10.41) or grain milling residues (10.61).

This division encompasses the manufacture of beverages, ranging from non-alcoholic refreshments and mineral waters to alcoholic products produced through fermentation or distillation, as well as the production of malt. The scope covers the entire spectrum of drink production, including the processing and bottling of liquids for human consumption.

This category includes the following logical clusters:

*   **Distilled and Fermented Alcoholic Beverages:** This includes the manufacture of distilled, potable alcoholic beverages such as whisky, brandy, gin, and liqueurs, along with the blending of spirits and the production of neutral spirits (11.01). It also encompasses the production of grape-based wines, including sparkling, fortified, and concentrated must-based wines, as well as aromatised wines like vermouth (11.02, 11.04). Additionally, it covers other fermented beverages such as cider, perry, mead, sake, and various fruit wines or mixtures of fermented and non-alcoholic beverages (11.03).
*   **Brewing and Malt Production:** This includes the production of malt liquors, such as beer, ale, porter, and stout (including low-alcohol or non-alcoholic variants) (11.05), as well as the production of malt derived from barley, wheat, or other grains (11.06).
*   **Non-Alcoholic Beverages:** This includes the production of natural mineral waters, bottled waters, and soft drinks, such as lemonade, cola, and tonic waters (11.07). It further includes fruit nectar beverages and plant-based milk substitutes, such as almond, rice, or soya-based drinks (11.07).

This division does not include: the production of fruit and vegetable juices (10.32), milk-based drinks (10.51), coffee, tea, and maté products (10.83), or the manufacture of malt extracts and syrups (10.89). It also excludes the manufacture of synthetic or fermented ethyl alcohol for industrial purposes (20.14) and services involving solely the bottling and labelling of beverages, which are classified under wholesale (46.34) or contract-based packaging activities (82.92).

This division includes the manufacture of alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages, as well as the production of malt, which serves as a key raw material for brewing. The scope covers the entire spectrum of drink production, ranging from fermented and distilled spirits to soft drinks and mineral waters.

This category includes the following logical clusters:

*   **Distilled and Fermented Alcoholic Beverages:** This includes the manufacture of distilled, potable alcoholic beverages such as whisky, brandy, gin, and liqueurs, as well as the blending of spirits and production of neutral spirits (11.01). It also encompasses the production of grape-based wines (including sparkling, fortified, and wine from concentrated must) and aromatised wines such as vermouth (11.02, 11.04). Additionally, it covers other fermented beverages, including cider, perry, mead, sake, and fruit wines, as well as mixtures of fermented and non-alcoholic beverages (11.03).
*   **Brewing and Malt Production:** This includes the production of malt liquors, including beer, ale, porter, and stout, as well as low-alcohol or non-alcoholic variants (11.05). It also includes the production of malt derived from barley, wheat, or other grains (11.06).
*   **Non-Alcoholic Beverages:** This includes the production of natural mineral waters, bottled waters, and soft drinks, such as lemonade, cola, and tonic waters (11.07). It further includes fruit nectar beverages and plant-based milk substitutes (e.g., almond, rice, or soya-based drinks) (11.07).

This category does not include: the production of fruit and vegetable juices (10.32), milk-based drinks (10.51), coffee, tea, and maté products (10.83), or the manufacture of malt extracts and syrups (10.89). It also excludes the manufacture of synthetic or fermented ethyl alcohol for industrial purposes (20.14) and services involving solely the bottling and labelling of beverages, which are classified under wholesale (46.34) or contract-based packaging activities (82.92).

This division encompasses the entire industrial value chain of textile production, ranging from the initial processing of raw fibres into yarns to the weaving of fabrics, the final finishing processes, and the manufacture of specialized textile articles. It covers a broad spectrum of applications, including household, industrial, and technical textiles, while excluding the garment-making industry.

This includes, among others:

*   **Preparation and Spinning:** The industrial activities involved in the treatment and processing of natural, man-made, and recycled fibres, including reeling, washing, scouring, carding, combing, and the subsequent spinning of these materials into yarn or thread (131).
*   **Weaving:** The mechanical weaving of broad fabrics from various raw materials, including cotton, wool, silk, synthetic filaments, and specialized industrial threads, as well as the production of woven pile, chenille, and imitation fur (132).
*   **Finishing Processes:** The chemical and mechanical treatment of textile fibres, yarns, fabrics, and textile articles to alter their physical properties or appearance, such as bleaching, dyeing, printing, shrinking, mercerising, and specialized coating or waterproofing (133).
*   **Specialized and Made-Up Textiles:** The manufacture of a vast array of textile products other than apparel, such as knitted and non-woven fabrics (1391), household furnishings like blankets and curtains (1392), textile floor coverings including carpets and synthetic turf (1393), cordage, rope, and industrial netting (1394), as well as technical textiles like conveyor belts, tarpaulins, sails, and narrow woven fabrics (1396, 1399).

This does not include:
*   The growing and harvesting of natural fibres (Division 01).
*   The chemical manufacture of synthetic or artificial fibres, tows, and single yarns (20.60).
*   The manufacture of wearing apparel and clothing accessories (Division 14).
*   The manufacture of non-textile floor coverings, such as cork or linoleum (16.28, 22.24).
*   The manufacture of transmission/conveyor belts made primarily of vulcanized rubber (22.12).
*   The manufacture of specific medical or sanitary textile articles, such as surgical drapes or napkins (21.20, 32.50).

detailled_description:
This category encompasses the industrial activities involved in the preparatory processing of textile fibres and the subsequent spinning of these materials into yarn or thread. It covers the transformation of a wide range of raw materials, including natural, man-made, and recycled textile fibres, into products suitable for weaving, sewing, or further industrial processing.

This includes, among others:
*   **Preparatory operations on textile fibres:** The treatment of raw materials to prepare them for spinning, such as the reeling and washing of silk; the scouring, degreasing, carbonising, and dyeing of wool fleece; and the carding and combing of animal, vegetable, and man-made fibres (1310).
*   **Spinning and manufacture of yarn:** The industrial production of yarn and thread, including the scutching of flax, as well as the texturising, twisting, folding, cabling, and dipping of synthetic or artificial filament yarns (1310).
*   **Processing of alternative materials:** The spinning of recycled fibres from secondary raw materials and the manufacture of paper yarn from cellulose-based fibres, such as wood or straw (1310).

This does not include:
*   Preparatory operations carried out in combination with agriculture (Division 01).
*   The retting of plants (jute, flax, coir, etc.) and cotton ginning, when not associated with the growing of the vegetable fibres (01.63).
*   The chemical manufacture of synthetic or artificial fibres, tows, and single yarns (20.60).
*   The manufacture of glass fibres (23.14).
*   The processing of textile waste into secondary raw materials (38.21).

It covers the production of broad woven fabrics through various mechanical weaving processes, regardless of the specific fiber composition or the origin of the textile material.

Furthermore, it includes the production of specialized woven textiles, such as woven pile or chenille fabrics, terry towelling, gauze, fabrics composed of aramid threads, and the manufacture of imitation fur through weaving processes (1320).

The production of carbon fibers and related articles for non-electrical purposes is also excluded (23.99).

This category encompasses the manufacture of a diverse range of textile products, excluding the production of wearing apparel. It covers the industrial transformation of textile materials into specialized goods, ranging from household furnishings and industrial fabrics to technical floor coverings and structural netting.

This includes, among others:
*   **Knitted and non-woven fabrics:** The manufacture and processing of various knitted and crocheted fabrics, including pile, terry, and net fabrics, as well as the production of imitation fur by knitting (1391). It also encompasses the production of non-woven fabrics, including those bonded with plastics or rubber (1395).
*   **Household textiles and furnishings:** The production of made-up household textile articles such as blankets, quilts, pillows, and sleeping bags, as well as furnishing items like curtains, valances, flags, and banners (1392). 
*   **Floor coverings:** The manufacture of textile floor coverings, including carpets, rugs, mats, tiles, needle-loom felt floor coverings, and artificial grass/synthetic turf (1393).
*   **Cordage and industrial netting:** The production of rope, twine, cables, and knotted netting, including specialized products like fishing nets, loading slings, and ships' fenders (1394).
*   **Technical and specialized textiles:** The manufacture of narrow woven fabrics, trimmings (braids, tassels), labels, and badges (1396). This cluster also includes treated or coated fabrics (such as those impregnated with plastics or rubber), technical articles like conveyor belts, transmission belts, hose piping, tarpaulins, sails, tents, and automotive trimmings, as well as fabrics made of glass fibers (1396).
*   **Other textile products:** The manufacture of felt, embroidery, lace, tulles, net fabrics for window furnishings, shoelaces, and pressure-sensitive cloth tape (1399).

This does not include the manufacture of knitted or crocheted apparel (14.10) or other garments made of non-wovens (14.29). It excludes various specialized non-textile or specific-use items, such as: napkins, liners, and sanitary articles (17.22); floor coverings made of cork or resilient materials like vinyl/linoleum (16.28, 22.24); wire rope or woven metal wire (25.93); medical textiles impregnated with pharmaceutical substances (21.20); individual protective masks or surgical drapes (32.50); and transmission/conveyor belts made primarily of vulcanized rubber (22.12).

This division encompasses the manufacture of all types of wearing apparel, whether ready-to-wear or made-to-measure, utilizing various materials such as leather, fur, textile fabrics, or knitted and crocheted materials. The scope includes all items of clothing and accessories for men, women, and children, covering outerwear, undergarments, and specialized professional or recreational apparel.

This division includes, among others, the following logical clusters:

*   **Knitted and Crocheted Apparel:** The production of garments and hosiery manufactured directly from knitted or crocheted fabrics, including pullovers, cardigans, T-shirts, underwear, nightwear, swimwear, hosiery (socks and tights), and infant wear (141).
*   **Woven and Other Non-Knitted Apparel:** The manufacture of garments from woven, coated, impregnated, or rubberized fabrics, including coats, suits, jackets, trousers, ceremonial clothing, and shirts (142).
*   **Underwear and Foundation Garments:** The production of intimate apparel such as nightwear, pajamas, dressing gowns, brassieres, and corsets, whether knitted or woven (141, 142).
*   **Leather and Fur Apparel:** The manufacturing of garments and clothing accessories derived from fur skins or leather and composition leather (142).
*   **Clothing Accessories and Specialized Items:** The production of headwear (hats and caps), gloves, ties, shawls, belts, and other textile accessories, as well as specialized professional or technical attire such as uniforms and sportswear (141, 142).

This division does not include the repair of wearing apparel (95.29), the manufacture of knitted fabrics (13.91), the production of raw hides, skins, or furs (01.48, 01.70, 10.11), the dressing and dyeing of fur (15.11), the manufacture of footwear with applied soles (15.20), the manufacture of apparel made of rubber or plastics (22.12, 22.26), the manufacture of fire-protective or safety headgear (32.99), or the manufacture of specialized sports gloves (32.30).

description: Manufacture of other wearing apparel and accessories
detailled_description:
This category encompasses the manufacture of diverse wearing apparel and clothing accessories, specifically excluding items produced through knitting or crocheting. The production process involves a wide range of materials, including woven fabrics, leather, and fur, which may be treated, coated, impregnated, or rubberised.

This category includes the following logical groupings:

*   **Outerwear and Specialized Apparel:** The production of garments such as coats, suits, jackets, trousers, shirts, blouses, and ceremonial clothing, including bridal dresses (1421). It also covers professional attire, such as uniforms and official clothing (e.g., judge’s gowns or church vestments) (1423).
*   **Underwear and Intimate Apparel:** The manufacture of woven underwear, nightwear (e.g., pyjamas, dressing gowns), swimwear, and foundation garments such as brassieres and corsets (1422).
*   **Leather and Fur Apparel:** The production of garments and working clothes made of leather or composition leather, as well as the manufacturing of fur apparel, clothing accessories, and assemblies of fur skins (1424).
*   **Sportswear and Accessories:** The manufacture of technical sportswear (e.g., tracksuits, ski suits), headwear (hats and caps), and various clothing accessories, including gloves, belts, shawls, ties, cravats, hairnets, and textile footwear without applied soles (1429).

This category does not include the repair of wearing apparel (95.29); the manufacture of knitted or crocheted garments (14.10); the production of raw hides, skins, or furs (01.48, 01.70, 10.11); the dressing and dyeing of fur (15.11); the manufacture of imitation furs (13.20, 13.91); the production of footwear with applied soles (15.20); the manufacture of wearing apparel made of rubber or plastics (22.12, 22.26); the manufacture of fire-protective clothing (32.99); the manufacture of safety headgear (32.99); or the manufacture of specialized sports gloves (32.30).

description: Manufacture of leather and related products of other materials
detailled_description:
This division encompasses the industrial processing of hides, skins, and furs, as well as the comprehensive manufacturing of leather products, footwear, and their direct material substitutes. It covers the entire production value chain, ranging from the initial tanning and dressing of raw materials to the fabrication of finished consumer goods and specialized technical articles.

This category includes, among others:

*   **Leather and Fur Processing:** The tanning, dyeing, dressing, scraping, shearing, plucking, and currying of hides, skins, and fur skins. This includes the production of chamois, parchment, patent, metallized, and composition leathers (1511).
*   **Luggage, Handbags, and Personal Accessories:** The manufacture of luggage, handbags, backpacks, and related articles made from leather, composition leather, or other materials, such as plastics or textiles, that utilize similar manufacturing technologies. This also covers the production of leather shoelaces and non-metallic watch bands (1512).
*   **Saddlery, Harnesses, and Technical Goods:** The production of saddlery, harnesses for animals, and specialized leather animal apparel, as well as industrial leather goods such as driving belts and packings (1512).
*   **Footwear Production:** The manufacture of footwear for all purposes and of any material, including footwear produced through moulding processes. This includes the production of essential footwear components, such as uppers, inner and outer soles, and heels made from leather, rubber, wood, or plastic, as well as gaiters and similar protective footwear accessories (1520).

This does not include the production of raw hides and skins (associated with slaughtering or ranching), the manufacture of leather wearing apparel, gloves, or hats, the manufacture of bicycle saddles, watch bands made of precious or base metals, or safety belts for occupational use. It also excludes the manufacture of knitted or crocheted footwear without applied soles (14.10), certain textile footwear without applied soles (14.29), sports-specific footwear like ski boots (32.30), or prescription orthopaedic shoes (32.50).

details.includes: This division includes dressing and dyeing of fur and the transformation of hides or skins into leather by tanning or curing and fabricating the leather into products for final consumption.
details.alsoIcludes: It also includes the manufacture of direct substitute products (like-products) made from materials other than leather (for example, rubber footwear, textile luggage). Products made from leather substitutes are included here because they are made in ways similar to those in which leather products are made (for example, luggage) and are often produced in the same unit.

description: Tanning, dyeing, dressing of leather and fur; manufacture of luggage, handbags, saddlery and harness
detailled_description:
This category encompasses the industrial processing of hides, skins, and furs, as well as the manufacturing of various leather and composition leather products. It covers the complete value chain from raw material preparation through to the production of consumer goods, travel accessories, and specialized animal equipment.

This category includes, among others:

*   **Leather and Fur Processing:** The tanning, dyeing, dressing, scraping, shearing, plucking, and currying of hides, skins, and fur skins. This encompasses the production of chamois, parchment, patent, metallised, and composition leathers (1511).
*   **Luggage and Personal Accessories:** The manufacture of luggage, handbags, backpacks, and related articles made from leather, composition leather, or other materials utilizing similar manufacturing technologies. It also includes the production of leather shoelaces and non-metallic watch bands (1512).
*   **Saddlery and Technical Leather Goods:** The manufacture of saddlery, harnesses for animals, and leather clothing for animals. Furthermore, it covers the production of various technical leather articles such as driving belts, packings, horse whips, and riding crops (1512).

This does not include the production of raw hides and skins (associated with ranching or slaughtering activities), the manufacture of leather wearing apparel, gloves, hats, or footwear, the manufacture of bicycle saddles, watch bands made of precious or non-precious metals, safety belts for occupational use, or the manufacture of imitation leather products not based on natural leather.

description: Manufacture of wood and of products of wood and cork, except furniture; manufacture of articles of straw and plaiting materials
detailled_description:
This division encompasses the industrial activities involved in the processing of wood and the manufacture of products derived from wood, cork, straw, and plaiting materials. It covers the entire value chain from initial sawing and mechanical shaping of raw timber to the production of complex, finished wooden components, construction materials, and specialized packaging or utility items.

This division includes, among others:

*   **Primary Wood Processing:** Industrial activities involving the sawing, planing, and machining of logs to create basic wood shapes, including the production of wooden railway sleepers, wood wool, and sawdust (161).
*   **Secondary Processing and Finishing:** Technical operations performed on wood, such as drying, chemical impregnation, preservation, boring, turning, milling, and surface finishing or coating of wood in the rough (161, 162).
*   **Veneer and Wood-Based Panels:** The manufacture of veneer sheets, plywood, laminated wood boards, particle boards (including OSB), fibreboards, and densified wood (162).
*   **Builders’ Carpentry and Joinery:** The production of construction-related wooden elements, including beams, roof trusses, assembled parquet flooring, stairs, railings, moldings, shingles, wooden doors, window frames, and prefabricated wooden buildings or mobile homes (162).
*   **Packaging and Utility Goods:** The manufacture of wooden containers such as packing cases, boxes, crates, pallets, cable drums, barrels, vats, and tubs, as well as turned wood products, kitchenware, and ornaments (162).
*   **Cork, Straw, and Biomass Products:** The manufacture of natural or agglomerated cork products, items made from plaiting materials (such as baskets and mats), and solid fuels produced from vegetable biomass, such as wood pellets, briquettes, and fire logs (162).

This division does not include logging and the production of wood in the rough (02.20); the manufacture of luggage (15.12); the manufacture of wooden footwear (15.20); the manufacture of matches (20.59); the manufacture of textile machinery parts (28.94); the manufacture of furniture (31.00); the manufacture of wooden toys (32.40); the manufacture of brushes, brooms, or coffins (32.91, 32.99); the installation of wooden fittings, doors, windows, or stairs (43.32); the installation of roof frames (43.41); disinfection and extermination services (81.23); or the repair and refinishing of furniture (95.24).

details.includes:
This division includes the manufacture of wood products (for example, lumber, plywood, veneers, wood containers, wood flooring, wood trusses, prefabricated wood buildings, the manufacture of solid fuels from vegetable biomass, the finishing of wooden products). The production processes include sawing, planing, shaping, laminating and assembling of wood products starting from logs that are cut into bolts, or lumber that may then be cut further, or shaped by lathes or other shaping tools. The lumber or other transformed wood shapes may also be subsequently planed or smoothed, and assembled into finished products (for example, wooden containers).

With the exception of sawmilling, this division is subdivided mainly based on the specific products manufactured.

description: Sawmilling and planing of wood; processing and finishing of wood
detailled_description:
This category encompasses the industrial activities involved in the primary processing of wood, including the mechanical shaping of logs and the subsequent treatment and finishing of wood products. It covers operations ranging from the initial sawing and machining of raw timber to specialized chemical treatments and surface finishing processes.

This category includes, among others:

*   **Primary Wood Processing (1611):** The sawing, planing, and machining of wood, including the slicing, peeling, or chipping of logs. This also includes the production of wooden railway sleepers, unassembled wooden flooring, and the manufacture (outside the forest) of wood wool, sawdust, flour, chips, and particles.
*   **Secondary Processing and Finishing (1612):** General technical processing activities, often performed on a fee or contract basis, such as boring, turning, milling, broaching, levelling, grinding, polishing, and splicing of wood. This also encompasses the drying of wood, its impregnation or chemical treatment, and the application of paints, stains, or other preservatives to wood in the rough.

This does not include logging and the production of wood in the rough (02.20), the manufacture of veneer sheets for plywood (16.21), the manufacture of assembled parquet panels (16.22), the manufacture of wooden shingles and shakes (16.23), or the manufacture of fire logs and pressed wood (16.26). Furthermore, it excludes the secondary coating or chemical treatment of finished wooden products (16.27), disinfection and extermination services (81.23), and the refinishing or repairing of furniture (95.24).
