description: Manufacture of products of wood, cork, straw and plaiting materials
detailled_description:
This category encompasses the manufacture of a wide range of products derived from wood, cork, straw, and plaiting materials, spanning from basic processed shapes to finished, assembled goods. It covers both industrial components used in construction and specialized consumer or utility items.

This group includes, among others:

*   **Veneer and Wood-Based Panels:** The manufacture of veneer sheets, plywood, laminated wood boards (such as glue-laminated and cross-laminated timber), particle boards (including OSB), fibreboards (including MDF and insulating boards), and densified wood (1621).
*   **Builders' Carpentry and Joinery:** The production of construction-related wooden elements such as beams, roof trusses, stairs, railings, moldings, shingles, and prefabricated wooden buildings or mobile homes (1623), as well as the manufacturing of wooden doors, windows, and their frames (1625).
*   **Containers and Packaging:** The production of wooden packing cases, boxes, crates, drums, pallets, cable drums, barrels, vats, and tubs (1624).
*   **Fuel and Surface Finishing:** The manufacturing of solid fuels from vegetable biomass, such as wood pellets, briquettes, and fire logs (1626), and the specialized processes involved in the surface finishing, coating, and protection of wooden products (1627).
*   **Flooring and Miscellaneous Wood/Cork/Straw Articles:** The manufacture of assembled parquet flooring (1622) and a broad array of articles including turned wood products (handles, spools, kitchenware), ornaments, marquetry, mirror and picture frames, natural and agglomerated cork products (including bottle corks and floor coverings), and items made from plaiting materials, such as baskets and mats (1628).

This does not include: the manufacture of unassembled wooden flooring (16.11); the manufacture of luggage (15.12); the manufacture of wooden footwear (15.20); the manufacture of furniture, including free-standing partitions, walk-in wardrobes, and clock cases (31.00); the installation of doors, windows, stairs, or kitchen fittings (43.32); the erection of roof frames (43.41); the manufacture of wooden toys (32.40); the manufacture of brushes and brooms (32.91); the manufacture of matches (20.59); the manufacture of coffins (32.99); or the manufacture of textile machinery parts (28.94).

description: Manufacture of paper and paper products
detailled_description:
This division encompasses the entire industrial value chain of the paper industry, ranging from the production of raw pulp to the manufacturing of finished converted paper and paperboard products. It includes the chemical and mechanical transformation of cellulose fibers—whether from wood, recycled waste paper, or other materials—into bulk paper products, as well as the subsequent processing and conversion of these materials into functional items for industrial, commercial, and household use.

This division includes, among others:

*   **Pulp, Paper, and Paperboard Production:** The manufacturing of bleached, semi-bleached, or unbleached pulp via chemical, mechanical, or semi-chemical processes, including the processing of recovered waste paper through de-inking (171). It also includes the production of bulk newsprint, printing and writing paper, cellulose wadding, and the finishing of paper and paperboard through coating, covering, impregnation, or laminating (171).
*   **Packaging and Containers:** The production of corrugated paper and paperboard, as well as cartons, boxes, cases, sacks, bags, and molded or pressed paper pulp articles such as egg trays (172).
*   **Sanitary and Household Articles:** The manufacturing of personal hygiene and household products made from paper or cellulose wadding, including toilet paper, tissues, towels, serviettes, diapers, sanitary products, and disposable cups or plates (172).
*   **Stationery and Office Supplies:** The production of finished stationery, including envelopes, letter cards, notebooks, binders, business forms, and adhesive papers (172).
*   **Wall Coverings and Specialized Paper Goods:** The manufacturing of wallpaper and similar wall coverings, alongside specialized items such as filter paper, cigarette paper, paper labels, and industrial bobbins (172).

This does not include printing and related service activities (18.1), publishing activities (58.1), the manufacture of plastic wallpaper (22.29), the manufacture of abrasive paper (23.91), the manufacture of games, toys, and playing cards (32.40), or the manufacture of coated/impregnated paper where the coating material is the primary ingredient (classified according to the nature of that ingredient).

details.includes:
This division includes the manufacture of pulp, paper, converted paper and the manufacture of products of recycled goods from wood, paper, cardboard and paperboard.

The manufacture of these products is grouped together because they constitute a series of vertically connected processes. More than one activity is often carried out in a single unit.

The manufacture of pulp involves separating the cellulose fibres from other matter in wood, or dissolving and de-inking of used paper, and mixing in small amounts of reagents to reinforce the binding of the fibres.

Converted paper products are made from paper and other materials by various techniques.

The paper articles may be printed (for example, wallpaper, gift wrap), as long as the printing of information is not the main purpose.

The production of pulp, paper and paperboard in bulk is included in group 17.1, while the remaining classes include the production of further-processed paper and paper products.

description: Manufacture of pulp, paper and paperboard
detailled_description:
This category encompasses the industrial production of basic pulp, paper, and paperboard products, ranging from raw material processing to the manufacturing and finishing of paper-based materials. It covers both the chemical and mechanical transformation of fibers into pulp and the subsequent conversion of these materials into various types of paper and paperboard for industrial or commercial use.

This category includes, among others:

*   **Pulp Production:** The manufacturing of bleached, semi-bleached, or unbleached paper pulp utilizing mechanical, chemical (dissolving or non-dissolving), or semi-chemical processes, as well as the production of cotton linter pulp and the manufacturing of pulp derived from recovered waste paper through de-inking (1711).
*   **Paper and Paperboard Manufacturing:** The production of newsprint, printing and writing paper, handmade paper, cellulose wadding, and webs of cellulose fibers. It also encompasses the further processing of paper and paperboard, such as colouring, coating, covering, impregnation, the creation of crêpe or crinkled paper, and the production of laminates and foils when laminated with paper or paperboard, as well as the manufacturing of carbon or stencil paper in rolls or large sheets (1712).

This does not include the manufacture of corrugated paper and paperboard (17.21); the manufacture of further-processed articles of paper, paperboard, or pulp (17.22 to 17.25); printing and related service activities (18.1); the manufacture of abrasive paper (23.91); publishing activities (58.1); or the manufacture of coated/impregnated paper where the coating or impregnation material constitutes the primary ingredient (classified according to the manufacturing activity of that specific ingredient).

description: Manufacture of articles of paper and paperboard
detailled_description:
This category encompasses the manufacture of a wide range of converted paper and paperboard products, excluding the production of raw paper pulp or bulk paper and paperboard. It covers the transformation of these materials into functional items for industrial, commercial, household, and decorative use.

This includes, among others:

*   **Packaging and Containers:** The production of corrugated paper and paperboard, along with cartons, boxes, cases, sacks, bags, and various containers of paper or paperboard (1721). This also includes the manufacture of molded or pressed articles of paper pulp, such as egg trays (1725).
*   **Household and Sanitary Goods:** The production of personal hygiene and household products made from paper or cellulose wadding, including cleansing tissues, handkerchiefs, towels, serviettes, toilet paper, sanitary products (towels, tampons, diapers), and disposable cups, dishes, and trays (1722).
*   **Stationery and Office Supplies:** The manufacturing of ready-to-use printing and writing paper, envelopes, letter cards, adhesive papers, and various educational or commercial stationery such as notebooks, binders, and business forms (1723).
*   **Wall Coverings and Specialized Paper Articles:** The production of wallpaper and similar wall coverings, including textile or vinyl-coated types (1724). Furthermore, it includes specialized items such as filter paper, cigarette paper, paper labels, industrial bobbins and spools, and paper novelties (1725).

This category does not include the manufacture of paper or paperboard in bulk (see 17.12), the printing of paper products (see 18.1), or the production of plastic wallpaper (see 22.26). It also excludes the manufacture of playing cards, games, and toys (see 32.40) and publishing activities (see 58.1).

description: Printing and reproduction of recorded media
detailled_description:
This division encompasses the industrial processes of printing on various substrates and the reproduction of recorded media. It covers the complete production cycle, including pre-press preparation, the physical printing or replication of content, and post-press finishing operations, regardless of whether the input materials are owned by the printing unit or provided by customers.

This division includes the following logical clusters:

*   **Printing and Support Services:** This includes the printing of newspapers, books, periodicals, and commercial documents such as business forms and greeting cards (181). It also covers printing on diverse materials like textiles, plastics, metal, glass, and wood using techniques such as lithographic, gravure, flexographic, screen, and digital printing (181). Furthermore, it includes essential support activities such as pre-press services (typesetting, plate-making, data imaging) and post-press finishing operations (bookbinding, trimming, lamination, and embossing) (181).
*   **Reproduction of Recorded Media:** This includes the mass reproduction of audio, video, and data from master copies, specifically covering the manufacturing of compact discs (CDs), video recordings, software on discs or tapes, and gramophone records (182).

This division does not include:
*   Publishing activities (Section J).
*   The production of master copies for records or audio material (Class 59.20).
*   The manufacture of products via 3D printing, which are classified according to the product and material used.
*   The reproduction of motion picture film for theatrical distribution (Class 59.12).
*   Software publishing (Class 58.2).

details.includes:
This division includes printing of products (for example, newspapers, books, periodicals, business forms and greeting cards), printing on T-shirts and other types of material, and associated support activities (for example, bookbinding, plate-making services, data imaging). The support activities included here are an integral part of the printing industry, and a product (a printing plate, a bound book, or a computer disk or file) that is an integral part of the printing industry is almost always provided by these operations.

The ownership of the input material is irrelevant to the classification of printing and reproduction of recorded media activities. Division 18 covers explicitly the processing activities.

Processes used in printing include a variety of methods for transferring an image from a plate, screen or computer file to a medium (for example, paper, plastics, metal, textile articles, wood). The most prominent of these methods entails the transfer of the image from a plate or screen to the medium through lithographic, gravure, screen or flexographic printing. Often a computer file is used to directly drive the printing mechanism to create the image or electrostatic and other types of equipment (digital or non-impact printing).

Though printing and publishing can be carried out by the same unit (for example, a newspaper), it is less and less the case that these distinct activities are carried out in the same physical location.

description: Printing and service activities related to printing
detailled_description:
This category encompasses the specialized industrial processes involved in printing on various materials and the comprehensive range of support services essential to the production of printed matter. The scope includes the physical printing of publications and commercial materials, the preparatory technical services required prior to printing, and the subsequent finishing and binding operations.

This encompasses the following logical clusters:

*   **Printing Services:** This includes the high-frequency printing of newspapers and periodicals (1811), as well as a broad spectrum of commercial printing including magazines, books, brochures, advertising materials, security documents, and smart cards (1812). It also covers printing on diverse substrates such as textiles, plastics, glass, metal, and wood using techniques like offset, flexographic, screen, and digital printing, along with large-format and photographic printing (1812).
*   **Pre-press and Pre-media Services:** This includes technical preparation for printing, such as typesetting, scanning, data input, and the electronic makeup of files (1813). It also encompasses the manufacturing of printing surfaces, such as plate-making (including CTP processes), cylinder engraving for gravure, and the creation of design proofs, layouts, and dummies (1813).
*   **Post-press and Binding Services:** This includes trade binding and finishing operations such as folding, trimming, stitching, adhesive binding, and lamination (1814). It further includes specialized post-production services like mailing preparation, embossing, gold stamping, and finishing services for electronic media (1814).

This category does not include the publishing of printed matter (58.1), advertising design activities (73.11), or the operation of self-service photocopying machines (82.10). Furthermore, it excludes the printing of textile fabrics when performed as an intermediate step in textile manufacturing (13.30), the manufacture of stationery where printing is not the primary characteristic (17.23), graphic design for non-print media (74.1), and general engraving on metal, glass, or wood when unrelated to printing processes (various classes according to material).

description: Manufacture of coke and refined petroleum products
detailled_description:
This division encompasses the industrial transformation of crude petroleum, coal, and lignite into usable energy products and chemical feedstocks. The core activities involve the operation of coke ovens and the primary refining of petroleum through processes such as distillation, cracking, and fractionation to isolate and produce various fuel and derivative products.

This includes, among others, the following clusters of activities:

*   **Coke Oven Operations:** The production of coke, semi-coke, and pitch coke through the carbonization of coal and lignite, the manufacture of coke oven gas, and the processing of crude coal and lignite tars, including the agglomeration of coke (191).
*   **Petroleum Refining and Fuel Production:** The manufacture of liquid and gaseous fuels, including motor fuels (gasoline, kerosene), light and heavy fuel oils, and refinery gases such as ethane, propane, and butane. This cluster also covers the production of solid fossil fuel products, such as peat, hard coal, and lignite briquettes, as well as the blending of biofuels with petroleum (192).
*   **Petroleum Derivatives and Specialised Products:** The production of lubricating oils and greases (including from waste oil), white spirit, Vaseline, paraffin wax, petroleum jelly, and bituminous products for road covering, as well as the processing of petroleum waste into refined materials (192).

This division does not include the extraction of natural gas (06.20), the manufacture of industrial gases (20.11), or the production of gases in other units (20.14). It also excludes the manufacture of gases through a permanent supply network (35.21), the production of petrochemicals and liquid biofuels (division 20), and the manufacture of solid fuels from biomass (16.29).

details.includes:
This division includes the transformation of crude petroleum and coal into usable products. The dominant process is petroleum refining, which involves the separation of crude petroleum into component products through such techniques as cracking and distillation. 

This division includes the manufacture of gases (for example, ethane, propane, butane) as products of petroleum refineries.
details.alsoIcludes: This division also includes the manufacture for own account of characteristic products (for example, coke, butane, propane, petrol, kerosene, fuel oil) as well as processing services (for example, custom refining).
details.excludes:
This division excludes the manufacture of such gases in other units (see 20.14), the manufacture of industrial gases (see 20.11), the extraction of natural gas (methane, ethane, butane or propane, see 06.20), and the manufacture of gases other than petroleum gases for the provision of gaseous fuels through a permanent supply network (for example, coal gas, water gas, producer gas, gasworks gas, see 35.21).

The manufacture of petrochemicals from refined petroleum and the manufacture of liquid biofuels are classified in division 20.

This category encompasses the industrial activities related to the processing of coal and lignite through carbonization to produce coke and its associated by-products. It focuses specifically on the operation of coke ovens and the primary distillation and refinement processes derived from coal transformation.

This includes, among others, the operation of coke ovens (1910) and the production of coke, semi-coke, and pitch coke (1910). The category also covers the manufacture of coke oven gas, the production of pitch, and the processing of crude coal and lignite tars, as well as the agglomeration of coke (1910).

This does not include the manufacture of coal fuel briquettes, which is classified under category 19.20.

description: Manufacture of refined petroleum products and fossil fuel products
detailled_description:
This category encompasses the manufacture of liquid and gaseous fuels, as well as various specialized products derived from crude petroleum, bituminous minerals, and solid fossil fuel sources. It covers the industrial transformation of these raw materials through processes such as fractionation, straight distillation, and cracking.

This includes, among others:

*   **Fuels and Energy Products:** The production of motor fuels (gasoline, kerosene), light, medium, and heavy fuel oils, and refinery gases (such as ethane, propane, and butane). This also includes the blending of biofuels with petroleum (e.g., gasohol) and the manufacture of solid fossil fuel products like peat, hard coal, and lignite briquettes (1920).
*   **Petroleum-based Derivatives and Chemicals:** The manufacture of lubricating oils and greases, including those produced from waste oil. It further includes the production of white spirit, Vaseline, paraffin wax, petroleum jelly, and various products intended for the petrochemical industry or for road covering applications (1920).
*   **Petroleum Waste Utilization:** The manufacture of petroleum briquettes and various refined products processed from petroleum waste materials (1920).

This does not include the manufacture of solid fuels from biomass (16.29) or the manufacture of liquid biofuels (20.51).

description: Manufacture of chemicals and chemical products
detailled_description:
This division encompasses the transformation of organic and inorganic raw materials through chemical processes to produce a wide range of industrial, agricultural, and consumer chemical products. It covers the entire spectrum of the industry, from the production of basic chemicals and polymers that serve as primary raw materials to the manufacturing of specialized intermediate and end-use chemical preparations.

This includes, among others:

*   **Basic Chemicals and Materials:** The manufacture of industrial gases (2011), dyes, pigments, and inorganic basic chemicals (2012, 2013), organic basic chemicals (2014), fertilizers and nitrogen compounds (2015), as well as plastics and synthetic rubber in primary forms (2016, 2017).
*   **Agrochemicals:** The production of pesticides, disinfectants, and various preparations for crop management and sanitation (2020).
*   **Paints and Coatings:** The manufacture of paints, varnishes, enamels, lacquers, printing inks, and mastics or surfacing preparations (2030).
*   **Cleaning and Personal Care Products:** The production of soaps, detergents, surface-active agents, perfumes, cosmetics, and specialized cleaning and polishing preparations (2041, 2042).
*   **Other Specialized Chemical Products:** The manufacture of liquid biofuels (2051), explosives and pyrotechnics, essential oils, adhesives, glues, photographic chemicals, laboratory reagents, and various industrial chemical preparations (2059).
*   **Man-made Fibres:** The production of synthetic or artificial filament tows, staple fibres, yarns, and monofilaments (2060).

This does not include the extraction of natural gas or petroleum (06.20, 09.10), the manufacture of fuel gases (19.20, 35.21), the manufacture of pharmaceutical products (21.10), the manufacturing of basic metals (division 24), the processing and recycling of waste (38.21), the spinning of synthetic or artificial fibres (13.10), or the manufacture of carbon fibres (23.99).

details.includes: This division includes the transformation of organic and inorganic raw materials by a chemical process and the formation of products. It distinguishes the production of basic chemicals that constitute the first industry group from the production of intermediate and end-products produced by further processing of basic chemicals that make up the remaining industry classes.

description: Manufacture of basic chemicals, fertilisers and nitrogen compounds, plastics and synthetic rubber in primary forms
detailled_description:
This category encompasses the manufacture of basic chemical products, fertilizers, and nitrogen compounds, as well as the production of plastics and synthetic rubber in their primary forms. It covers a broad range of industrial processes—such as thermal cracking, distillation, and chemical synthesis—that yield separate chemical elements or defined compounds for subsequent use in further manufacturing.

This includes, among others:
*   **Industrial Gases:** Manufacture of compressed or liquefied inorganic and medical gases, including elemental, inert, and mixed gases (2011).
*   **Dyes, Pigments, and Inorganic Chemicals:** Manufacture of dyes, pigments, and fluorescent brightening agents (2012), as well as other inorganic basic chemicals including chemical elements, inorganic acids, alkalis, lyes, distilled water, and the enrichment of nuclear ores (2013).
*   **Organic Basic Chemicals:** Production of hydrocarbons, alcohols, carboxylic acids, nitrogen-function organic compounds, synthetic aromatic products, and refrigerant gases (2014).
*   **Fertilizers and Nitrogen Compounds:** Manufacture of straight or complex nitrogenous, phosphatic, or potassic fertilizers, urea, ammonia, nitric acids, and various nitrogen-based chemical compounds (2015).
*   **Polymers and Synthetic Materials:** Manufacture of plastics in primary forms, including polymers, resins, silicones, and cellulose derivatives (2016), as well as synthetic rubber and rubber-like gums in primary forms (2017).

This does not include the extraction of natural gas or petroleum (06.20, 09.10), the manufacture of fuel gases (19.20, 35.21), the production of agrochemicals such as pesticides (20.20), the manufacture of prepared dyes (20.30), the manufacture of pharmaceutical products (21.10), the manufacture of artificial/synthetic fibers (20.60), the manufacturing of basic metals (division 24), or the processing and recycling of waste (38.21).

description: Manufacture of pesticides, disinfectants and other agrochemical products
detailled_description:
This category encompasses the industrial production of chemical preparations designed for pest control, crop management, and sanitation. It focuses on the manufacturing of specialized agrochemical agents and chemical substances used to control biological organisms in both agricultural and non-agricultural environments.

This includes, among others:
*   **Pesticides and Biocides:** The production of insecticides, rodenticides, fungicides, herbicides, acaricides, and molluscicides, as well as general biocides (2020).
*   **Plant Growth and Development Products:** The manufacturing of plant growth regulators and anti-sprouting agents (2020).
*   **Disinfectants:** The production of chemical disinfectants intended for agricultural, industrial, or general use (2020).
*   **Other Agrochemicals:** Any other agrochemical products not elsewhere classified (2020).

This does not include the manufacture of fertilisers and nitrogen compounds, which is classified under category 2015.

description: Manufacture of paints, varnishes and similar coatings, printing ink and mastics
detailled_description:
This category comprises the manufacturing activities related to surface coatings, specialized colorants, and bonding preparations used across various industrial and artistic applications. It covers the production of substances designed to protect, color, or finish surfaces, as well as essential additives and solvents required for their application and removal.

This includes, among others:
*   **Paints, Varnishes, and Coatings:** The manufacture of paints, varnishes, enamels, and lacquers (2030).
*   **Colorants and Glazes:** The production of prepared pigments, dyes, opacifiers, and colors, as well as vitrifiable enamels, glazes, and engobes (2030).
*   **Mastics and Surfacing Preparations:** The manufacture of mastics, caulking compounds, and related non-refractory filling or surfacing preparations (2030).
*   **Ancillary Products:** The manufacture of organic composite solvents and thinners, prepared paint or varnish removers, and printing inks (2030).

This does not include the manufacture of basic dyes, tuffs, and pigments (classified under 20.12), or the manufacture of specialized writing and drawing inks (classified under 20.59).

description: Manufacture of washing, cleaning and polishing preparations
detailled_description:
This category encompasses the manufacture of a broad range of chemical preparations used for personal hygiene, grooming, and household or industrial cleaning and maintenance. It covers the production of soaps, surface-active agents, and specialized cosmetic and toiletry products, as well as various polishing and deodorizing formulations.

This category includes, among others:

*   **Soaps, Detergents, and Surface-Active Agents:** The production of organic surface-active agents, washing powders, liquid detergents, dish-washing preparations, textile softeners, and soap products, including those used in technical and household applications (2041).
*   **Cosmetics and Toilet Preparations:** The manufacture of perfumes, toilet waters, beauty and make-up preparations, suntan and sunburn prevention products, and manicure and pedicure preparations. This also includes hair care products (shampoos, lacquers, waving and straightening agents), oral hygiene products (dentifrices and denture fixatives), shaving preparations, deodorants, bath salts, depilatories, and cosmetic soaps (2042).
*   **Cleaning and Polishing Products:** The production of scouring pastes and powders, artificial and prepared waxes, and polishes and creams for leather, wood, coachwork, glass, and metal. It also includes preparations for perfuming or deodorizing rooms and cleaning materials coated or covered with soap, detergents, or scouring agents (2041).
*   **Chemical Intermediates:** The manufacture of crude glycerol (2041).

This does not include the extraction and refining of natural essential oils (2059), the manufacture of separate chemically defined compounds (2013, 2014), or the synthesis of glycerol from petroleum products (2014).

This category encompasses the manufacture of a diverse range of specialized chemical products not classified elsewhere, including liquid biofuels and a broad spectrum of industrial and technical chemical preparations. It covers everything from high-energy pyrotechnic and explosive materials to essential oils, specialized adhesives, and advanced chemical reagents used in laboratory or industrial processes.

This includes, among others:

*   **Liquid Biofuels:** The production of biodiesel, ethanol from biomass, and mixtures of bioethanol and ethers derived from biomass, regardless of whether the inputs include waste materials (20.51).
*   **Explosives and Pyrotechnic Products:** The manufacture of propellant powders, explosives, pyrotechnic products such as percussion caps, detonators, and signalling flares (20.59).
*   **Adhesives, Inks, and Coating Chemicals:** The production of glues and prepared adhesives (including rubber-based), writing and drawing inks, and materials used in the finishing of textiles and leather (20.59).
*   **Photographic and Laboratory Chemicals:** The manufacture of sensitised photographic materials (plates, films, and paper), chemical preparations for photographic uses, composite diagnostic or laboratory reagents, and gelatine and its derivatives (20.59).
*   **Essential Oils and Aromatic Products:** The production of essential oils, extracts of natural aromatic products, resinoids, and mixtures of odoriferous products used for perfumes or food (20.59).
*   **Specialized Industrial Chemicals:** A wide array of technical preparations including activated carbon, fuel and lubricating oil additives, catalysts, anti-knock and antifreeze preparations, hydraulic transmission fluids, soldering/welding pastes, metal pickling substances, and additives for cements (20.59).
*   **Consumer-related Chemical Products:** The production of matches and e-liquids for vaping devices (20.59).

This does not include the manufacture of solid fuels from vegetable biomass (16.26), ethyl alcohol not intended for use as biofuel (20.14), synthetic aromatic products (20.14), printing ink (20.30), or perfume and toilet preparations (20.42).

This category encompasses the industrial production of man-made synthetic and artificial fibres, covering all stages from the initial filament creation to the production of staple fibres. It focuses on the chemical and mechanical processing required to produce base materials before they are converted into textile yarns or fabrics.

This includes, among others, the manufacture of synthetic or artificial filament tow, as well as synthetic or artificial staple fibres that have not yet been carded, combed, or otherwise processed for spinning (2060). Furthermore, this category covers the production of synthetic or artificial filament yarns, including high-tenacity yarns, as well as the manufacture of synthetic or artificial monofilaments, strips, and various recycled fibres (2060).

This does not include the spinning of synthetic or artificial fibres or the manufacture of yarns made of man-made staple fibres, which are classified under class 13.10. Additionally, the manufacture of carbon fibres is excluded from this category and is classified under class 23.99.

description: Manufacture of basic pharmaceutical products and pharmaceutical preparations
detailled_description:
This division encompasses the industrial manufacturing of fundamental pharmaceutical active ingredients and the processing of these substances into finished pharmaceutical preparations for human and veterinary use. The scope spans the entire production value chain, from the chemical and biological synthesis of basic components to the formulation of complex medicinal products and therapeutic materials.

This division includes, among others, the manufacture of active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) such as antibiotics, basic vitamins, and salicylic and O-acetylsalicylic acids (211); the processing of blood, glands, and the production of chemically pure sugars (211); and the manufacturing of diverse finished medicaments including vaccines, antisera, blood fractions, hormonal preparations, and homeopathic remedies (212). It also covers the production of specialized medical diagnostic preparations, such as pregnancy tests and radioactive in-vivo diagnostic substances, as well as advanced therapy medical products, including cell and gene therapies and viral vector-based medicines (212). Furthermore, it includes the manufacturing of botanical products prepared for pharmaceutical use (e.g., via grinding or milling) and medical impregnated materials like bandages, gauze, and dressings (212).

This division does not include the manufacture of herb infusions (10.83), dental materials such as fillings and cements (32.50), or probiotics (21.10). Additionally, it excludes wholesale and retail pharmaceutical trade (46.46, 47.73), research and development activities in biotechnology or pharmaceuticals (72.10), and the independent packaging of pharmaceutical products (82.92).

details.includes: This division includes the manufacture of basic pharmaceutical products and pharmaceutical preparations.
details.alsoIcludes: This division also includes the manufacture of medicinal chemical and botanical products.

It focuses on the chemical and biological processing of raw materials into high-purity components required for therapeutic applications.

This category includes, among others, the manufacture of active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) utilized for their pharmacological properties, such as antibiotics, basic vitamins, and salicylic and O-acetylsalicylic acids (2110). Furthermore, it covers the processing of blood, the extraction and processing of glands, and the manufacture of chemically pure sugars and probiotics (2110).

This category does not include the manufacture of advanced cell and gene therapy pharmaceutical preparations (2110).

description: Manufacture of rubber and plastic products
detailled_description:
This division encompasses the industrial production of products made from natural or synthetic rubber and the transformation of new or recycled plastic resins into a wide range of intermediate and finished goods. The classification is primarily defined by the raw materials utilized, though it is not exhaustive of all products made from these materials, and it further includes items composed of composite materials where plastic is the predominant component.

This includes, among others:

*   **Rubber Products:** The manufacture of tires and related equipment, including inner tubes, treads, and retreading services (2211). It also covers industrial and technical components such as conveyor belts, seals, hoses, and profiles, alongside consumer goods like rubberized apparel, hygienic articles, and hard rubber items (2212).
*   **Plastic Products:** The production of semi-manufactured industrial profiles including sheets, films, tubes, and pipes (2221), as well as plastic packaging materials such as bottles, containers, and bags (2222). It also includes builders’ ware like doors, windows, shutters, and sanitaryware (2223, 2224), as well as miscellaneous consumer goods such as tableware, stationery, and insulating fittings (2226). 
*   **Processing and Finishing:** Specialized plastic processing activities performed on a contract basis, such as CNC milling, welding, gluing, and surface metallisation (2225).

This does not include the production of plastics in primary forms (20.16); the manufacture of luggage and handbags (15.12); footwear (15.20); plastic furniture or mattresses (31.00); sporting goods, games, and toys (32.30, 32.40); medical, dental, or ophthalmic appliances (32.50); personal safety equipment (32.99); or plastic components intended solely for use in motor vehicles (29.3). Furthermore, it excludes the manufacture of tyre cord fabrics (13.96), apparel made of elastic fabrics (14.22, 14.29), glues and adhesives (20.59), inflatable rafts and boats (30.11-30.13), the plastic coating of metal surfaces (25.51), the industrial reclaiming of rubber (38.21), and the maintenance or repair of tires (95.3).

detailled_description:
This division encompasses the industrial production of various products made from natural or synthetic rubber, including the specialized manufacture and maintenance of automotive and industrial tires. It covers the full lifecycle of rubber manufacturing, ranging from the production of raw or processed rubber components to finished consumer and industrial goods.

This includes, among others:

*   **Tires and Related Products:** The manufacture of pneumatic, solid, and cushion tires for vehicles, aircraft, machinery, and equipment; the production of inner tubes, interchangeable tyre treads, tyre flaps, and camelback strips; and the professional rebuilding and retreading of used tyres (2211).
*   **Rubber Industrial and Technical Components:** The production of plates, sheets, strips, rods, profile shapes, tubes, pipes, and hoses; conveyor and transmission belts; rubberized yarns and fabrics; rubber rings, fittings, and seals; and rubber expansion joints for the construction industry (2212).
*   **Consumer and Specialized Rubber Goods:** The manufacture of rubber hygienic articles (such as sheath contraceptives, teats, and hot-water bottles); rubberized apparel and accessories (including wetsuits, diving suits, bathing caps, and latex clothing); inflatable items (such as mattresses and balloons); as well as hard rubber goods like combs and pipe stems; rubber brushes; and rubber floor coverings (2212).

This does not include the manufacture of tyre cord fabrics (13.96); apparel made of elastic fabrics (14.22, 14.29); rubber soles or other rubber parts for footwear (15.20); glues and adhesives based on rubber (20.59); tyre and tube repair, fitting, or replacement services (95.3); inflatable rafts and boats (30.11, 30.12, 30.13); mattresses made of uncovered cellular rubber (31.00); rubber sports requisites (32.30); rubber games and toys (32.40); or the industrial reclaiming of rubber (38.21).

This category encompasses the transformation of new or recycled plastic resins into a wide range of intermediate and finished goods through industrial processes such as compression, extrusion, injection, and blow moulding. It covers the production of structural components, packaging, building materials, and various consumer articles, as well as specialized processing and finishing services for plastic materials.

This division includes the manufacture of:
*   **Semi-manufactures and Industrial Profiles:** Production of plastic plates, sheets, blocks, film, foil, strips, tubes, pipes, and associated fittings (2221).
*   **Packaging Goods:** Plastic articles designed for the containment and transport of goods, including bags, sacks, containers, bottles, and cases (2222).
*   **Builders’ Ware and Construction Components:** Doors, windows, and their frames; shutters and blinds (2223); as well as sanitaryware (baths, basins, cisterns), tanks, reservoirs, and wall, floor, or ceiling coverings (2224).
*   **Processing and Finishing Services:** General plastic working activities carried out on a contract basis, including cutting, CNC milling, welding, gluing, surface polishing, coating, and the metallisation of plastic surfaces (2225).
*   **Consumer and Specialized Goods:** Plastic tableware, kitchenware, toilet articles, office and school supplies, insulating fittings, and miscellaneous plastic novelties, including products made from polymer clay (2226).

This group does not include the production of plastics in primary forms (20.16); the manufacture of rubber products (22.1); the manufacture of luggage and handbags (15.12); plastic footwear (15.20); plastic furniture or mattresses (31.00); plastic sporting, gaming, or toy goods (32.30, 32.40); medical, dental, or ophthalmic appliances (32.50); personal safety equipment (32.99); or plastic components used exclusively for motor vehicles (29.3). description: Manufacture of other non-metallic mineral products
detailled_description:
This division encompasses the industrial manufacturing activities related to the processing of non-metallic minerals, transforming raw materials into a wide variety of finished products. It covers the entire value chain for mineral-based goods, including glass, ceramics, cement, concrete, stone, and specialized abrasive or insulating materials.

This includes, among others:

*   **Glass and Glass Products:** The manufacturing of flat glass and its specialized processing, hollow glass containers and domestic glassware, glass fibres, and technical glassware for laboratory, industrial, or construction purposes (231).
*   **Ceramic and Refractory Products:** The production of refractory goods designed for high-temperature use (232), structural clay building materials such as bricks and roofing tiles (233), and finished porcelain or ceramic items including household articles, sanitary fixtures, and technical or electrical ceramic components (234).
*   **Cement, Lime, and Plaster:** The industrial manufacture of hydraulic binders like clinker and cement, as well as lime and gypsum-based plasters (235).
*   **Articles of Concrete, Cement, and Plaster:** The manufacture of precast concrete and plaster structural elements, ready-mixed concrete and mortars, fibre-cement products, and decorative or specialized articles made from these binders (236).
*   **Stone and Mineral-based Products:** The cutting, shaping, and finishing of stone for construction and monuments (237), as well as the manufacture of abrasive products, mineral insulating materials (such as slag or rock wool), and various articles of non-metallic minerals like mica, peat, or graphite not classified elsewhere (239).

This division does not include the printing onto glass (18.12), the manufacture of woven fabrics of glass yarn (13.96), the extraction and production of rough-cut stone (08.11), the manufacture of graphite electrodes (27.90), the manufacture of carbon or graphite gaskets (28.29), or the manufacture of fibre-optic cables (27.31). Furthermore, it excludes medical-grade materials such as dental cements, artificial teeth, or medical equipment like syringes (32.50).

details.includes: This division includes manufacturing activities related to a single substance of mineral origin. This division includes the manufacture of glass and glass products (for example, flat glass, hollow glass, fibres, technical glassware), ceramic products, tiles and baked clay products, cement, concrete and plaster, from raw materials to finished articles.
details.alsoIcludes:
The manufacture of shaped and finished stone and other mineral products is also included in this division.

This division also includes the manufacture of products of composite materials in which glass and non-metallic minerals (for example, sand, gravel, stone or clay) are the predominant material.

description: Manufacture of glass and glass products
detailled_description:
This category encompasses the manufacturing of glass in all its forms, regardless of the production process, and the subsequent shaping and processing of glass products. It covers the entire value chain from basic glass material production to the creation of finished glass components for industrial, commercial, and domestic use.

This category includes, among others:

*   **Flat Glass and Processing:** The manufacture of flat glass including cast, rolled, drawn, or blown sheets, as well as float glass, wired, tinted, or coated glass (2311). It further includes the specialized shaping and processing of these sheets, such as bending, engraving, drilling, enamelling, toughening, and laminating, as well as the production of mirrors and multiple-walled insulating glass units (2312).
*   **Hollow Glass:** The production of bottles, containers, and domestic glassware, including drinking glasses, table or kitchenware made of glass or crystal, and glass inners for vacuum vessels (2313).
*   **Glass Fibres:** The manufacturing of glass fibres, including glass wool, non-woven glass fibre products, and various secondary products derived from glass fibres (2314).
*   **Technical and Other Glassware:** The production of technical glass for laboratory, hygienic, or pharmaceutical purposes, clock or watch glass, optical glass (not optically worked), glass envelopes for lamps, and glass insulators. It also covers construction-related glass such as blocks, bricks, tiles, and foam glass, as well as decorative items like glass figurines and jewellery components (2315).

This does not include the printing onto glass (18.12), the manufacture of woven fabrics of glass yarn (13.96), the manufacture of slag or rock wool (23.99), the manufacture of fibre-optic cables (27.31), the manufacture of optical elements that are optically worked (26.70), the manufacture of medical equipment like syringes (32.50), the manufacture of vehicle mirrors (29.32), or the manufacture of glass toys (32.40).

This category encompasses the industrial production of specialized refractory products designed to withstand high temperatures and extreme thermal conditions. These goods are primarily manufactured from non-metallic minerals and are essential for high-heat industrial processes and equipment.

This includes the manufacture of refractory ceramic goods and intermediate products derived from mined or quarried non-metallic minerals such as stone, gravel, or clay (2320). Specifically, this category covers the production of heat-insulating ceramic goods made from siliceous fossil meals, as well as the fabrication of refractory bricks, blocks, tiles, and specialized shapes such as retorts, crucibles, muffles, nozzles, tubes, and pipes (2320). Furthermore, it includes the manufacture of refractory mortars and concretes, along with refractory articles containing magnesium oxide, calcium magnesium oxide, or chromite (2320).

*   **Structural clay construction products:** The manufacture of structural non-refractory ceramic articles obtained by firing clay, such as ceramic bricks, roofing tiles, chimney pots, pipes, and conduits, as well as flooring blocks made of baked clay (2332).

This does not include the manufacture of refractory ceramic products (23.20), the manufacture of non-structural non-refractory ceramic products (23.4), or the manufacture of artificial stone articles for construction use (23.61).

description: Manufacture of other porcelain and ceramic products
detailled_description:
This category encompasses the manufacture of a diverse range of finished porcelain and ceramic products, excluding primary construction materials and refractory goods. The activities included range from consumer-oriented household items and sanitary fixtures to specialized technical, electrical, and industrial ceramic components.

This group includes, among others:

*   **Ceramic household and ornamental articles:** The production of ceramic tableware, kitchenware, toilet articles, statuettes, and various ornamental items manufactured from porcelain, china, stoneware, earthenware, or fine pottery (2341).
*   **Ceramic sanitary fixtures:** The manufacture of plumbing and sanitary installations such as sinks, washbasins, pedestals, baths, bidets, water closet pans, and flushing cisterns (2342).
*   **Electrical and technical ceramic components:** The production of ceramic electrical insulators and insulating fittings (2343), as well as other technical ceramic products including ceramic ware for laboratory or chemical use, and non-metallic permanent magnets such as agglomerated ferrite (2344).
*   **General ceramic products:** The manufacture of ceramic receptacles for agricultural or transport use, such as pots, jars, troughs, and tubs, alongside other miscellaneous ceramic products not elsewhere classified (2345).

This category does not include the manufacture of refractory ceramic goods (23.20), ceramic building materials (23.3), artificial stone or cultured marble (23.66), imitation jewellery (32.13), ceramic toys (32.40), or artificial teeth (32.50).

description: Manufacture of cement, lime and plaster
detailled_description:
This category encompasses the industrial production of essential hydraulic binders and construction materials derived from mineral sources. It focuses on the chemical and thermal processing required to manufacture substances used as foundations for mortar, concrete, and various structural applications.

This category includes the manufacture of clinker and various types of hydraulic cements, such as Portland, aluminous, slag, and supersulphate cements (2351). Furthermore, it covers the production of lime—including quicklime, slaked lime, and hydraulic lime—as well as plasters produced from calcined gypsum or calcium sulphate and calcined or sintered dolomite (2352).

This does not include the manufacture of pure chemical calcium oxide and calcium hydroxide (20.12), the manufacture of refractory mortars, concrete, or ready-mixed/dry-mix mortars (23.20, 23.63, 23.64), the manufacture of articles made of cement or plaster (23.62, 23.65, 23.66), or the manufacture of cements used in dentistry (32.50).

description: Manufacture of articles of concrete, cement and plaster
detailled_description:
This category encompasses the manufacture of a wide range of products primarily composed of concrete, cement, and plaster, intended for both construction and decorative or specialized applications. It covers the production of structural elements, ready-to-use mixtures, and finished articles made from these mineral-based materials.

This includes, among others:

*   **Construction Products (Concrete and Plaster):** The manufacture of precast concrete, cement, or artificial stone articles for construction, including tiles, flagstones, building blocks, bricks, panels, pipes, and posts (23.61). This category also encompasses the production of plaster-based articles for construction such as non-ornamented boards, sheets, panels, and tiles (23.62), as well as calcium silicate and autoclaved aerated concrete masonry units (23.61).
*   **Concrete Mixtures and Mortars:** The production of ready-mixed concrete, which is delivered ready to pour (23.63), as well as the manufacturing of non-refractory mortars and concrete mixtures that have not yet been mixed with water (23.64).
*   **Fibre Cement Products:** The manufacture of panels, boards, and tiles made of vegetable substances agglomerated with mineral binders, and the production of articles made of asbestos cement or cellulose fibre cement, such as corrugated sheets, reservoirs, and basins (23.65).
*   **Other Specialized Articles:** The manufacture of decorative or specialized items made of concrete, plaster, cement, or artificial stone, including statuary, vases, flowerpots, and ornamented plaster panels (23.66).

This does not include:
*   The manufacture of refractory cements or mortars (23.20).
*   The manufacture of insulating fibreboards of wood or other ligneous fibres (16.21).
*   The manufacture of precast concrete articles for construction (when categorized under 23.61, specifically in relation to the exclusions listed for other concrete and plaster articles in 23.66).

This includes, among others, the cutting, shaping, and finishing of stone for use in construction, such as roofing materials, stonework for roads, and monuments for cemeteries (2370). Additionally, this category includes the manufacturing of stone furniture (2370).

This does not include quarrying operations, such as the extraction and production of rough-cut stone (08.11), or the production of millstones, abrasive stones, and similar specialized products (23.9).

*   **Abrasive Products:** The production of millstones, grindstones, and grinding wheels, as well as the manufacturing of natural or artificial abrasive powders or grains applied to bases such as paper, paperboard, or textile materials (2391).

detailled_description:
This division encompasses the industrial activities involved in the smelting, refining, and casting of ferrous and non-ferrous metals. It covers the entire metallurgical process chain, from the reduction of ores and the processing of metal waste or scrap to the production of primary metal forms and semi-finished products that serve as inputs for further industrial manufacturing.

This includes, among others, the following clusters:

*   **Primary Iron and Steel Production:** The operation of blast furnaces and steel converters to produce pig iron, ferro-alloys, and primary steel shapes (241). This also includes the manufacture of specialized steel-based tubular products, such as seamless and welded pipes, tubes, hollow profiles, and associated fittings (242), as well as the cold-processing of steel into narrow strips, drawn bars, wire, and cold-formed structural sections (243).
*   **Non-Ferrous and Precious Metal Production:** The industrial refining, alloying, and semi-manufacturing of precious metals (gold, silver, platinum), aluminium, lead, zinc, tin, copper, and other non-ferrous metals (244). This also encompasses the industrial processing of natural uranium for nuclear fuel (244).
*   **Metal Casting:** The operation of foundries utilizing various casting techniques to manufacture components from ferrous (iron and steel) and non-ferrous (light and heavy) metal alloys, including the casting of specialized dental implements (245).

This division does not include the manufacture of finished metal products by further processing castings (such as boilers, radiators, or household items), the manufacturing of forged, pressed, stamped, or powder metallurgy products (classified under Division 25), the shredding of metal waste and scrap (38.21), the manufacture of precious metal jewellery (32.12), or the enrichment of uranium and thorium ores (20.13).

details.includes: This division includes the activities of smelting and/or refining ferrous and non-ferrous metals from ore, pig, metal waste or scrap, using electro-metallurgic and other metallurgical process techniques.
details.alsoIcludes: This division also includes the manufacture of metal alloys and super-alloys by introducing other chemical elements to pure metals. The output of smelting and refining, usually in ingot form, is used in rolling, drawing and extruding operations to make, for example, plate, sheet, strip, bars, rods, wire or tubes, pipes and hollow profiles and other basic metal products, and in molten form to make castings.

description: Manufacture of basic iron and steel and of ferro-alloys
detailled_description:
This category encompasses the primary production processes of the iron and steel industry, ranging from the reduction of iron ore to the manufacturing of primary steel shapes and semi-finished products. It covers the full spectrum of metallurgical operations required to transform raw materials into basic ferrous forms and alloys suitable for further industrial manufacturing.

This includes, among others:

*   **Primary Iron and Steel Production:** The operation of blast furnaces and steel converters, including the production of pig iron and spiegeleisen in primary forms (blocks or pigs), the production of iron of exceptional purity, and the production of ferrous products through direct reduction or other chemical/electrolytic processes (2410).
*   **Ferro-alloys and Raw Processing:** The production of ferro-alloys and the remelting of scrap iron or steel ingots (2410).
*   **Intermediate Steel Products:** The production of granular iron, iron powder, and various primary forms of iron or steel, including semi-finished products, ingots, and blast furnace gas (2410).
*   **Rolling and Finishing Mill Operations:** The manufacture of hot-rolled and cold-rolled flat-rolled products (including coated or uncoated products in coils or lengths of 600 mm or more), hot-rolled bars and rods, open sections, sheet piling, welded open sections, and railway track materials such as unassembled rails (2410).

This does not include the cold drawing of bars, which is classified under category 24.31.

description: Manufacture of tubes, pipes, hollow profiles and related fittings, of steel
detailled_description:
This category encompasses the industrial production of various steel-based tubular products and their associated fittings. It covers the transformation of steel inputs into finished or semi-finished tubes, pipes, and hollow profiles through processes such as rolling, extrusion, drawing, and welding.

This includes, among others:
*   **Seamless Steel Tubes and Pipes:** The manufacture of seamless tubes, pipes, and hollow profiles of circular or non-circular cross-sections, including the production of blanks for further processing via hot rolling or hot extrusion (2420). It also covers precision and non-precision seamless products refined through cold drawing or cold rolling (2420).
*   **Welded Steel Tubes and Pipes:** The production of welded tubes and pipes, whether of circular or non-circular cross-sections. This includes large-diameter pipes (exceeding 406.4 mm) formed from hot-rolled flat products, as well as smaller-diameter (406.4 mm or less) precision and non-precision welded tubes produced via continuous hot or cold forming of strip or flat products (2420).
*   **Pipe and Tube Fittings:** The manufacture of specialized fittings including flat flanges, flanges with forged collars, butt-welding fittings (such as elbows and reductions), and threaded or other miscellaneous steel tube and pipe fittings (2420).

This does not include the manufacture of seamless tubes and pipes of steel produced by centrifugal casting, which is classified under 24.52.

description: Manufacture of other products of first processing of steel
detailled_description:
This category encompasses the manufacture of various steel products through specialized cold-processing techniques, including drawing, rolling, and forming. It focuses on the further processing of intermediate steel products into refined structural shapes, strips, and wire.

This includes, among others:

*   **Cold Drawing of Bars and Wire:** The production of steel bars, rods, and solid sections via cold drawing, grinding, or cold-finishing (24.31), as well as the manufacturing of drawn steel wire through the cold drawing of steel wire rod (24.34).
*   **Cold Rolling of Narrow Strip:** The manufacture of coated or uncoated flat-rolled steel products, in coils or straight lengths, with a width of less than 600 mm, produced by the cold re-rolling of hot-rolled flat products or steel rods (24.32).
*   **Cold Forming and Folding:** The production of open sections through progressive cold forming on a roll mill or folding on a press, as well as the manufacture of cold-formed or cold-folded ribbed sheets and sandwich panels (24.33).

This does not include:
*   The manufacture of flat-rolled steel products with a width of 600 mm or more (24.10).
*   The manufacture of derived wire products (25.93).

description: Manufacture of basic precious and other non-ferrous metals
detailled_description:
This category encompasses the industrial production, refining, and semi-manufacturing of precious metals, aluminium, lead, zinc, tin, copper, and other non-ferrous metals, as well as the processing of nuclear fuel. It covers the transformation of ores, oxides, and metal waste and scrap into unwrought, alloyed, or semi-manufactured forms.

The scope of this category includes the following areas:

*   **Precious Metals:** The production and refining of gold, silver, and platinum group metals, including the creation of precious metal alloys, powders, and semi-finished products such as wire, plates, sheets, and foil, as well as the cladding of base metals with precious metals (2441).
*   **Aluminium Production:** The production of unwrought aluminium and its alloys, the manufacturing of aluminium products (bars, rods, profiles, wires, tubes, pipes, plates, sheets, strips, and foil), and the production of aluminium oxide/alumina (2442).
*   **Lead, Zinc, and Tin:** The production of unwrought lead, zinc, and tin (including alloys) and the manufacturing of their respective semi-manufactured forms such as bars, profiles, sheets, and foils, including zinc powder production (2443).
*   **Copper Production:** The production of unrefined or refined copper and its alloys (such as brass), including the manufacture of bars, rods, profiles, wires, tubes, pipes, and foils (2444).
*   **Other Non-Ferrous Metals:** The production of other non-ferrous metals, such as chrome, manganese, and nickel, including the production of mattes and various semi-manufactured forms derived from ores, oxides, or scrap (2445).
*   **Nuclear Fuel Processing:** The production of natural uranium metal and its compounds, including the manufacturing of ceramic products, alloys, and dispersions containing natural uranium (2446).

This category does not include the casting of non-ferrous metals (see 24.53, 24.54), the shredding of metal waste and scrap (see 38.21), the manufacture of precious metal jewellery (see 32.12), or the enrichment of uranium and thorium ores (see 20.13).

detailled_description:
This category encompasses the industrial activities of foundries that employ various casting processes to manufacture products from ferrous and non-ferrous metal alloys. These operations may include subsequent trimming or descaling of the castings, provided no further processing is performed to create finished goods.

The scope of this category is organized into the following clusters:

*   **Casting of Ferrous Metals:** This includes the manufacture of castings made from iron, such as grey iron, ductile iron (including spheroidal graphite and malleable iron), and other special iron alloys (2451). It also includes the casting of steel, covering carbon, commercial, alloy, high-alloy, and stainless-steel castings (2452).
*   **Casting of Light Metals:** This includes the activities of light metal foundries, specifically producing castings made of aluminium, magnesium, and titanium, as well as the casting of specialized items like dental implements made from these metals (2453).
*   **Casting of Other Non-Ferrous Metals:** This includes the activities of foundries working with non-ferrous metals other than light metals, encompassing the manufacture of castings made from copper, zinc, lead, nickel, and their respective alloys, as well as the casting of dental implements composed of these materials (2454).

This category does not include the manufacture of products obtained through processes other than casting, such as forged, pressed, drawn, stamped, or rolled metal parts, or powder metallurgy products (Division 25). Furthermore, it excludes the manufacture of finished products that require further processing of castings, such as boilers and radiators (25.21), or cast household items, anchors, ships’ propellers, and bells (25.99).

description: Manufacture of fabricated metal products, except machinery and equipment
detailled_description:
This division encompasses the manufacture of a wide range of fabricated metal products, typically characterized by a static or immovable function, as well as the production of composite metal-predominant materials. It covers the transformation of metal into structural elements, industrial containers, weapons, tools, and various specialized hardware components.

This division includes, among others:
*   **Structural Metal Products and Fixtures:** The fabrication of load-bearing metal frameworks, industrial infrastructure, bridges, prefabricated metal buildings, and essential architectural components such as windows, doors, gates, shutters, and blinds (251).
*   **Industrial Vessels and Thermal Equipment:** The manufacture of steam and vapour-generating boilers (excluding central heating boilers), nuclear reactors, industrial reservoirs, tanks, vats, and containers for compressed or liquefied gas with a capacity exceeding 300 litres (252).
*   **Weapons and Ammunition:** The production of military and combat weapon systems, firearms for sporting or protective purposes, and various types of ammunition including bombs, grenades, and cartridges (253).
*   **Metal Forming and Metallurgy:** The mechanical shaping of metal through forging, pressing, stamping, and roll-forming, alongside the production of components using powder metallurgy (254).
*   **Metal Treatment, Coating, and Machining:** Professional services for surface treatment (galvanizing, electroplating, anodizing, and non-metallic coatings), heat treatment (hardening, tempering, annealing), and mechanical machining operations such as boring, turning, milling, welding, and laser-cutting (255).
*   **Cutlery, Tools, and Hardware:** The production of domestic and professional cutlery, edged implements, security hardware (locks and hinges), non-power-driven hand tools, and interchangeable industrial tools such as drills, saw blades, and press tools (256).
*   **General Fabricated Metal Products:** The manufacture of diverse metal items including packaging (cans, drums, buckets), fasteners (screws, bolts, nuts), wire-based goods (springs, chains, fencing), and miscellaneous items such as office supplies, safes, ship propellers, and anchors (259).

This division does not include the manufacture of complex assemblies with moving parts (other than purely electrical or electronic) which are typically classified under divisions 26 to 30. Furthermore, it does not include specialised repair and maintenance activities of fabricated metal products and machinery (33.1), or the specialised installation of manufactured goods into buildings, such as central heating boilers (43.22).

details.includes: This division includes the manufacture of pure metal products (for example, parts, containers, structures), usually with a static, immovable function. This is in contrast to divisions 26 to 30, which cover the manufacture of combinations or assemblies of such metal products (sometimes with other materials) into more complex units that – unless they are purely electrical, electronic or optical – work with moving parts.
details.alsoIcludes:

detailled_description:
This category encompasses the manufacture of various structural metal products, ranging from large-scale load-bearing frameworks to specialized architectural building components. It covers the production of essential construction elements, industrial infrastructure, and diverse fixtures for residential and commercial buildings.

This category includes, among others:

*   **Metal Frameworks and Structural Components:** The fabrication of metal skeletons and frameworks for construction, including towers, lattice masts, trusses, and bridge sections (2511). This cluster also encompasses industrial frameworks for blast furnaces and heavy handling equipment, as well as general supporting structures for items such as lights or loudspeakers (2511).
*   **Construction Support Equipment:** The production of specialized hardware for construction sites, including equipment for scaffolding, shuttering, propping, and pit-propping (2511).
*   **Prefabricated Buildings and Architectural Features:** The manufacture of prefabricated metal structures such as site huts and modular exhibition elements, as well as temporary spatial extensions (2511, 2512).
*   **Doors, Windows, and Fixtures:** The production of metal doors, windows, and their associated frames, thresholds, shutters, and gates. It also includes the manufacture of metal room partitions for floor attachment, as well as metal blinds, sunblinds, and insect screens (2512).

This does not include the manufacture of parts for marine or power boilers (25.21), assembled railway track fixtures (25.99), motor vehicle coachwork (29.20), or sections of ships (30.11, 30.13).

description: Manufacture of tanks, reservoirs and containers of metal
detailled_description:
This category encompasses the manufacture of industrial and domestic metal vessels, structures for steam generation, and heating equipment. It covers the production of both large-scale industrial containers and specialized thermal and pressure-based equipment.

This includes, among others:

*   **Steam Generation and Heating Equipment:** The manufacture of central heating radiators (non-electrically heated), steam or other vapour-generating boilers, and marine or power boilers. It also encompasses the production of auxiliary plant for steam generation, including economisers, superheaters, steam collectors, accumulators, and condensers for steam power units, as well as the manufacturing of nuclear reactors (2521).
*   **Metal Reservoirs and Containers:** The manufacture of metal reservoirs, tanks, vats, and similar containers with a capacity exceeding 300 litres, whether or not lined or heat-insulated, as well as metal containers designed for compressed or liquefied gas (2522).

This does not include the manufacture of electrical ovens and water heaters (27.51), boiler turbine sets (28.11), household heating equipment (28.21), or isotope separators (28.99). Furthermore, it excludes metal packaging such as casks, drums, cans, pails, and boxes with a capacity not exceeding 300 litres (25.91, 25.92), specialized transport containers (29.20), and armoured military vehicles (30.40).

This category encompasses the manufacturing of firearms, weapons systems, and associated ammunition intended for both military and civilian use. It covers the production of various types of projectile-based equipment and their specific munitions.

This category includes, among others:
*   **Military and Combat Weapons:** The production of artillery weapons, rocket and grenade launchers, flame-throwers, torpedo tubes, machine guns, and other similar projectors (2530).
*   **Firearms for Various Purposes:** The manufacturing of pistols, rifles, and shotguns, as well as spring, air, or gas-powered guns and pistols intended for hunting, sporting, or protective purposes (2530).
*   **Ammunition:** The production of war ammunition, including bombs, grenades, torpedoes, mines, and missiles, as well as cartridges designed for shotguns, revolvers, and pistols (2530).

This does not include the manufacture of percussion caps, detonators, or signalling flares (20.59); the manufacture of cold steel weapons such as cutlasses, swords, and bayonets (25.61); the manufacture of optical gun-sighting equipment (26.70); the manufacture of bodies for armoured vehicles (29.20); the building of military ships and vessels (30.13); the manufacture of military air and spacecraft (30.32); or the manufacture of tanks and other armoured and motorised fighting vehicles (30.40).

description: Forging and shaping metal and powder metallurgy
detailled_description:
This category encompasses industrial processes involved in the physical shaping and transformation of metal through mechanical force and thermal treatment. It covers both traditional metal forming techniques and the specialized production of components from metallic powders.

This category includes the following activities:
*   **Metal Forming:** The mechanical shaping of metal through processes such as forging, pressing, stamping, and roll-forming (2540). 
*   **Powder Metallurgy:** The production of metal objects directly from metal powders, achieved through processes such as heat treatment (sintering) or the application of pressure (2540).
*   **Post-Forming Treatments:** Essential preparatory or finishing work, specifically the subsequent trimming or descaling of metal parts, provided no further manufacturing processes are performed (2540).

This category does not include the production of metal powder itself, which is classified under the manufacture of basic metals (24.10, 24.4).

description: Treatment and coating of metals; machining
detailled_description:
This category encompasses specialized industrial activities related to the surface treatment, heat treatment, and mechanical processing of metals, typically performed on a fee or contract basis. It covers a broad spectrum of technical operations designed to alter the physical or chemical properties of metal workpieces or to achieve specific surface finishes.

The activities in this category are organized into the following areas:

*   **Coating and Surface Finishing:** This includes various methods for applying protective or decorative coatings to metal surfaces, such as galvanizing (including general batch hot-dip galvanizing), electroplating, anodizing, cladding, and chemical conversion coating (phosphate or chromate). It also encompasses non-metallic coating processes like powder or plastic coating, enameling, lacquering, and the general coloring of metals (2551).
*   **Heat Treatment:** This covers professional heat treatment services aimed at modifying the metallurgical properties of metals. It includes thermomechanical processes (such as preheating, annealing, hardening, tempering, quenching, and deep freezing) as well as thermochemical treatments (including carburizing, carbonitriding, nitriding, oxidizing, and boriding) (2552).
*   **Machining and Mechanical Processing:** This involves a wide range of subtractive and finishing operations performed on metalwork pieces, such as boring, turning, milling, eroding, planing, lapping, broaching, levelling, sawing, grinding, sharpening, deburring, sandblasting, tumbling, polishing, and buffing. Additionally, it includes welding, splicing, and precision metal cutting or engraving using laser beam technology (2553).

This category does not include the activities of farriers (01.62), printing onto metals (18.12), or the metal coating of plastics (22.25). It also excludes the cladding of base metals with precious metals like silver, gold, or platinum (24.41), the painting of metals on buildings and civil engineering structures (43.34), and "while-you-wait" engraving services (95.29).

description: Manufacture of cutlery, tools and general hardware
detailled_description:
This category comprises the manufacturing of a wide range of metal goods, including domestic and specialized cutlery, locking mechanisms, and various professional-grade tools. It encompasses the production of both manual implements and essential hardware fittings used in construction, furniture, and industrial machinery.

The scope of this category is organized into the following clusters:

*   **Cutlery and Personal Blades:** This includes the production of domestic cutlery such as knives, forks, and spoons (2561), as well as specialized items including razors, razor blades, scissors, hair clippers, cleavers, choppers, and edged weapons like swords and bayonets (2561).
*   **Locks and Hardware Fittings:** This includes the manufacture of security hardware and structural fittings, specifically padlocks, locks, keys, and hinges, as well as general metal mountings for buildings, furniture, and vehicles (2562).
*   **Tools and Industrial Implements:** This includes the manufacture of non-power-driven hand tools such as pliers, screwdrivers, and blacksmiths’ tools (2563). description: Manufacture of other fabricated metal products
detailled_description:
This category encompasses the manufacture of a wide range of fabricated metal products intended for diverse household, commercial, and industrial applications. It includes the production of metal containers, packaging, wire-based goods, fasteners, and various specialized metal articles.

The scope of this category covers the following logical clusters:

*   **Metal Containers and Packaging:** This includes the manufacture of steel tanks, drums, buckets, and boxes (2591), as well as light metal packaging such as aluminium casks, tins, cans for food products, collapsible tubes, and various metallic closures (2592).
*   **Wire Products, Chains, and Springs:** This involves the production of metal cables, plaited bands, barbed wire, fencing, grills, netting, and wire cloth (2593). It also includes coated electrodes for welding, nails, pins, various types of springs (e.g., leaf, helical, torsion), and chains, excluding power transmission chains (2593).
*   **Fasteners and Screw Machine Products:** This includes the production of threaded fasteners such as bolts, screws, and nuts, as well as non-threaded products like rivets and washers (2594).
*   **Miscellaneous Fabricated Metal Products:** This includes a broad array of articles, such as household flatware, hollowware, and non-electrical kitchen utensils; building components like gutters and washbasins; office supplies; safes and armoured doors; and specialized items such as ship propellers, anchors, bells, metal ladders, road signs, and various personal accessories (2599).

This category does not include the manufacture of containers for compressed or liquefied gas with a capacity exceeding 300 litres (2591, 2592); clock or watch springs (2593); electrical wire and cable (2593); power transmission chains (2593); swords and bayonets (2599); shopping carts (2599); metal furniture (2599); or sports goods, games, and toys (2599).
