description: Manufacture of computer, electronic and optical products
detailled_description:
The division encompasses the manufacture of computers, computer peripherals, communication equipment, and a wide array of electronic and optical products, including their essential components. These production processes are characterized by the integration of electronic circuits and the application of highly specialized miniaturization technologies.

This category includes, among others, the following clusters of activity:

*   **Electronic Components and Boards:** The fabrication of semiconductors, integrated circuits, microprocessors, and passive components (e.g., capacitors, resistors), as well as the manufacturing and assembly of bare and loaded printed circuit boards and display components (261).
*   **Computing and Data Infrastructure:** The production of computing systems ranging from mainframes to handheld devices, along with peripheral equipment such as monitors, keyboards, storage hardware, and multifunctional office and imaging equipment (262).
*   **Communication Equipment:** The manufacture of wired and wireless telecommunication apparatus, including switching equipment, mobile telephones, modems, routers, and broadcasting infrastructure for radio and television (263).
*   **Consumer Electronics:** The manufacture of home and automotive audio/video equipment, including television receivers, optical media players, amplifiers, home theater systems, and interactive devices like gaming consoles (264).
*   **Precision Measuring and Timing Instruments:** The production of industrial and scientific sensing, testing, and navigation systems (e.g., radar, GPS, laboratory analytical instruments), alongside time-keeping devices such as clocks and watches (265).
*   **Medical and Radiation Technology:** The manufacture of specialized equipment for medical diagnosis and therapy, including X-ray and radiation apparatus, MRI and CT scanners, and electromedical/therapeutic devices (266).
*   **Optical and Photographic Equipment:** The production of optical instruments such as binoculars, telescopes, and microscopes; photographic cameras and projection equipment; and unrecorded magnetic and optical storage media (267).

This division does not include the manufacture of conductors for electronic use and optical fiber cables (Division 27); the printing of smart cards (18.12); the reproduction of recorded media (18.20); the manufacture of medical thermometers (32.50) or ophthalmic goods (32.50); or the manufacture of electronic games with fixed, non-replaceable software (32.40).

description: Manufacture of electronic components and boards
detailled_description:
This category encompasses the manufacturing activities related to the production of essential electronic components and the assembly of printed circuit boards. It covers the full lifecycle of these parts, from the fabrication of individual electronic semiconductors and discrete devices to the specialized mounting of components onto circuit boards.

This includes, among others:

*   **Electronic Components:** The manufacture of semiconductors, integrated circuits (analogue, digital, or hybrid), microprocessors, diodes, transistors, and related discrete devices (2611). It also encompasses the production of electron tubes, electronic crystals and assemblies, and passive components such as capacitors, resistors, inductors (chokes, coils, transformers), and solenoids (2611). Furthermore, it includes the manufacturing of bare printed circuit boards (consisting only of conductor elements and contacts), specialized cables (printer, monitor, USB), display components (plasma, LCD, LEDs), and photovoltaic cells (2611).
*   **Loaded Electronic Boards:** The manufacture of loaded printed circuit boards, which involves the physical assembly and mounting of passive elements or electronic components onto circuit boards (2612). This also includes the production of interface cards, such as sound, video, controller, network, and modem cards that are loaded with electronic components (2612).

This does not include:
*   The printing of smart cards (18.12).
*   The manufacture of finished computer and television displays (26.20, 26.40), modems as carrier equipment (26.30), X-ray tubes (26.60), or optical equipment (26.70).
*   The manufacture of electrical equipment such as fluorescent ballasts, electrical relays, solar generators, electrical wiring devices, or assembled insulated electric conductors (Division 27).
*   The manufacture of solar water heaters (28.21) or the installation services of solar panels and heating systems (43.21, 43.22).

description: Manufacture of computers and peripheral equipment
detailled_description:
This category encompasses the manufacture and assembly of electronic computers and their associated peripheral equipment. It covers various types of computing devices—including analogue, digital, and hybrid systems—as well as the hardware used for data input, output, and storage.

The scope of this category includes the following logical clusters:

*   **Computing Systems:** The manufacture of all classes of computers, including mainframe computers, desktop computers, laptops, handheld computers, and computer servers (2620).
*   **Peripheral and Input/Output Equipment:** The production of various devices such as monitors, keyboards, mice, joysticks, trackball accessories, and dedicated computer terminals, including non-mechanically operated automatic teller machines (ATMs) and point-of-sale (POS) terminals (2620).
*   **Storage and Data Processing Hardware:** The manufacture of storage devices such as magnetic disk drives and flash drives, optical disc drives, scanners (including barcode scanners), smart card readers, and computer projectors (video beamers) (2620).
*   **Office and Imaging Equipment:** The manufacture of printers and multifunction office equipment capable of performing two or more functions, such as printing, scanning, copying, or telefaxing, as well as the production and refilling of toner and ink cartridges (2620).

This does not include the reproduction of recorded media (18.20); the manufacture of electronic components, interface cards, modems, or loaded printed circuit boards (26.1, 26.12); the manufacture of carrier equipment, digital communication switches, bridges, routers, or gateways (26.30); the manufacture of consumer electronic devices such as CD/DVD players or video game consoles (26.40); the manufacture of television monitors (26.40); the manufacture of blank optical and magnetic media (26.70); or the refilling of ink and toner cartridges by retail sellers (47.40).

description: Manufacture of computers and peripheral equipment

details.includes:
This class includes the manufacture and/or assembly of electronic computers (for example, mainframes, desktop computers, laptops, computer servers); computer peripheral equipment (for example, storage devices, input/output devices, such as printers, monitors, keyboards). Computers can be analogue, digital, or hybrid. Digital computers, the most common type, are devices that do all of the following: (1) store the processing program or programs and the data immediately necessary for the execution of a program, (2) can be freely programmed in accordance with the requirements of the user, (3) perform arithmetical computations specified by the user and (4) execute, without human intervention, a processing program that requires the computer to modify its execution by logical decision during the processing run. Analogue computers are capable of simulating mathematical models and comprise at least analogue control and programming elements.

This category encompasses the manufacture of telephone and data communication equipment designed to facilitate the electronic transmission of signals through wired or wireless networks, including radio and television broadcasting infrastructures.

This includes, among others, the production of central office switching equipment, private branch exchange (PBX) systems, and various forms of telephone and facsimile apparatus, such as cordless phones, telephone answering machines, and mobile telephones (Manufacture of communication equipment). The scope also covers data communication hardware, including bridges, routers, gateways, and modems, as well as specialized transmission and receiving infrastructure, such as antennas, carrier equipment, and cable television apparatus. This does not include the manufacture of electronic components, sub-assemblies (such as computer modems), or loaded printed circuit boards (26.12); computers and peripheral equipment (26.20); consumer audio and video equipment (26.40); burglar and fire-alarm systems or Global Positioning System (GPS) devices (26.51); or electronic scoreboards and traffic lights (27.90).

description: Manufacture of measuring testing instruments, clocks and watches
detailled_description:
This category encompasses the manufacture of precision equipment designed for sensing, measuring, testing, navigating, and monitoring, as well as the production of time-measuring devices, clocks, and watches. It covers both industrial and consumer-oriented instrumentation, including sophisticated electronic systems, laboratory apparatus, and mechanical or synchronous timing mechanisms.

This includes, among others:

*   **Measuring, Testing, and Navigation Systems:** The manufacture of search, detection, guidance, aeronautical, and nautical systems (including radar equipment and GPS devices); instruments for measuring, displaying, recording, and controlling physical and chemical parameters such as temperature, humidity, pressure, flow, viscosity, and acidity (2651). This cluster also includes automatic controls for industrial and domestic applications (e.g., heating, air conditioning, and appliances), environmental controls, laboratory analytical instruments (e.g., spectrometers, balances, incubators), and consumption meters for gas, water, and electricity (2651).
*   **Time-keeping and Timing Devices:** The manufacture of watches, clocks of all kinds, and instrument panel clocks. It also encompasses the production of time-recording and interval-measuring equipment, such as parking meters, time clocks, process timers, and time switches or locks driven by watch movements or synchronous motors (2652).
*   **Components and Specialized Parts:** The production of parts for clocks and watches, including movements, springs, jewels, dials, hands, and housings of all materials, as well as parts for the aforementioned measuring and navigational instruments (2651, 2652).

This does not include the manufacture of telephone answering machines (2630), irradiation equipment (2660), optical positioning equipment (2670), dictating machines (2823), or heavy weighing machinery such as non-laboratory scales and tape measures (2829). Furthermore, it excludes the manufacture of medical thermometers (3250), smartwatches (2630), non-metallic watch bands (1512), and watch bands made of precious or non-precious metals (3212, 3213). The installation of industrial process control equipment is also excluded (3320).

description: Manufacture of irradiation, electromedical and electrotherapeutic equipment
detailled_description:
This category encompasses the manufacture of specialized electronic equipment used for radiation, medical diagnosis, and therapeutic treatment. It covers a wide range of sophisticated instruments designed for industrial, scientific, and clinical healthcare applications.

This category includes, among others, the manufacture of radiation apparatus and associated tubes, such as alpha, beta, gamma, and X-ray equipment (2660). It further comprises high-technology diagnostic imaging systems, including computed tomography (CT) scanners, positron emission tomography (PET) scanners, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) equipment, and medical ultrasound devices (2660). Additionally, it covers the production of various electromedical and therapeutic instruments, such as electrocardiographs, endoscopic equipment, medical laser devices, artificial or therapeutic respiration apparatus, pacemakers, and hearing aids (2660). The scope also extends to equipment utilized for food and milk irradiation (2660).

This does not include the manufacture of tanning beds (see 27.90).

description: Manufacture of optical instruments, magnetic and optical media and photographic equipment
detailled_description:
This category encompasses the manufacture of precision optical instruments, photographic apparatus, and unrecorded magnetic and optical storage media. It covers the production of specialized optical components, light-sensitive equipment, and various technical measuring devices essential for scientific, industrial, and consumer applications.

This category includes the following logical clusters:

*   **Optical Instruments and Components:** This includes the manufacture of optical mirrors, prisms, and various types of lenses, as well as the coating, polishing, and mounting of lenses (excluding ophthalmic lenses). It also encompasses the production of microscopes (excluding electron and proton microscopes), telescopes, binoculars, and optical magnifying instruments.
*   **Precision Optical and Measuring Equipment:** This includes the manufacture of optical machinist’s precision tools, optical comparators, and optical positioning or gun-sighting equipment. It further covers optical measuring and checking devices, such as rangefinders, fire control equipment, and photographic light meters.
*   **Photographic and Projection Equipment:** This includes the manufacture of film and digital cameras, motion picture and slide projectors, and overhead transparency projectors, as well as the production of objective lenses for these devices.
*   **Media and Laser Assemblies:** This includes the manufacture of unrecorded magnetic audio and videotapes, unrecorded optical disks, and specialized laser assemblies.

This does not include the reproduction of recorded media (18.20); the manufacture of computer projectors (26.20); the manufacture of television studio and broadcasting equipment, including television cameras (26.30); the manufacture of household-type video cameras (26.40); the manufacture of fire alarms (26.51); the manufacture of complete equipment using laser components, such as medical laser equipment (26.60); the manufacture of photocopy machines (28.23); or the manufacture of ophthalmic goods (32.50).

detailled_description:
This division encompasses the manufacture of a broad range of products that generate, distribute, and utilize electrical power, including electrical lighting, signaling equipment, and various domestic appliances. It serves as the industrial backbone for electrical infrastructure, covering everything from heavy-duty power generation and control systems to consumer-facing electrical goods.

This includes, among others:

*   **Power Generation, Distribution, and Control:** The manufacture of electric motors, generators, and power, distribution, or arc welding transformers (2711), as well as electricity distribution and control apparatus such as power circuit breakers, relays, fuses, and power switching equipment (2712).
*   **Energy Storage:** The industrial production of primary cells, dry-cell batteries, and rechargeable accumulators (including lead-acid, NiCad, NiMH, and lithium-ion technologies), along with essential battery components (2720).
*   **Wiring and Connectivity:** The production of insulated wires and cables, including fibre-optic cables for data transmission (2731, 2732), and a wide array of current-carrying and non-current-carrying wiring devices like switches, sockets, plugs, and junction boxes (2733).
*   **Lighting Equipment:** The manufacture of light sources (such as LED, discharge, and incandescent lamps) and fixed or portable lighting fixtures for residential, industrial, and transport applications (2740).
*   **Domestic Appliances:** The manufacture of household appliances powered by electricity, gas, or other fuels, spanning major kitchen and laundry equipment (refrigerators, dishwashers, washing machines), floor care devices, and small personal care or kitchen electrics (2751, 2752).
*   **Miscellaneous Electrical Equipment:** The production of specialized hardware, including electrical signaling equipment (traffic lights, sirens, electronic signs), industrial welding and soldering equipment, power supplies (UPS, battery chargers), and various electromechanical components like capacitors, resistors, and carbon/graphite electrodes (2790).

This does not include the manufacture of electronic components, such as integrated circuits, photovoltaic cells, or electronic-grade transformers and switches (Division 26); glass or porcelain insulators (23); or the manufacture of specific motor vehicle electrical components, such as automotive wiring harnesses, ignition systems, or electric motors specifically designed for vehicles (Division 29).

description: Manufacture of electric motors, generators, transformers and electricity distribution and control apparatus
detailled_description:
This category encompasses the manufacture of equipment essential for the generation, transformation, and distribution of electric power, as well as the apparatus required to control these electrical currents. It covers a broad range of industrial electrical machinery, from heavy-duty power generation units and distribution transformers to specialized switching and control systems.

This category includes, among others:
*   **Electric motors, generators, and transformers:** The manufacture of all types of electric motors (excluding motor vehicles) and power, distribution, and arc welding transformers (2711). This cluster also includes the production of power and solar generators, motor generator sets (excluding turbine generator sets), voltage regulators, ballasts for discharge lamps, and the industrial rewinding of armatures (2711). Additionally, it includes power conversion equipment such as inverters, rectifiers, converters, and electric linear actuators (2711).
*   **Electricity distribution and control apparatus:** The manufacture of equipment designed for the regulation and distribution of electricity, including power circuit breakers, electrical relays, electric fuses, and surge suppressors for distribution-level voltage (2712). This also includes the production of control panels for electric power distribution, power switching equipment, and ducts for electrical switchboard apparatus (2712).

This does not include the manufacture of electronic component-type transformers, switches, or photovoltaic cells (26.11); environmental controls and industrial process control instruments (26.51); switches for electrical circuits such as push-button, snap, or tumbler switches (27.33); electric welding and soldering equipment (27.90); turbine generator sets (28.11); electric motors designed specifically for motor vehicles (29.10); or starting motors and generators for internal combustion engines (29.31).

description: Manufacture of wiring and wiring devices

description: Manufacture of machinery and equipment n.e.c.
detailled_description:
This division encompasses the manufacture of machinery and equipment that act independently on materials—either mechanically or thermally—or perform operational tasks such as handling, spraying, weighing, or packing. It covers a vast range of devices, including fixed, mobile, and handheld equipment designed for industrial, agricultural, building, and commercial use, as well as the production of primary mechanical components that generate and apply force.

The scope of this division is categorized into the following logical clusters:

*   **General-Purpose Machinery:** This includes prime movers and energy-conversion systems such as internal combustion engines (excluding automotive), steam and hydraulic turbines (2811), and fluid power equipment (2812). It also covers pumps, compressors, and pneumatic systems (2813), industrial taps and valves (2814), and mechanical power transmission components like bearings, gears, and clutches (2815).
*   **Other General-Purpose Equipment:** This encompasses thermal and climate control systems including industrial furnaces and non-domestic refrigeration (2821, 2825), as well as material handling machinery like cranes, hoists, and conveyors (2822). It further includes office-support equipment, such as vending machines and cash registers (2823, 2829), power-driven handheld tools (2824), and various processing machines for weighing, filtering, spraying, and cleaning (2829).
*   **Agricultural and Forestry Machinery:** This covers specialized equipment for the full agricultural value chain, including tractors (2830), soil preparation and cultivation machinery (ploughs, harrows, seeders), harvesting and threshing equipment, and specialized livestock management systems (2830).
*   **Metal Forming and Machine Tools:** This involves stationary equipment designed for shaping and processing hard materials, including metalworking machine tools (2841) and machine tools for working wood, bone, stone, hard rubber, and hard plastics (2842).
*   **Other Special-Purpose Machinery:** This includes equipment designed for exclusive use in specific industries, such as mining, construction, and earth-moving machinery (2891, 2892); machinery for food, beverage, and tobacco processing (2893); and equipment for the textile, apparel, and leather industries (2894). It also covers machinery for paper production (2895), plastics and rubber processing (2896), additive manufacturing (2897), and miscellaneous applications like printing and fairground amusement equipment (2899).

This division does not include the manufacture of metal products for general use (division 25), measurement and testing equipment, computer equipment, control devices, electricity distribution apparatus (divisions 26 and 27), or general-purpose motor vehicles (division 29).

details.includes:
This division includes the manufacture of machinery and equipment that act independently on materials either mechanically or thermally or perform operations on materials (for example, handling, spraying, weighing or packing), including their mechanical components that produce and apply force, and any specially manufactured primary parts. This includes the manufacture of fixed and mobile or handheld devices, regardless of whether they are designed for industrial, building and civil engineering, agricultural or home use. The manufacture of special equipment for passenger or freight transport within demarcated premises also belongs within this division.
This division distinguishes between the manufacture of special-purpose machinery, in other words, machinery for exclusive use in a NACE activity or a small cluster of NACE activities, and general-purpose machinery, in other words, machinery that is being used in a wide range of NACE activities.
details.alsoIcludes: This division also includes the manufacture of other special-purpose machinery, not covered elsewhere in the classification, whether or not used in a manufacturing process (for example, fairground amusement equipment, automatic bowling alley equipment).
details.excludes: This division excludes the manufacture of metal products for general use (division 25), associated control devices, computer equipment, measurement and testing equipment, electricity distribution and control apparatus (divisions 26 and 27) and general-purpose motor vehicles (division 29).

detailled_description:
This category encompasses the manufacture of machinery and equipment that serve a broad range of industrial and functional purposes across multiple sectors, excluding highly specialized equipment designed for specific vehicles or aircraft. It covers the production of prime movers, energy-conversion systems, and critical mechanical components essential for the operation of diverse industrial machinery.

This includes, among others:
*   **Engines and Turbines:** The production of non-automotive/non-aerospace internal combustion engines, such as marine and railway engines, as well as steam, hydraulic, gas, and wind turbines (2811). This also covers engine components like pistons, valves, and turbine-generator sets.
*   **Fluid Power and Pumping Equipment:** The manufacture of hydraulic and pneumatic power systems, including cylinders, motors, and valves (2812), alongside air and vacuum pumps, gas compressors, and various pumps for liquids, including hand-operated pumps (2813).
*   **Taps and Valves:** The production of industrial taps and valves, including regulating valves for sanitary fixtures and central heating systems (2814).
*   **Mechanical Power Transmission:** The manufacture of ball and roller bearings, gears, gearboxes, speed changers, clutches, shaft couplings, flywheels, pulleys, and transmission chains (2815).

This does not include:
*   The manufacture of specialized engines and components for motor vehicles, aircraft, or motorcycles (29.10, 29.3, 30.3, 30.91).
*   The manufacture of electric generators (except turbine-generator sets) (27.11).
*   The manufacture of specific materials like rubber, glass, or ceramic valves (22.12, 23.15, 23.44) or general-purpose metal chains not used for power transmission (25.93).
*   Valves, gears, or clutches specifically designed for automotive or aircraft use (29.31, 29.32).

detailled_description:
This category encompasses the manufacture of a broad range of machinery and equipment designed for general industrial, commercial, and office applications that are not specific to a single industry. It includes the production of thermal processing equipment, lifting and handling systems, office-support hardware, power-driven tools, professional-grade climate control systems, and various other specialized mechanical appliances.

This includes, among others:
*   **Thermal and Climate Control Equipment:** Industrial and laboratory furnaces, ovens, and incinerators, as well as central heating boilers, solar water heaters, and non-domestic air conditioning, refrigerating, and freezing equipment, including heat exchange units and gas liquefaction machinery (2821, 2825).
*   **Lifting and Handling Machinery:** Mechanical equipment for moving goods, such as cranes, hoists, winches, conveyors, lifts, escalators, moving walkways, and industrial robots specifically designed for loading or handling tasks (2822).
*   **Office and Utility Equipment:** Machinery for office tasks including cash registers, calculators, postage meters, photocopying machines, dictating machines, and various binding or mailing equipment, as well as automatic goods vending machines (2823, 2829).
*   **Power-Driven Tools:** Hand-held tools equipped with integrated electric, pneumatic, or other motors, such as industrial saws, drills, sanders, grinders, and pneumatic nailers or rivet guns (2824).
*   **General-Purpose Process Machinery:** A wide array of mechanical equipment, including weighing machinery, filtering and purifying apparatus for liquids, spray and fire-extinguishing equipment, industrial packaging and labeling machines, cleaning machines for non-domestic use, centrifuges (excluding laboratory types), and non-electrical welding and soldering apparatus (2829).

This does not include domestic electrical appliances (such as household fans, electric ovens, or domestic refrigerators), specialized agricultural or horticultural machinery, specific machinery for metallurgy (metal rolling), printing machinery, laboratory-grade testing or sterilization equipment, or computers and their peripherals.

description: Manufacture of agricultural and forestry machinery
detailled_description:
This category encompasses the manufacture of specialized machinery and equipment designed specifically for agricultural, horticultural, and forestry operations. It covers the full spectrum of equipment used from soil preparation and cultivation to harvesting, processing, and livestock management.

This includes, among others:
*   **Tractors:** The manufacture of agricultural and forestry tractors, including track-laying tractors and single-axle (pedestrian-controlled) tractors (2830).
*   **Soil Preparation and Cultivation Machinery:** Equipment such as ploughs, harrows, manure spreaders, seeders, and fertilizer distributors (2830).
*   **Harvesting and Post-Harvesting Machinery:** Harvesting and threshing machinery, including harvesters, threshers, sorters, as well as machines for cleaning, sorting, or grading eggs and fruits (2830).
*   **Livestock and Specialized Equipment:** Machinery for milking, poultry-keeping, bee-keeping, fodder preparation, and specialized equipment for vertical farming (2830).
*   **General Agricultural Equipment:** Mowers (including lawnmowers) and self-loading or self-unloading trailers and semi-trailers specifically designed for agricultural purposes (2830).

This does not include the manufacture of non-power-driven hand tools used in agriculture or forestry (25.63), power-driven hand tools (28.24), or conveyors for farm use (28.22). Furthermore, it excludes earth-moving machinery (28.92), cream separators and machinery for cleaning, sorting, or grading seed, grain, or dried leguminous vegetables (28.93), road tractors for semi-trailers (29.10), and trailers or semi-trailers intended for non-agricultural use (29.20).

description: Manufacture of metal forming machinery and machine tools
detailled_description:
This category encompasses the manufacture of industrial machinery and machine tools designed for shaping, finishing, and processing metals and other hard materials. It covers a broad spectrum of stationary equipment, ranging from high-precision metal-forming systems to specialized tools for working non-metallic materials such as wood, stone, and plastics.

This includes, among others:
*   **Metalworking machinery (2841):** The manufacture of machine tools for removing metal or cermets through turning, drilling, boring, threading, milling, planing, or grinding processes. This category also includes high-tech machining centers and multi-station machines, as well as specialized metal-forming equipment like stamping presses, hydraulic brakes, drop hammers, forging machines, wire-working machines (draw benches, thread rollers), and various metal-finishing tools (filing, riveting, and sheet metal cutting). These tools may utilize advanced technologies, including laser beams, ultrasonic waves, plasma arcs, or magnetic pulses.
*   **Other machine tools and accessories (2842):** The manufacture of stationary machine tools designed for working hard materials such as wood, cork, bone, stone, hard rubber, hard plastics, ceramics, concrete, and cold glass. It also covers stationary assembly machines (e.g., for nailing, stapling, or gluing), specialized attachments such as dividing heads and work holders, and the production of parts and accessories specifically for these machine tools.

This does not include the manufacture of interchangeable tools for machine tools (e.g., drills, dies, saw blades) (25.63); electrical welding and soldering machinery or equipment (27.90); power-driven hand tools (28.24); machinery used specifically in metal mills, foundries, mining, or quarrying (28.91, 28.92); or machinery dedicated to additive manufacturing (28.97).

This group encompasses the manufacture of special-purpose machinery designed for exclusive use within a specific industry or a limited cluster of industries. It includes machinery utilized in manufacturing processes—such as food processing, textile production, and metallurgy—as well as specialized equipment for non-manufacturing sectors, including amusement park equipment, aircraft launching gear, and industrial robots.

This category includes the following functional clusters:
*   **Metallurgy, Mining, and Construction Machinery:** Equipment for handling hot metals and rolling mills (2891), as well as machinery for mining, quarrying, and earth-moving (e.g., excavators, bulldozers, and boring machinery) and construction equipment like concrete mixers and pile-drivers (2892).
*   **Food, Beverage, and Tobacco Processing:** Machinery for the industrial preparation of dairy, grain, bakery, meat, and beverage products, as well as tobacco processing equipment and industrial-grade cooking or heating apparatus for hotels and restaurants (2893).
*   **Textile, Apparel, and Leather Production:** Equipment for the production and processing of fibres, yarns, and fabrics, including knitting, weaving, and textile printing machines, as well as industrial laundry, dry-cleaning, sewing, and leather-working machinery (2894).
*   **Material Processing Machinery:** Equipment for paper and paperboard production (2895), machines for working soft rubber and plastics (2896), and machinery for additive manufacturing across various materials (2897).
*   **Miscellaneous Special-Purpose Machinery:** A wide range of industrial equipment, including printing and bookbinding machinery, semiconductor manufacturing equipment, machines for glass and ceramic production, industrial robots, waste-compressing machines, and various fairground and amusement equipment (2899).

This does not include the manufacture of moulding boxes and moulds (except ingot moulds) (25.63); household appliances (27.5); domestic washing and drying machines (27.51); lifting and handling equipment (28.22); office equipment such as photocopiers (28.23); general-purpose packing, wrapping, or weighing machinery (28.29); tractors (28.30, 29.10); specific machine tools for working stone, hard rubber, or cold glass (28.42); or concrete mixer lorries (29.20). Additionally, it excludes machines for cleaning/grading agricultural crops (except seeds/grains) (28.30) and paper/paperboard cards for jacquard machines (17.25).

description: Manufacture of motor vehicles, trailers and semi-trailers
detailled_description:
This division encompasses the industrial manufacture of motor vehicles for the transport of passengers and freight, alongside the production of specialized bodies, trailers, semi-trailers, and essential parts and accessories for motor vehicles. It covers the entire value chain from the assembly of complete vehicles and propulsion systems to the fabrication of individual mechanical, electrical, and structural components.

This includes, among others:
*   **Motor Vehicles:** The industrial manufacture of passenger cars, commercial vehicles (vans, lorries, road tractors), public transport vehicles (buses, coaches, trolleybuses), and specialized transport such as all-terrain vehicles, snowmobiles, golf carts, and racing cars, as well as the production of engines, including electric motors and factory engine rebuilding (291).
*   **Bodies, Trailers, and Semi-trailers:** The fabrication of vehicle bodies, cabs, and specialized superstructures such as fire engines, armoured vehicles, and concrete mixer lorries, as well as the production of trailers, semi-trailers, caravans, and specialized containers for multi-modal transport (292).
*   **Parts and Accessories:** The manufacture of electrical and electronic components (e.g., starters, alternators, spark plugs, ignition wiring, instrument panels, and inverters) (2931), and mechanical or body-related parts such as gearboxes, brakes, axles, road wheels, bumpers, safety systems (seat belts, airbags), seating (including child seats), and vehicle air-conditioning systems (2932).

This does not include the manufacture of motor vehicle batteries (27.20), lighting equipment (27.40), tyres (22.11), or rubber hoses and belts (22.12). It also excludes the manufacture of agricultural or forestry tractors (28.30), works trucks fitted with cranes (28.22), off-road dumper trucks (28.92), tanks and military fighting vehicles (30.40), or animal-drawn vehicles (30.99). Furthermore, this division excludes the production of specific components like pumps for engines (28.13) and pistons/carburettors not intended for motor vehicles (28.11), as well as the repair and maintenance of motor vehicles (95.31).

details.includes:
This division includes the manufacture of motor vehicles for transporting passengers or freight. The manufacture of various parts and accessories, as well as the manufacture of trailers and semi-trailers, is included here.

The repair and maintenance of motor vehicles produced in this division are classified in 95.31.

detailled_description:
This category encompasses the industrial manufacture of various types of motor vehicles, including those powered by electric, combustion, and hybrid engines, as well as autonomous systems. It covers the entire production process from basic chassis assembly to the manufacturing of complete vehicles and their propulsion systems.

This category includes the manufacture of passenger cars (29.10), commercial vehicles such as vans, lorries, and road tractors for semi-trailers (29.10), and public transport vehicles like buses, trolleybuses, and coaches (29.10). Furthermore, it covers the production of motor vehicle engines, including electric motors (29.10), and specialized transport such as snowmobiles, golf carts, amphibious motor vehicles, and road sweeper trollies (29.10). The scope also extends to the production of all-terrain vehicles (ATVs), go-carts, racing cars (29.10), as well as the factory rebuilding of motor vehicle engines and the manufacture of chassis fitted with engines (29.10).

This does not include the manufacture of lamps for motor vehicles (27.40); pistons, piston rings, and carburettors not intended for motor vehicles or motorcycles (28.11); works trucks fitted with a crane (28.22); agricultural, forestry, or track-laying tractors (28.30); or off-road dumper trucks (28.92). It also excludes the manufacture of specialized bodies for motor vehicles (e.g., fire engines, concrete mixers, or armoured vehicles) (29.20); electrical parts for motor vehicles (29.31); general parts and accessories for motor vehicles (29.32); tanks and other military fighting vehicles (30.40); or the repair and maintenance of motor vehicles (95.31).

description: Manufacture of bodies and coachwork for motor vehicles; manufacture of trailers and semi-trailers
detailled_description:
This category encompasses the manufacture of specialized structures and superstructures for motor vehicles, as well as the production of towed transport equipment. It includes the fabrication of bodies, coachwork, and chassis for various transport purposes, along with the outfitting, reconditioning, and customisation of motor vehicles and trailers.

This category includes, among others:
*   **Bodies and Coachwork:** The manufacture of vehicle bodies and cabs, including specialized vehicles such as fire engines, armoured vehicles, travelling libraries, and concrete mixer lorries (2920).
*   **Trailers and Semi-Trailers:** The production of diverse trailers, semi-trailers, and their chassis, ranging from tankers and open or closed-body trailers to caravans (2920).
*   **Containers and Customisation:** The manufacturing of specialized containers designed for multi-modal transport, including those intended for fluid carriage, as well as the general outfitting and reconditioning of motor vehicles, trailers, and semi-trailers (2920).

This does not include the manufacture of trailers and semi-trailers specifically designed for agricultural use (28.30), the manufacture of parts and accessories of motor vehicle bodies (29.32), or the manufacture of animal-drawn vehicles (30.99).

description: Manufacture of motor vehicle parts and accessories
detailled_description:
This category encompasses the manufacture of a wide range of parts and accessories for motor vehicles, regardless of the materials used in their production. It covers both the electrical and electronic components necessary for vehicle functionality as well as mechanical parts, body accessories, and specialized interior fittings.

This includes, among others:

*   **Electrical and Electronic Equipment:** The manufacture of motor vehicle electrical components, including starter motors, generators, alternators, spark plugs, insulated ignition wiring, voltage regulators, and power window and door systems. It also includes the assembly of instrument panel gauges, the production of electromagnetic clutches, inverter modules, fuel cells, and specialized automotive cable and wiring sets (2931).
*   **Mechanical and Body Components:** The production of diverse mechanical parts such as gearboxes, clutches, brakes, axles, road wheels, and shock absorbers. Furthermore, it covers body-related accessories including bumpers, safety seat belts, airbags, and rear-view mirrors (2932).
*   **Interior and Climate Control Equipment:** The manufacture of vehicle seating, including specialized seats for infants and children, as well as the production of air-conditioning systems for motor vehicles (2932).

This category does not include the manufacture of batteries for vehicles (27.20), lighting equipment for motor vehicles (27.40), tyres (22.11), or rubber hoses and belts (22.12). It also excludes the manufacture of pumps for motor vehicles and engines (28.13), the production of pistons, piston rings, and carburettors not intended for motor vehicles (28.11), and the repair, maintenance, or alteration of motor vehicles (95.31).

detailled_description:
This division encompasses the industrial manufacturing, assembly, and factory-level overhaul of transport equipment not elsewhere classified, covering a broad spectrum of civilian, commercial, military, and personal transit machinery. It includes the production of vessels, railway rolling stock, aerospace vehicles, specialized armored combat units, and miscellaneous personal or hand-drawn transport devices.

This category includes, among others:

*   **Maritime and Floating Structures:** The construction, factory conversion, and assembly of civilian, commercial, and military ships, boats, and specialized floating structures such as drilling platforms, barges, and submarines (3011, 3012, 3013).
*   **Railway and Tramway Equipment:** The production of locomotives, self-propelled rail units, non-powered rolling stock, and specialized components such as bogies, wheels, and signalling or traffic control equipment for rail, water, and air transit (3020).
*   **Air and Spacecraft:** The manufacture, overhaul, and conversion of civilian and military aircraft, including airplanes, helicopters, gliders, spacecraft, satellites, launch vehicles, and unmanned aerial systems (drones), along with their engines and primary structural assemblies (3031, 3032).
*   **Military Fighting Vehicles:** The production and heavy rebuilding of combat-ready land transport, such as tanks and armored vehicles, including their specialized armored bodies, turrets, and drive mechanisms (3040).
*   **Personal and Miscellaneous Transport:** The manufacture of motorcycles, mopeds, and their engines (3091); bicycles (including those with auxiliary motors), carriages for disabled persons, and baby carriages (3092); and other human- or animal-powered vehicles like handcarts, sledges, and hearses (3099).

This does not include the manufacture of motor vehicles for the transport of persons or goods (covered under division 29); weapons and ammunition (25.30); navigational instruments (26.51); electrical lighting equipment (27.40); general-purpose engines and turbines (28.11); specialized repair and maintenance services (division 33); the manufacture of toys (32.40); or the rental and leasing of transport equipment (division 77).

detailled_description:
This category encompasses the industrial construction, assembly, and factory conversion of ships, boats, and various floating structures intended for commercial, military, or recreational purposes. It covers the full lifecycle of new production, from the manufacturing of hull sections to the installation of technical interiors.

This category includes the following logical clusters:

*   **Civilian and Commercial Vessels:** This includes the construction of commercial vessels such as passenger ships, ferries, cargo ships, tankers, and tugs, as well as specialized fishing and fish-processing vessels (3011). It also covers the construction of floating structures, including drilling platforms (floating or submersible), docks, pontoons, cofferdams, landing stages, buoys, tanks, barges, lighters, floating cranes, and non-recreational inflatable rafts (3011).
*   **Pleasure and Sporting Craft:** This includes the building of yachts, sailing boats (with or without auxiliary motors), motorboats, personal watercraft, recreation-type hovercraft, and small human-powered or rowing craft such as canoes, kayaks, and skiffs, as well as inflatable rafts for sport and recreation (3012).
*   **Military Ships and Vessels:** This includes the building of combat-ready vessels and floating structures, such as aircraft carriers, cruisers, destroyers, submarines, amphibious assault ships, landing crafts, and specialized military tugs (3013).
*   **Production and Conversion Activities:** In addition to primary construction, this includes the manufacture of submersible drones and the factory conversion of ships and vessels (3011, 3012, 3013).

This does not include the manufacture of specialized vessel components such as sails (13.96), ship propellers or iron/steel anchors (25.99), weapons and ammunition (25.30), marine engines (28.11), navigational instruments (26.51), or lighting equipment (27.40). Furthermore, it excludes the factory overhaul of engines (28.11), the manufacture of sailboards and surfboards (32.30), the manufacture of amphibious motor vehicles (29.10, 30.40), specialized repair and maintenance services (33.15), ship-breaking (38.21), non-technical interior finishing (43.3), and the rental or leasing of vessels (50.10, 50.30, 77.21).

description: Manufacture of railway locomotives and rolling stock
detailled_description:
This category encompasses the industrial production of railway and tramway transport equipment, including both self-propelled units and non-powered rolling stock. It further extends to the manufacture of specialized railway components, mining transport equipment, and associated traffic control and safety systems.

This category includes, among others:
*   **Locomotives and Self-Propelled Units:** The production of electric, diesel, steam, and other rail locomotives, as well as self-propelled railway or tramway coaches, vans, and trucks (3020).
*   **Rolling Stock:** The manufacture of non-self-propelled railway and tramway vehicles, including passenger coaches, goods vans, tank wagons, self-discharging wagons, workshop and crane vans, and tenders (3020).
*   **Specialized Components:** The production of dedicated parts for locomotives and rolling stock, such as bogies, axles, wheels, braking systems, coupling devices, buffers, shock absorbers, and structural elements like frames, bodies, and corridor connections (3020).
*   **Additional Equipment and Infrastructure Support:** The manufacture of mining locomotives and mine carts, railway car seats, and mechanical or electromechanical signalling, safety, and traffic control equipment for various transit modes including railways, tramways, inland waterways, roads, and airfields (3020).

This does not include the manufacture of unassembled rails (24.10), assembled railway or tramway track fixtures and fittings (25.99), electric motors not for motor vehicles (27.11), electrical signalling, safety or traffic-control equipment for railways or tramways (27.90), or engines and turbines, including railway engines (28.11).

description: Manufacture of air and spacecraft and related machinery
detailled_description:
This category encompasses the manufacturing, overhaul, and conversion of both civilian and military air and spacecraft, including associated machinery and specialized components. It covers the production of various flying vehicles, ranging from transport aircraft and spacecraft to unmanned aerial systems.

This category includes, among others:

*   **Air and Space Vehicles:** The manufacture of fixed-wing aircraft (airplanes for transport, recreation, and sports), helicopters, tiltrotor aircraft, gliders, hang-gliders, dirigibles, and hot-air balloons (3031, 3032). This also includes the production of spacecraft, launch vehicles, satellites, planetary probes, orbital stations, and shuttles (3031).
*   **Unmanned Aerial Systems:** The manufacture of both civilian drones (3031) and military unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) (3032).
*   **Engines and Specialized Components:** The production of civilian aircraft engines, including turbojets and turboprops, and parts suitable for civilian aircraft internal combustion engines (3031). It also encompasses major assemblies such as fuselages, wings, control surfaces, landing gear, fuel tanks, nacelles, airscrews, helicopter rotors, and rotor blades (3031).
*   **Support and Ground Equipment:** The manufacture of ground flying trainers (3031), aircraft seats (3031, 3032), and the factory overhaul and rebuilding of air and spacecraft and their engines (3031, 3032).

This category does not include the manufacture of parachutes (13.96); weapons, ammunition, or military missiles (25.30); telecommunication equipment for satellites, aircraft instrumentation, or air navigation systems (26.51); lighting equipment for aircraft (27.40); ignition parts or specific engine components like pistons and carburettors (28.11, 29.31); aircraft launching gear or carrier catapults (28.99); toy drones (32.40); or the repair and maintenance services of civilian or military air and spacecraft (33.16, 33.18).

This category encompasses the industrial production, factory-level overhaul, and rebuilding of specialized military fighting vehicles. It focuses on the manufacturing processes for combat-ready land transport and armored units, including their essential specialized structural components.

This category includes the manufacture of tanks and various types of armored combat vehicles, such as those designed for transporting personnel, supply logistics, and recovery operations equipped with cranes (3040). It also covers specialized armored amphibious military vehicles and remotely operated tanks (3040). Furthermore, the scope extends to the production of essential sub-assemblies and parts, specifically armored vehicle bodies (including turrets, doors, and covers), specialized armored plates identifiable as components for military vehicles, and specialized drive mechanisms such as tracks, special wheels, and drive wheels designed for armored fighting vehicles (3040). Factory-level overhaul and complete rebuilding of these military fighting vehicles are also included (3040).

This category does not include the manufacture of weapons and ammunition (25.30); the manufacture of standard passenger cars or trucks that feature only light or removable armor (29.10); the manufacture of military ships (30.13); the manufacture of military drones (30.32); or the routine repair and maintenance of military fighting vehicles (33.18).

This category encompasses the manufacture of various types of transport equipment that are not classified as motor vehicles, rail transport, aircraft, spacecraft, or military vehicles. It primarily covers personal transport devices, specialized mobility aids, and a range of manually or animal-drawn vehicles.

This category includes the following clusters of activity:

*   **Motorcycles and Related Components:** This involves the production of motorcycles, mopeds, and their associated engines (Manufacture of motorcycles, 3091). It also encompasses the manufacturing of specialized parts and accessories for these vehicles, such as brakes, gearboxes, clutches, wheels, silencers, exhaust pipes, pistons, piston rings, and carburettors.
*   **Bicycles and Personal Mobility Equipment:** This covers the manufacturing of non-motorized bicycles and cycles, including tandems, tricycles, and children’s cycles, as well as bicycles equipped with auxiliary electric motors (Manufacture of bicycles and invalid carriages, 3092). This cluster also includes the production of carriages for disabled persons, personal transporters (such as electric skateboards and kickscooters), baby carriages, and their respective parts and accessories.
*   **Other Transport Equipment:** This includes the manufacture of various hand-propelled vehicles—such as luggage carts, handcarts, sledges, and shopping carts—as well as vehicles designed to be drawn by animals, including sulkies, donkey-carts, and hearses (Manufacture of other transport equipment n.e.c., 3099).

This does not include the manufacture of pneumatic rubber tyres and inner tubes for these vehicles (22.11); the manufacture of works trucks used in factories, such as industrial hand carts and wheelbarrows (28.22); the manufacture of decorative restaurant carts (31.00); or the manufacture of wheeled toys designed for riding, such as plastic bicycles or tricycles (32.40).

This division encompasses the manufacture of furniture for a wide variety of locations and purposes, utilizing standard methods of forming materials and assembling components such as cutting, moulding, and laminating. The scope includes the production of complete furniture units as well as individual furniture components designed for both aesthetic and functional qualities.

This category includes the following functional areas:

*   **Office, Commercial, and Institutional Furniture:** This includes seating for offices, workrooms, public premises, theatres, and cinemas (310). It covers specialized furniture for shops such as counters, display cases, and shelves, as well as office and laboratory-specific equipment including benches, cabinets, and tables (310).
*   **Domestic Furniture:** This includes furniture intended for living rooms, bedrooms, kitchens, and gardens, such as sofas, sofa beds, sofa sets, and specialized cabinets for appliances like televisions or sewing machines (310).
*   **Mattresses and Finishing:** The production of mattresses and mattress supports is included (310). Furthermore, it covers finishing processes for furniture—including upholstery, spraying, painting, and polishing—as well as the production of catering carts and walk-in wardrobes (310).

This does not include the manufacture of: pillows, pouffes, cushions, quilts, and eiderdowns (13.92); wooden mouldings not recognizable as furniture parts (16.1); builders’ carpentry and joinery (16.23); inflatable rubber or waterbed mattresses (22.12); or sheets or slabs of ceramics, concrete, or stone used as parts of furniture (23.42, 23.66, 23.70). Furthermore, it excludes light fittings or lamps (27.40), blackboards (28.23), vehicle seats for cars, railways, or aircraft (29.32, 30.20, 30.31, 30.32), and medical, surgical, dental, or veterinary furniture (32.50). Finally, it excludes the installation of modular furniture, partitions, or laboratory equipment at construction sites (43.32), as well as the professional reupholstering, refinishing, and repairing of furniture (95.24).

details.includes:
This division includes the manufacture of furniture and parts thereof, except of sheets and slabs of glass, stone, concrete or similar material as parts of furniture. The processes used in the manufacture of furniture are standard methods of forming materials and assembling components, including cutting, moulding and laminating. The design of the article, for both aesthetic and functional qualities, is an important aspect of the production process.

Some of the processes used in furniture manufacturing are similar to processes that are used in other segments of manufacturing (for example, cutting and assembly occurs in the production of wood trusses that are classified in division 16). However, the multiple processes distinguish wood furniture manufacturing from wood product manufacturing. Similarly, metal furniture manufacturing uses techniques that are also employed in the manufacture of roll-formed products classified in division 25. The moulding process for plastic furniture is similar to the moulding of other plastic products. However, the manufacture of plastic furniture tends to be a specialised activity.

detailled_description:
This division encompasses the manufacture of a wide variety of goods that are not covered in other parts of the industrial classification system. Due to its nature as a residual category, it covers diverse production processes and input materials, spanning high-precision medical technology, cultural and recreational equipment, and various specialized personal or household articles.

This includes, among others:

*   **Jewellery and Related Articles:** The manufacture of precious jewellery, goldsmiths’ and silversmiths’ articles, imitation jewellery, and the striking of coins (321).
*   **Musical Instruments:** The industrial production of acoustic, mechanical, and electronic musical instruments, including string, keyboard, wind, and percussion instruments, as well as specialized components and accessories (322).
*   **Sports Goods:** The manufacturing of athletic equipment, including gear for ball and racket games, winter and aquatic sports, fishing, hunting, and general gymnasium or fitness centre apparatus (323).
*   **Games and Toys:** The production of dolls, board games, puzzles, scale models, construction sets, wheeled toys for children, and equipment for gambling and funfairs (324).
*   **Medical and Dental Equipment:** The manufacture of surgical and dental instruments, prosthetic and orthopaedic devices, ophthalmic goods (such as corrective lenses and safety eyewear), and specialized medical or laboratory furniture and equipment (325).
*   **Miscellaneous Manufacturing:** The production of various specialized items such as cleaning tools (brooms and brushes), occupational safety gear (protective helmets, earplugs, and vests), office supplies (pens and pencils), umbrellas, lighters, candles, and burial coffins (329).

This does not include the manufacture of non-metallic watch bands (15.12); the production of sporting apparel (14.19/14.29) or footwear (15.20); the manufacture of electronic consumer audio equipment (26.40); the production of electromedical and electrotherapeutic apparatus and hearing aids (26.60); the manufacture of sports vehicles (divisions 29 and 30); the manufacture of video game consoles (26.40); or the repair and maintenance of the goods mentioned above (divisions 95).

details.includes: This division includes the manufacture of a variety of goods not covered in other parts of the classification. description: Manufacture of jewellery, bijouterie and related articles
detailled_description:
This category encompasses the manufacturing activities related to the production of coins, precious jewellery, and costume or imitation jewellery. It covers the transformation of precious metals and gemstones into finished articles, as well as the creation of decorative accessories using base metals and synthetic materials.

This includes, among others:

*   **Striking of coins:** The production of coinage, including legal tender, regardless of whether precious metals are used (3211).
*   **Manufacture of precious jewellery and goldsmiths’ articles:** The production of jewellery using precious metals or metals clad with precious metals, as well as those incorporating precious or semi-precious stones (including the working of diamonds and pearls). This also covers the manufacture of goldsmiths’ articles, such as dinnerware, hollowware, toilet, desk, and religious articles, alongside technical or laboratory items made of precious metal (e.g., crucibles, spatulas) and precious metal watch bands or cigarette cases (3212).
*   **Manufacture of imitation jewellery and accessories:** The production of costume or imitation jewellery that does not incorporate natural pearls or genuine gemstones, such as necklaces, rings, and earrings made from base metals. This group also includes the manufacture of non-precious metal watch bands (3213).

This does not include the manufacture of non-metallic watch bands (15.12); the production of base metals clad with precious metals that are not further worked (24.41); the manufacture of statuettes and ornaments made of base metal plated with precious metal (25.99); the manufacture of watch cases (26.52); or the repair of jewellery (95.25).

This category encompasses the industrial production of a wide range of acoustic, mechanical, and electronic musical instruments, as well as the manufacturing of dedicated components and musical accessories. It covers the craftsmanship and technical assembly of sound-generating equipment intended for musical performance and signaling.

The scope of this category includes the following functional clusters:

*   **String and Keyboard Instruments:** This comprises the manufacture of various string instruments, keyboard stringed instruments (including automatic pianos), pipe organs, harmoniums, and keyboard instruments featuring free metal reeds (3220).
*   **Wind and Percussion Instruments:** This includes the production of wind instruments, percussion instruments (such as drums, xylophones, cymbals, castanets, and maracas), and various mouth-blown sound-signalling instruments, such as whistles and call horns (3220).
*   **Electronic and Mechanical Instruments:** This covers the manufacture of instruments that generate sound electronically, such as digital pianos and synthesizers, as well as mechanical musical devices like musical boxes, fairground organs, and calliopes (3220).
*   **Accordions and Accessories:** This includes the production of accordions and similar instruments (e.g., mouth organs), as well as essential instrument parts and accessories, such as metronomes, tuning forks, pitch pipes, and specialized media for automatic mechanical instruments (3220).

This category does not include the manufacture of toy musical instruments (32.40); the manufacture of electronic consumer audio equipment such as microphones, amplifiers, loudspeakers, headphones, or record players (26.40); the reproduction or publishing of pre-recorded sound (18.20, 59.20); or the repair and maintenance of musical instruments, including piano tuning (95.29).

This category encompasses the manufacture of a wide variety of sporting and athletic equipment intended for professional or recreational use, regardless of the materials employed. It covers the production of specialized tools, apparatus, and gear used in indoor and outdoor sports, athletics, and various leisure games.

This category includes the manufacture of articles and equipment for sports, specifically:
*   **Ball and racket games:** Such as hard, soft, and inflatable balls, as well as rackets, bats, and clubs (3230).
*   **Winter and aquatic sports gear:** Including skis, bindings, and poles, ski/snowboard boots, sailboards, surfboards, and waterskis (3230).
*   **Sporting and field equipment:** Comprising requisites for sport fishing (including landing-nets), hunting or shooting requisites (such as decoy 'birds'), mountain climbing equipment, bows, and crossbows (3230).
*   **General athletic and gymnasium gear:** Including gymnasium and fitness centre equipment, weightlifting weights, ice and roller skates, and sports gloves made of leather or composition leather (3230).
*   **Recreational structures:** Such as basins for swimming and padding pools (3230).

This does not include the manufacture of boat sails (13.96), sports apparel (14.19/14.29), saddlery, harnesses, whips, or riding crops (15.12), or sports footwear (15.20). description: Manufacture of medical and dental instruments and supplies
detailled_description:
This category encompasses the manufacture of a wide range of medical, surgical, and dental instruments, specialized equipment, and supplies. It covers the production of laboratory apparatus, prosthetic devices, ophthalmic goods, and specialized furniture designed for medical and veterinary applications.

This category includes, among others, the manufacture of surgical and dental instruments, including needles, syringes, catheters, and cannulae (3250); dental supplies such as fillings, cements, artificial teeth, and orthodontic appliances (3250); and orthopaedic and prosthetic devices, including made-to-measure orthopaedic footwear and glass eyes (3250). It further includes the production of specialized medical and laboratory furniture—such as operating tables, hospital beds with mechanical fittings, and dentist chairs—as well as laboratory equipment like sterilizers, ultrasonic cleaning machinery, centrifuges, and furnaces (3250). Additionally, this category covers the production of ophthalmic goods, including prescription lenses, eyeglasses, and protective eyewear, as well as individual protective masks such as surgical, FFP2, and FFP3 respirators (3250).

This does not include the manufacture of series-produced orthopedic shoes (15.20), denture fixative pastes and powders (20.42), or medical dressings, wadding, gauze, and bandages (21.20). Furthermore, it excludes the manufacture of electromedical and electrotherapeutic apparatus and hearing aids (26.60), the manufacture of wheelchairs (30.92), and the retail sale of corrective glasses and lenses (47.74).

The primary objective of these activities is to restore capital assets to working order, ensure operational efficiency, and prevent mechanical failure through systematic servicing.

This includes, among others:

*   **Repair and Maintenance of Fabricated Metal Products and Industrial Machinery:** The restoration and servicing of tanks, pipelines, steam generators, and various industrial machinery, such as engines (non-automotive), pumps, compressors, machine tools, materials handling equipment, and agricultural or construction machinery (3311, 3312).
*   **Electronic, Optical, and Electrical Equipment Repair:** Technical services for measuring, testing, and navigational instruments, electromedical and electrotherapeutic apparatus, as well as electrical power infrastructure like transformers, motors, generators, and battery systems (3313, 3314).
*   **Transport Equipment Maintenance:** The repair and upkeep of civilian ships, aircraft, locomotives, railway rolling stock, vehicles for the disabled, and specialized military transport or fighting vehicles (3315, 3316, 3317, 3318).
*   **Specialized Installation Services:** The assembly, rigging, and dismantling of industrial machinery and equipment, including production process control systems, large-scale warehouse equipment, and specialized industrial apparatus (3320).
*   **Other Miscellaneous Repair:** The repair of diverse items such as fishing nets, ropes, wooden pallets, gaming machines, and hospital furniture (3319).

This division does not include the factory-level rebuilding or remanufacturing of machinery (classified under divisions 25 to 30), the cleaning of industrial machinery (81.22), or the installation of equipment that forms an integral part of buildings or structures, such as electrical wiring, escalators, or air-conditioning systems (classified under construction). Furthermore, it excludes the repair and maintenance of computers and communication equipment (95.10), household goods (95.2), and motor vehicles and motorcycles (95.3).

details.includes:
This division includes the specialised repair of goods produced in the manufacturing sector with the aim to restore machinery, equipment and other products to working order. The provision of general or routine maintenance (in other words, servicing) on such products to ensure they work efficiently and to prevent breakdown and unnecessary repairs is included. 

This division only includes specialised repair and maintenance activities. A substantial amount of repair is also done by manufacturers of machinery, equipment and other goods. In such cases, the units engaged in these repair and manufacturing activities are classified according to the value-added principle, which would often assign these combined activities to the manufacture of the good. The same principle is applied for combined trade and repair.

The rebuilding or remanufacture of machinery and equipment is considered a manufacturing activity and is included in other divisions of this section.
details.alsoIcludes: Also included in this division is the specialised installation of machinery.

description: Repair and maintenance of fabricated metal products, machinery and equipment

*   **Machinery and Equipment:** The maintenance of industrial and commercial machinery, including engines (non-automotive), pumps, compressors, machine tools, materials handling equipment, construction and mining machinery, agricultural equipment, and office machinery like photocopiers and vending machines (3312).
*   **Electronic, Optical, and Electrical Equipment:** The repair of measuring, testing, navigating, and control instruments; electromedical and electrotherapeutic apparatus; optical equipment; and electrical power infrastructure such as transformers, motors, generators, switchgear, and battery systems (3313, 3314).
*   **Transport Equipment:** The maintenance of civilian ships and boats, civilian aircraft and spacecraft, locomotives, railway cars, vehicles for the disabled, and specialized military fighting vehicles, ships, and aircraft (3315, 3316, 3317, 3318).

description: Installation of industrial machinery and equipment
detailled_description:
This category encompasses the specialized installation of industrial machinery, equipment, and related systems designed for production or operational processes. It covers the assembly, installation, and dismantling of complex equipment, as well as the specialized services of millwrights and machinery riggers.

The scope of this category includes the following areas:

*   **Industrial and Process Equipment:** The installation of machinery in industrial plants, the setup of industrial process control equipment, and the installation of specialized equipment such as irradiation and electromedical devices (3320).
*   **Infrastructure and Specialized Installations:** The installation of large-scale warehouse machinery, warehouse shelving (provided it is not an integral part of the building), communication equipment, mainframe computers, and other stand-alone industrial equipment such as bowling alley equipment and stand-alone charging facilities (3320).
*   **Support Services:** Activities related to the professional assembly, rigging, and dismantling of large-scale machinery and industrial plants (3320).

This category does not include the installation of equipment that forms an integral part of buildings or structures, such as elevators, escalators, automated doors, vacuum cleaning systems, electrical wiring, or air-conditioning systems (classified under construction). Furthermore, it excludes the construction of complete warehouses, the installation of doors, staircases, shopfittings, furniture, or the erection of structural steel for warehouse shelves. Also excluded are the installation of wall-box charging facilities and the setup of personal computers.

description: Electricity, gas, steam and air conditioning supply
detailled_description:
This category encompasses the provision of utility services related to the production, transmission, distribution, and commercial trade of energy in the form of electricity, gas, steam, and cooled air. It covers the management of infrastructure necessary for the supply of these essential services to residential, commercial, and industrial end-users.

This includes, among others:

*   **Electric Power:** The generation of electricity from both non-renewable (fossil fuel, nuclear) and renewable sources (hydro, wind, solar, etc.), as well as its transmission, distribution, storage, and commercial sale through grids (351).
*   **Gaseous Fuels:** The manufacture of synthetic gases, the processing of biogas, the regasification of natural gas for mains distribution, and the storage and trading of gaseous fuels via a network of mains (352).
*   **Thermal Energy and Climate Control:** The production, collection, and distribution of steam and hot water for heating or industrial purposes, as well as the provision of chilled water and air for air conditioning and cooling systems (353).
*   **Intermediation Services:** The activities of brokers and agents who arrange the sale or distribution of electricity and natural gas through utility systems operated by third parties (354).

This does not include the extraction of crude natural gas (06.20); the production of coke oven gas, refined petroleum products, or basic industrial gases not intended for network supply (19.10, 19.20, 20.11, 20.14); the manufacturing of edible ice (10.52); the transport of gas through long-distance pipelines (49.50); the wholesale or retail of bottled gas (46.81, 47.30); or the production of energy derived from the incineration of waste (38.22).

description: Electric power generation, transmission and distribution
detailled_description:
This category encompasses the complete value chain of the electric power sector, covering the generation, transmission, storage, and distribution of electricity, as well as its commercial trade. It includes the operation of diverse facilities and infrastructure required to deliver electrical energy from the point of production to end users.

This includes, among others:
*   **Electricity Generation:** The operation of generation facilities utilizing non-renewable sources such as coal, natural gas, and nuclear energy (3511), as well as renewable sources including hydropower, wind, solar (photovoltaic and thermal), geothermal, and ocean energy (3512).
*   **Transmission and Distribution:** The operation of high-voltage systems for the bulk transmission of electricity from generation sites to distribution grids (3513), and the operation of distribution networks—including lines, meters, and associated infrastructure—to deliver power to final consumers, as well as the rental and leasing of such networks (3514).
*   **Trade and Infrastructure:** The sale of electricity on own account and the operation of charging facilities for electric vehicles and electronic devices (3515).
*   **Storage:** The conversion of electrical energy into a storable form, the maintenance of such storage facilities (e.g., pump storage, compressed air, or battery storage), and the subsequent reconversion and injection of this power back into the mains (3516).

This does not include the separate production and distribution of steam and heat (35.3), activities of electric power brokers or agents acting on behalf of others (35.40), the pretreatment of waste for energy recovery (38.22), or the production of electricity not associated with storage activities.

description: Manufacture of gas, and distribution of gaseous fuels through mains
detailled_description:
This category encompasses the production of gaseous fuels, the management of gas storage facilities within network supply systems, and the distribution and trading of gaseous fuels to end-users through a system of mains. It covers the entire value chain of gaseous energy supply, from manufacturing processes and purification to the physical distribution and commercial sale via gas utility networks.

This category includes, among others:
*   **Manufacture and Production:** The production of gaseous fuels for energy supply through distribution networks, including the carbonation of coal, gasification of lignite, electrolysis, methanisation, and the production or cleansing of biogas (from sewage, manure, or waste) and gaseous biofuels. It also includes the production of specific calorific value gases via blending and purification, and the regasification of natural gas for mains distribution (3521).
*   **Distribution and Trading:** The transport, distribution, and supply of all kinds of gaseous fuels through a system of mains, as well as the rental and leasing of gas utility networks (3522). This also includes the sale of gaseous fuels through mains on one's own account (3523).
*   **Storage:** The storage of gaseous fuels, including hydrogen gas, specifically when performed as part of network energy supply services (3524).

This does not include the extraction of crude natural gas (06.20); the production of coke oven gas (19.10), refined petroleum products (19.20), industrial or basic organic gases not for network supply (20.11, 20.14), or blast furnace gas (24.10); the sale of gas on behalf of others (35.40); the transport of gas over long distances through pipelines (49.50); the wholesale of bottled gaseous fuels (46.81); the retail sale of bottled gas or motor fuels (47.30, 47.78); or storage activities that are not part of network energy supply services (52.10).

*   **Steam and Hot Water Services:** The production, collection, and distribution of steam and hot water for heating, industrial power, and other utility purposes (3530).

description: Activities of brokers and agents for electric power and natural gas
detailled_description:
This category encompasses the specialized intermediary services provided by brokers and agents who facilitate the commercial transaction and distribution rights of electric power and natural gas. These activities focus on the arrangement of sales and capacity trading rather than the physical production or direct operation of utility distribution systems.

This category includes the activities of brokers and agents who arrange the sale of electricity and gaseous fuels through distribution systems operated by third parties (3540). It also covers the services of brokers and agents involved in commodity and distribution capacity exchanges for gaseous fuels, as well as those managing electricity distribution and transmission capacity exchanges (3540).

This section includes activities related to the management, collection, pretreatment, recovery and disposal, of various forms of waste (for example, solid or non-solid industrial or household waste) and its organisation.

The output of the waste or sewage treatment process can either be disposed of or become an input into other production processes. Secondary raw materials are materials and products which can be used as raw materials by simple reuse, or via recycling and recovery of waste. Activities of water supply are also grouped in this section, since they are often carried out in connection with, or by units also engaged in, the treatment of sewage.

The activities also include remediation of contaminated buildings and sites, soil, surface and groundwater (for example, oceans, mangroves, seas), and so on.

Units that usually take over their clients’ waste procedures and become the customer of the waste hauler, and then in turn charge their clients for waste services, are classified in division 38. Even if these units do not render the corresponding services themselves, they are responsible for their fulfilment. This activity is regarded as the complete outsourcing of a service.

- waste trade activities as wholesalers, see 46.87
