description: Retail sale of cultural and recreational goods
detailled_description:
This category encompasses the specialized retail sale of cultural, recreational, and sporting goods intended for leisure, education, and creative activities. It covers a broad spectrum of consumer products, ranging from literature and office supplies to athletic gear, musical instruments, and collectible items.

This group includes, among others:

*   **Literature and Stationery:** The retail sale of books, including audiobooks on physical media (47.61), as well as newspapers, periodicals, journals, and a comprehensive range of office and school stationery supplies (47.62).
*   **Sporting and Camping Equipment:** The retail sale of sports goods, including fishing gear, weapons and ammunition, and camping equipment such as tents and sleeping bags (47.63). This cluster also covers specialized sports transport, such as boats, bicycles (including electric models, monowheels, and kickscooters), and specialized athletic apparel and footwear, such as ski boots or ballet attire (47.63).
*   **Games, Toys, and Party Supplies:** The retail sale of toys and games made of all materials, including toy drones and various party favors, such as masks and magic items (47.64).
*   **Cultural, Musical, and Specialized Goods:** The retail sale of recorded media (excluding video games), musical instruments and their accessories (e.g., scores, metronomes), and art supplies, such as paints, canvases, and clay (47.69). Additionally, this includes the retail sale of philatelic and numismatic items and the commercial activities of art galleries (47.69).

This does not include the retail sale of antique or second-hand goods (books, games, toys, recorded media, or musical instruments), which are classified under 47.79. It also excludes the retail sale of non-specialized sports footwear (47.72), video game consoles and games on physical media (47.40), souvenirs, craftwork, or religious articles (47.78). Finally, this category excludes the digital distribution (streaming or downloading) of books, newspapers, periodicals, audio, or video games, as well as the publishing or content-sharing platform activities related to these media.

description: Retail sale of other goods, except motor vehicles and motorcycles
detailled_description:
This category encompasses the specialised retail sale of a diverse range of new and second-hand goods that are not classified elsewhere. It covers a broad spectrum of consumer products, including personal items, health-related goods, household maintenance products, and specialized ornamental or practical articles.

This includes, among others:
*   **Apparel and Personal Accessories:** Retail sale of clothing, including underwear, furs, work clothes, uniforms, costumes, and clothing accessories (4771); footwear and leather goods, including travel accessories made of leather or substitutes (4772); as well as watches, jewellery, and silverware (4777).
*   **Health and Pharmaceutical Goods:** Retail sale of pharmaceutical and veterinary medicines, including homeopathic and herbal remedies (4773); as well as medical and orthopaedic supplies, such as corrective spectacles, lenses, hearing aids, wheelchairs, crutches, prostheses, and elastic compression products (4774).
*   **Cosmetic and Personal Care:** Retail sale of perfumes, cosmetics, and various toiletries (4775).
*   **Flora, Fauna, and Pet Supplies:** Retail sale of flowers, plants, fertilisers, pet animals, and pet food, as well as hygiene and grooming products for domestic animals (4776).
*   **Miscellaneous New Goods:** Retail sale of photographic, optical, and precision equipment; cleaning products; household fuels (such as heating oil, bottled gas, and coal); packaging materials; funeral and cemetery articles; souvenirs, craftwork, religious items, and imitation jewellery (4778).
*   **Second-hand Goods:** Retail sale of various second-hand items, including clothing, books, antiques, furniture, and household appliances (4779).

This does not include the retail sale of textiles (47.51); special sports equipment and clothing (47.63); protective gear for motorcyclists (47.83); motor vehicles, motorcycles, and their parts (47.8); retail auctioneering and online auctions (47.9); or the activities of pawnshops (64.92).

description: Retail sale of motor vehicles, motorcycles and related parts and accessories
detailled_description:
This category encompasses the retail trade of motor vehicles, motorcycles, and their associated components, covering both new and second-hand items. It spans the distribution of transportation units as well as the specialized supply chain for maintenance-related parts and equipment.

This category includes the following logical clusters:

*   **Motor Vehicles and Motorcycles:** This covers the retail sale of passenger motor vehicles, camping vehicles (such as caravans and motorhomes), and off-road motor vehicles (4781). It also includes the sale of motorcycles and mopeds (4783).
*   **Parts, Accessories, and Equipment:** This encompasses the retail sale of all types of new and used parts, components, and equipment for motor vehicles (4782) and motorcycles (4783). Specific inclusions are rubber tyres and inner tubes, spark plugs, batteries, lighting equipment, vehicle charging equipment, electrical parts, and protective gear for motorcyclists. description: Intermediation service activities for retail sale
detailled_description:
This category comprises intermediation service activities for both specialised and non-specialised retail sale that facilitate transactions between buyers and sellers of physical goods for a fee or commission. These activities involve connecting parties without the intermediary taking legal ownership of the goods, and may be conducted via digital platforms or traditional channels such as face-to-face, door-to-door, telephone, or mail.

This includes, among others:
*   **Non-specialised Retail Intermediation:** Facilitation of transactions for the ordering and delivery of a broad range of goods, as well as space rental (including staff) for the retail sale of second-hand goods (4791).
*   **Specialised Retail Intermediation:** Facilitation of transactions for the ordering and delivery of specific types of goods or categories of merchandise (4792).
*   **Supportive Commercial Activities:** The provision of intermediation services for the retail sale of second-hand goods, the operation of retail auctioneering houses (including internet-based platforms) for both new and used third-party goods, and the activities of agents specifically engaged in the retail sale of motor vehicles and motorcycles.

This does not include:
*   The retail sale of petrol in combination with electro fuels (e-fuels), where the sale of electro fuels is not the predominant activity (classified under 47.30).
*   Intermediation service activities between the specific categories of 4791 and 4792, as each class excludes the activities of the other.

*   **Passenger Rail and Road Transport:** The provision of passenger services via mainline, regional, and urban rail systems, including subways, trams, and funiculars (491); as well as scheduled and non-scheduled road transport via bus, coach, and taxi, alongside cableway and lift operations (493).

This division encompasses the water transport of passengers and freight, whether scheduled or unscheduled, conducted for professional, personal, or recreational purposes across all types of waterways. The scope of activities is categorized primarily by the type of vessel used, distinguishing between seagoing and coastal vessels and those designed specifically for inland navigation.

This includes, among others:
* **Passenger Transport Services:** The operation of vessels for passenger travel, including scheduled and non-scheduled services, water taxis, and ferries—both for sea/coastal routes (501) and inland waterways (503). This also covers excursion, cruise, and sightseeing boat operations (501, 503).
* **Freight Transport Services:** The transport of goods via water, encompassing sea and coastal freight (502) as well as inland freight transport on rivers, canals, and lakes (504).
* **Operational and Support Activities:** The operation of towing or pushing services for barges, oil rigs, and other floating structures, as well as the provision of vessel rental services with crew for both passenger and freight transport (501, 502, 503, 504).

This does not include restaurant and bar activities performed by separate business units aboard ships (56.11, 56.30); harbor operations and auxiliary services such as docking, pilotage, lighterage, or vessel salvage (52.22); cargo handling and storage (52.10, 52.24); the rental of pleasure boats, yachts, or commercial vessels without a crew (77.21, 77.34); or the operation of stationary floating casinos (92.00).

* **Passenger Air Transport:** The operation of air transport for passengers on established, regular routes (scheduled) or through specialized charter and sightseeing flights (511). This also includes the rental of air transport equipment with an operator for passenger transport purposes (511).
* **Freight Air Transport:** The transport of freight by air, whether conducted on a scheduled or non-scheduled basis, including the rental of air transport equipment with an operator for freight services (512).
* **Space Transport:** The execution of space transport activities, such as the launching of satellites and space vehicles, and the transport of freight or passengers into space (512).

This division does not include:
* Agricultural support activities such as crop spraying (01.61).
* Repair and maintenance of civilian aircraft or aircraft engines (33.16).
* The operation of airports (52.23).
* Specialized aerial services including advertising (73.11), photography (74.20), and civil or military aerial surveillance (80.09, 84.22).
* The rental of air transport equipment without an operator (77.35).
* The provision of air ambulance services (86.92).

description: Warehousing, storage and support activities for transportation
detailled_description:
This division encompasses the operation of warehousing and storage facilities, as well as the provision of critical support services and intermediation activities for the transport of passengers and freight. It covers the management of physical infrastructure, cargo handling, logistics support, and the brokerage services required to facilitate transportation across land, water, and air networks.

This includes, among others:

*   **Warehousing and Storage:** The operation of general and specialized warehousing facilities, including refrigerated stores, grain silos, storage tanks, and the storage of physical archives and paper files (521).
*   **Support for Transportation Infrastructure:** The operation of transport terminals and infrastructure, such as road, rail, and water transport facilities (bridges, tunnels, stations, harbours, piers, and waterway locks), as well as air traffic control and airport ground services (522).
*   **Cargo Handling and Logistics:** Physical cargo handling, including stevedoring and loading/unloading services across all transport modes, along with freight forwarding, customs agency activities, weighing, sampling, and crating (522).
*   **Transport Intermediation:** Professional brokerage and matchmaking services for both freight and passenger transportation, including the operation of digital transport platforms, freight brokerage, and booking or reservation services for passenger travel (523).

This division does not include the storage of electricity or gaseous fuels (35.16, 35.24), the construction or repair of transport infrastructure (42), courier activities (53.20), the operation of parking facilities for vehicles or aircraft (52.21, 52.22, 52.23), the rental of vacant storage space or self-storage (68.20), transport insurance (65.12), transport consultancy (70.20), or the services of travel agencies and tour operators (79.1). Furthermore, it excludes the actual operation of freight or passenger transport services (49, 50, 51).

details.includes:
This division includes warehousing and support activities for transport, such as the operation of transport infrastructure (for example, airports, harbours, tunnels, bridges). It also includes the activities of transport agencies and cargo handling.

The activities mentioned are carried out on behalf of third parties. If the related services are provided solely to support transport activities by the same unit, they are considered as ancillary activities to transport and this unit is classified elsewhere in section H.

This does not include the storage of electricity (35.16), the storage of gaseous fuels for energy supply through a network (35.24), or the storage of furniture as an integrated component of a removal service (49.42). This category encompasses a wide range of services designed to support the transport of passengers, animals, or freight. It covers the operation of transport infrastructure and terminal facilities, physical cargo handling, logistics management, and various specialized activities essential to the efficiency and safety of transportation across all modes.

This includes, among others:
*   **Support for Land Transportation (52.21):** The operation of road, rail, and terminal infrastructure, including bridges, tunnels, railway stations, bus stations, and cargo terminals. This cluster also covers car parking facilities, winter road maintenance, toll collection, towing services, and roadside assistance, as well as the liquefaction/regasification of natural gas for land transport.
*   **Support for Water Transportation (52.22):** Infrastructure and navigation services, such as harbours, piers, waterway locks, pilotage, tug and berthing services, lighthouses, salvage activities, and winter storage for vessels. It also includes waterway information services and the processing of natural gas for water transport.
*   **Support for Air Transportation (52.23):** Services related to airfield operations, including air traffic control, terminal facilities, ground handling, aircraft storage, and airport fire-prevention and safety services.
*   **Cargo Handling (52.24):** The physical loading and unloading of goods and luggage (stevedoring) across all transport modes, including specialized industrial site cargo movement and the rental/leasing of loading equipment with operators.
*   **Logistics and Freight Support (52.25 & 52.26):** Activities related to supply chain operations, including distribution centres, goods grouping, crating, weighing, and sampling. It also covers the organization of intermodal transport, freight forwarding, customs agency activities, and the procurement of transport documentation.

This does not include: intermediation service activities for freight transport (52.31); intermediation service activities for passenger transport (52.32); construction or repair of transport infrastructure (division 42); courier activities (53.20); provision of transport insurance (65.12); logistics management or planning consultancy (70.20); or the operation of travel agencies and tour operators (79.1).

This category encompasses professional intermediation services that facilitate the movement of freight and passengers by connecting clients with transport service providers. These activities are conducted for a fee or commission, through either digital platforms or traditional channels, without the intermediary itself providing the underlying transportation services.

This category includes the following functional areas:

*   **Freight Transportation Intermediation:** This encompasses brokerage services for rail, road, ship, and aircraft freight, as well as the operation of digital platforms dedicated to freight transport matchmaking (5231).
*   **Passenger Transportation Intermediation:** This includes the operation of online ride-sharing platforms, the provision of booking and reservation services for land, water, or air passenger travel, brokerage of seats in ships or aircraft, and intermediation for radio taxi services (5232).

This category does not include the actual operation of freight or passenger transport services (divisions 49, 50, and 51), nor does it include taxi operations (49.3), vehicle rental platforms without a driver (77.51), or travel agency and tour operator activities involving travel advice or combined travel/accommodation packages (79.11, 79.12).

details.includes:
This class includes the intermediation of freight transport, by bringing clients and service providers together for a fee or commission, without the intermediary providing the freight transport services that are intermediated. These intermediation activities can be carried out on digital platforms or through non-digital channels (including face-to-face, door-to-door, telephone, mail, and so on). The fee or commission can be received from either the client or the provider of the freight transport service. Revenue for the intermediation activities can include other sources of income (for example, revenues from the sale of advertising space).

This category encompasses the comprehensive range of postal, courier, and intermediation service activities involved in the collection, sorting, transport, and delivery of letters, documents, parcels, and other goods. It covers both universal postal service providers and commercial courier operators, as well as third-party intermediation services that facilitate these delivery processes.

This includes, among others:
* **Postal and Universal Services:** The handling of letters, postcards, and printed materials, as well as the collection and delivery of mail and parcels conducted by providers operating under a universal service obligation (531).
* **Courier and Delivery Services:** The domestic and international pickup, sorting, transport, and delivery of mail, parcels, and packages, including dedicated home delivery services for goods and food items, conducted by businesses outside the universal service scope (532).
* **Intermediation Services:** Third-party activities, including digital platforms and booking services, that connect customers with postal and courier service providers for a fee or commission, without performing the actual delivery (533).

This does not include:
* The transport of freight (classified under 49.20, 49.41, 50.20, 50.40, 51.21, 51.22).
* The delivery of furniture involving specialized services such as unpacking or installation (49.41).
* Financial services such as postal giro, postal savings, or money order activities (64.19).
* The home delivery of prepared meals when performed by the same business unit that prepares the meals (division 56).

description: Postal activities under universal service obligation
detailled_description:
This category encompasses the collection, sorting, transport, and delivery activities conducted by postal service providers operating under a universal service obligation. It covers the maintenance and utilization of the essential universal service infrastructure, including retail post offices, processing facilities, and established carrier routes for both domestic and international mail.

This includes, among others:
*   **Postal Operations:** The comprehensive handling of letter post, which comprises letters, postcards, and printed materials such as newspapers, periodicals, and advertising items (5310).
*   **Parcel and Document Delivery:** The processing and distribution of small packets, parcels, and various documents, utilizing either private or public transport modes (5310).
*   **Collection and Infrastructure Services:** The collection of mail and parcels from public letter boxes or retail locations, as well as other supporting services necessary to fulfill the universal service obligation (5310).

This does not include postal giro, postal savings activities, or money order activities (64.19).

description: Postal activities under universal service obligation

details.includes:
This class includes the activities of postal services operating under a universal service obligation by one or more designated universal service providers. The activities include use of the universal service infrastructure, including retail sale locations, sorting and processing facilities, and carrier routes to pick up and deliver mail. The delivery can include letter post, in other words, letters, postcards, printed papers (newspapers, periodicals, advertising items, and so on), small packets, goods or documents. Also included are other services necessary to support the universal service obligation.

This class includes:
- pickup, sorting, transport and delivery (domestic (national) or international) of letter post and (mail-type) parcels and packages by postal services operating under a universal service obligation. One or more modes of transport may be involved and the activity may be carried out with either self-owned (private) transport or via public transport.
- collection of letter-mail and parcels from public letter boxes or from post offices
details.excludes:
This class excludes:

It covers the end-to-end management of mail and package delivery, including pickup, sorting, transport, and delivery operations through various modes of transport.

This includes, among others:
*   **Postal and Courier Operations:** The domestic and international pickup, sorting, transport, and delivery of letter post, parcels, and packages, utilizing either private or public transport networks (5320).
*   **Home Delivery Services:** Dedicated delivery services for goods, including the home delivery of food items (5320).

This does not include the transport of freight (classified under 49.20, 49.41, 50.20, 50.40, 51.21, 51.22), the delivery of furniture involving specialized services such as unpacking or installation (49.41), or the home delivery of prepared meals when performed by the same business unit that prepares the meals (division 56).

description: Intermediation service activities for postal and courier activities
detailled_description:

These activities facilitate the matching of business or household customers with service providers through various channels, including digital platforms or traditional methods such as telephone, mail, or face-to-face contact.

This category includes, among others, the following activities:
*   **Postal and Courier Intermediation:** Third-party intermediation services for postal and courier providers, offered to both business and domestic clients (5330).

detailled_description:
This division encompasses the provision of short-term accommodation for visitors, travelers, and other transient populations, such as students or workers, often including associated services like meals, cleaning, and recreational facilities. It covers the entire spectrum of lodging, from professional hospitality operations and self-contained vacation rentals to outdoor camping environments and specialized residential-style facilities, as well as the intermediation services that facilitate these bookings.

This includes, among others:
* **Hotels and Professional Hospitality:** The provision of lodging with on-the-spot customer services, such as daily housekeeping, bed-making, and hospitality amenities in hotels, resort hotels, and suite or apartment hotels (551).
* **Holiday and Self-Catering Accommodation:** Lodging in furnished units intended for short-term stays, including holiday homes, visitor flats, bungalows, cottages, cabins, hostels, bed and breakfast units, and mountain huts, typically without daily housekeeping (552).
* **Camping and Outdoor Stays:** Short-term accommodation for guests using tents, recreational vehicles, or mobile lodging, including camping grounds, recreational, fishing and hunting camps, glamping, and basic shelters or bivouacs (553).
* **Other Specialized Accommodation:** Temporary housing solutions for specific groups, such as dormitories for students or seasonal workers, boarding houses, and the operation of railway sleeping cars when managed by third-party entities (559).
* **Intermediation and Reservation Services:** Activities involving the facilitation of accommodation bookings between clients and providers for a fee or commission, including digital platform operations, reservation services, and timeshare exchanges (554).

This does not include the provision of residences, such as flats or apartments, that are typically leased on an annual basis (68.20). It also excludes the operation of railway sleeping cars when integrated as part of railway company services (49.11), the operation of cruise ships (50.10, 50.30), and the activities of travel agencies or tour operators that bundle accommodation with travel and catering services (79.11, 79.12).

details.includes: This division includes the provision of short-term accommodation for visitors and other travellers. The accommodation may include meals, recreational facilities and other services.
details.alsoIcludes: Also included is the provision of short-term accommodation (for example, for students, workers).
details.excludes: This division excludes activities related to the provision of residences in facilities (for example, flats or apartments), typically leased on annual basis, see division 68.

detailled_description:

It primarily focuses on the operation of furnished accommodation facilities that provide professional housekeeping and hospitality amenities.

This category includes, among others, the provision of accommodation in hotels, resort hotels, and suite or apartment hotels (5510). These establishments generally offer daily cleaning and bed-making services, and may provide a range of additional facilities such as food and beverage services, laundry, recreational amenities, and conference or convention facilities (5510).

This category does not include accommodation services that lack daily cleaning, bed-making, and on-the-spot customer service (5520), nor does it include intermediation service activities for the booking or arrangement of accommodation (5590).

Establishments in this category generally operate with minimal or no on-the-spot customer services, such as daily housekeeping or meal services.

This category includes the provision of lodging in a variety of residential-style settings, such as holiday homes and apartments (5520), visitor flats and bungalows (5520), as well as cottages and cabins that do not offer housekeeping services (5520). This division encompasses the provision of food and beverage services designed for immediate consumption, whether through permanent dining establishments, mobile units, contractual arrangements, or specialized intermediation services. The scope is defined by the objective of providing meals and drinks ready for consumption, regardless of the physical setting or the service model employed.

This includes, among others:

*   **Restaurant and Mobile Food Services:** The provision of food to the general public through traditional sit-down restaurants, cafeterias, fast-food outlets, and take-away establishments, as well as food prepared and served from mobile carts, portable stalls, or specialized vehicles (561).
*   **Contractual and Event Catering:** Specialized food service activities provided on a contractual basis to a limited clientele, including event catering for specific occasions, industrial catering, and the operation of canteens, cafeterias, or concessions in settings such as offices, factories, hospitals, and sports facilities (562).
*   **Beverage Serving Activities:** The preparation and service of beverages for immediate consumption on-premises, including bars, pubs, cocktail lounges, coffee houses, tea rooms, and fruit juice bars, as well as beverage services operated by separate units aboard transport vehicles (563).
*   **Intermediation Services:** Activities that facilitate transactions between clients and food or beverage service providers through digital or non-digital channels, including reservation services and brokerage platforms that operate on a fee or commission basis (564).

This division does not include the production of food or meals not intended for immediate consumption (divisions 10 and 11), the retail sale of food or beverages not considered a meal (division 47), the operation of coffee or food vending machines where the preparation is performed by the machine itself (division 47), food delivery services operated by independent units (53.20), or the operation of entertainment venues where beverage service is not the primary activity (93.29).

description: PUBLISHING, BROADCASTING, AND CONTENT PRODUCTION AND DISTRIBUTION ACTIVITIES

details.includes:
This section includes the production and publishing, broadcasting and other distribution of information products.

This section includes: book, newspaper, periodical and software publishing activities (division 58); the production of motion picture, video and television programme elements , sound recording and music publishing activities (division 59); radio and television broadcasting as well as television or radio programme production and distribution activities, including the operation of streaming, downloads and content distribution (sharing) platforms not associated with publishing of the content, the operation of blogs and wiki sites, social network sites and online gaming / video game sites (division 60).

Publishing refers to the acquisition of copyrights to content (information products) and making this content available to the general public by engaging in (or arranging for) the reproduction and distribution of this content in various forms. Publishers may solely publish and then license rights to others to distribute their content, or they may publish and distribute content they create or own. All the feasible forms of publishing (in print, electronic, digital, analogue, or any other form) and self-publishing activities are included in this section.

Individual television programming components (for example, movies, television series) are produced by activities in division 59, while the creation of a complete programme for a television channel, from components produced in division 59 or other components (for example, live news programming), is included in division 60. Division 60 also includes the broadcasting of this programme by the producer.
details.alsoIcludes:
This section also includes:
- the creation and leasing of copyrights for published content
details.excludes:
This section excludes:
- wholesale and retail sale of recorded media, see section G
- activities of providing telecommunication and related service activities, i.e. transmitting voice, data, text, sound and video, computer programming activities, computing infrastructure and hosting activities, and web search portals, see section K
- provision of financial and insurance services using published financial and insurance technologies software, see section L
- the management of copyrights, see 74.91
- rental of discs, see 77.22
- activities of independent musicians and actors (including influencers appearing in vlogs), writers and bloggers, whose content is published by a third party, and gambling sites, see section S

This division encompasses the publishing of information-based products, including books, newspapers, journals, software, and other digital or physical media, characterized by intellectual creativity and copyright protection. These activities involve the acquisition of rights, content development, and the making of such content available to the public through various distribution channels, including print, digital, and streaming platforms.

This division includes, among others:
* **Publishing of Books and Periodicals (581):** The publishing of books, brochures, dictionaries, encyclopaedias, atlases, maps, and charts (5811); newspapers and advertising newspapers (5812); journals, periodicals, and radio/television schedules (5813); and various other works such as directories, mailing lists, catalogues, photographs, greeting cards, posters, and datasets without associated data processing services (5819).
* **Software Publishing (582):** The development, updating, and publishing of video games across all platforms (5821), as well as general-purpose software, including operating systems, business and financial technology applications, cybersecurity software, and modelling software (5829). This also covers intermediation services for software and the operation of digital marketplaces for software downloads.

This division does not include the production of motion pictures, videos, or music recordings (Division 59); the broadcast or distribution of content where rights are obtained from publishers (Division 60); computer programming or software development services performed on a fee or contract basis (Division 62); or the physical printing and mass reproduction of recorded media (Group 18.1 and Class 18.20).

details.includes:

description: Motion picture, video and television programme production, sound recording and music publishing activities
detailled_description:
This division encompasses the complete lifecycle of audiovisual and sound-based media, covering the creation, technical refinement, commercial rights management, distribution, and exhibition of content. It integrates the production of motion pictures, television programmes, and digital video content with the recording and publishing of musical works and master audio productions.

This includes, among others:
* **Audiovisual Production and Exhibition:** The production of theatrical and non-theatrical motion pictures, television programmes, advertising films, and digital audiovisual content (591). This also includes technical post-production services such as film and video editing, dubbing, titling, and format conversion (591), as well as the physical or digital projection of these works in cinemas or other venues (591).
* **Distribution and Rights Management:** The acquisition, buying, and selling of distribution rights for audiovisual works (591), alongside the distribution of these productions to television networks, streaming platforms, and cinema exhibitors (591).
* **Sound Recording and Music Publishing:** The production of original sound master recordings in studio or external environments (592), the promotion and distribution of these recordings, and the music publishing industry, which encompasses the acquisition and registration of copyrights, promotion of musical compositions, and direct distribution to the public via streaming and digital downloads (592).

This does not include the provision of streaming and download services that are not associated with the publishing of content (division 60), the physical reproduction of media from master copies (18.20), or the wholesale and retail sale of audio and video recordings on physical media (section G). Furthermore, it excludes the professional activities of independent actors, musicians, directors, stage designers, and other support activities to the performing arts (section S), as well as the rental of video or audio media to the general public (division 77).

Further included is the buying and selling of distribution rights for motion pictures or other audiovisual productions.

description: Motion picture, video and television programme activities
detailled_description:
This category encompasses the lifecycle of audiovisual content, covering the creation, refinement, commercial distribution, and public exhibition of motion pictures, videos, and television programmes. It includes activities involving professional production, technical post-production, rights management, and the physical or digital projection of works for theatrical, broadcast, or streaming audiences.

This category includes, among others:
*   **Production Activities:** The creation of motion pictures, television programmes, advertising films, and animated audiovisual works, including the production of modern digital content such as vlogs and video podcasts (5911).
*   **Post-Production and Laboratory Services:** Essential technical processes including film and video editing, titling, subtitling, closed captioning, and conversion to streaming formats. This also covers the activities of film laboratories, including the development, processing, and reproduction of motion picture film for cinema distribution, as well as the management of stock footage libraries (5912).
*   **Distribution Activities:** The acquisition of copyrights and distribution rights for audiovisual works, and the supply of these productions to motion picture theatres, television networks, and streaming exhibitors (5913).
*   **Projection Activities:** The operation of motion picture or audiovisual projection services in cinemas, open-air venues, or other exhibition spaces (5914).

This category does not include the mass duplication or reproduction of recorded media from master copies (18.20), the wholesale or retail sale of recorded media (46.49, 47.69), or the rental of DVDs and videotapes to the general public (77.22). It also excludes sound recording and the production of audiobooks (59.20), television broadcasting and the creation of complete channel programming (60.20), and the activities of independent artists such as actors, directors, or cartoonists (division 90). Furthermore, it excludes real-time (simultaneous) closed captioning (82.99), the management of copyrights/royalties (74.91), and general film processing services outside of the motion picture industry (74.20).

description: Sound recording and music publishing activities
detailled_description:
This category encompasses the technical and intellectual processes involved in the creation, production, and commercial management of audio content and musical compositions. It covers the full lifecycle of sound production, from the recording of master tracks to the legal protection, licensing, and distribution of music and audio media.

This includes, among others:
*   **Sound Recording and Production:** The production of original sound master recordings, including digital formats, and the provision of sound recording services for diverse media such as radio, podcasts, television, film, and audiobooks (5920).
*   **Music Publishing and Copyright Management:** Activities related to the acquisition and registration of copyrights for musical compositions, including their promotion, authorization for use in various media (e.g., live performances, broadcasts, print), and the publishing of sheet music (5920).
*   **Distribution and Format Conversion:** The release, distribution, and joint publishing of sound recordings via streaming and download platforms, as well as the technical conversion of recordings into audio streaming formats (5920).

This does not include the physical reproduction of media from master copies (18.20); the wholesale (46.49) or retail sale (47.69) of recorded media; the activities of individual musicians (90.20); or audio streaming and download distribution services that are not associated with music publishing activities (60.10).

description: Programming, broadcasting, news agency and other content distribution activities
detailled_description:
This division encompasses the creation, acquisition, and distribution of media content, including radio, television, and digital information services. It covers the full lifecycle of content delivery—ranging from the assembly of programming to broadcasting and streaming—across various technologies, such as over-the-air transmission, satellite, cable, and internet platforms.

This includes, among others:
* **Radio and Audio Services:** The operation of radio studios and networks, including the broadcasting of aural programming, live podcasts, and on-demand audio streaming or download services (601).
* **Television and Video Programming:** The creation and assembly of television channel programmes, including specialized narrowcast formats and the operation of video-on-demand, video streaming, and live video event broadcasting services (602).
* **News Agencies and Digital Content Platforms:** The professional gathering and syndication of news, photos, and feature stories to media organizations, as well as the operation of social networking sites, wiki sites, blogs, and online gaming or video game distribution sites (603).

This does not include: the physical operation of transmission networks for cable or satellite television (61); the production of motion pictures, videos, or audiovisual works (59); the publishing of software or video games (58); the provision of raw computing infrastructure, web hosting, or web search portals (63); the retail sale of physical media (46, 47); the rental of videodiscs (77); independent creative activities of actors, influencers, or bloggers (90); or the activities of gambling sites (92).

details.includes: This division includes the activities of creating content or acquiring the right to distribute content and subsequently broadcasting or distributing that content. Types of produced or distributed content included in this division are radio, television, audio and audiovisual entertainment, news, talk, etc., including programmes that are typically narrowcast in nature (programmes that appeal to a particular segment of the population, such as news, sport, education, youth-oriented programming). The broadcasting or content distribution can be performed using different technologies, over-the-air, via satellite, via a cable network or via the internet broadcasting, streaming or downloads. This division also includes the broadcasting of live podcasts, third-party on-demand distribution of recorded podcasts and downloads, and activities of news agencies, social network sites, blogs and wiki sites, and online gaming / video game sites. Content may be made freely available to users or may be available only on a subscription or fee basis.
details.excludes: This division excludes: the operation of cable or satellite television transmission networks (division 61); the production of audio and audiovisual recordings (including recorded podcasts), activities of vlog sites and the distribution of motion pictures, videos or audiovisual works and similar productions to motion picture theatres, television networks and stations, and exhibitors (division 59); wholesale/retail sale of audio and video recordings on physical media (divisions 46 and 47); retail sale outlets of newspapers (division 47); videodisc rental (division 77); activities of independent actors (including influencers appearing in vlogs) and independent bloggers (division 90); publishing of video games and other software (division 58); provision of computing infrastructure and hosting activities, and activities of web search portals (division 63); activities of gambling sites (division 92).

description: Radio broadcasting and audio distribution activities
detailled_description:
This category encompasses the broadcasting of audio signals and the distribution of audio content to the public, affiliates, or subscribers through various platforms. It covers the end-to-end operation of transmission facilities and services dedicated to the delivery of sound-based programming.

This includes, among others: 
* **Broadcasting and Network Operations:** The operation of radio broadcasting studios and facilities for the transmission of aural programming, including the activities of radio networks that assemble and transmit content via over-the-air broadcasts, cable, or satellite (Radio broadcasting and audio distribution activities). 
* **Digital and Internet-Based Services:** Radio broadcasting activities conducted over the internet, including internet radio stations, as well as the provision of on-demand audio streaming and download services where the distributor holds the necessary rights. This also includes the broadcasting of live podcasts and radio programme broadcasting that may involve concurrent filming for video broadcast (Radio broadcasting and audio distribution activities).

This does not include the wholesale or retail sale of audio recordings on physical media (46.49, 47.69), the publishing of audiobooks or music/sound recordings (58.11, 59.20), the creative production of radio programming and audio podcasts (59.20), or the provision of technical infrastructure services for audio streaming where the provider does not hold the rights to the content (63.10).

description: Television programming, broadcasting and video distribution activities
detailled_description:
This category encompasses the creation and distribution of television programming, as well as the provision of video streaming services. It covers the full lifecycle of content delivery, from the assembly of channel programming to the transmission of specialized and on-demand video content.

This includes, among others:
*   **Television Programming and Broadcasting:** The creation of complete television channel programmes, utilizing a mix of purchased content (such as movies or documentaries) and self-produced elements (such as news, live reports, and local programming), including both general and specialized narrowcast formats (6020).
*   **Distribution Models:** The broadcasting of content by the producing unit or via third-party transmission facilities, whether provided freely or on a subscription basis (6020).
*   **Video Streaming and Digital Services:** The programming of video-on-demand channels, video streaming and download service activities not associated with publishing, the broadcasting of live performances and events, and the operation of video game streaming sites (6020).

This does not include:
*   The production of individual television programme elements, such as movies, documentaries, talk shows, or commercials (59.11).
*   Video game publishing and the streaming/download distribution activities performed by video game publishers (58.21).
*   The assembly of channel packages and the operation of cable or satellite transmission networks (61.10).
*   The provision of technical infrastructure for video streaming services, data processing, and related activities (63.10).
*   The rental of recorded videos on physical media to the general public (77.22).

description: News agency and other content distribution activities
detailled_description:
This category encompasses the professional activities of news agencies and the operation of various online content distribution platforms that facilitate the sharing, access, and dissemination of information and digital media. It covers both the formal gathering and syndication of news content and the hosting of user-generated or third-party digital content.

This category includes the following activities:
*   **News Agency and Syndication Services:** The gathering, furnishing, and syndication of news, photographs, and feature stories to media organizations, publishers, and broadcasters (60.31).
*   **Content Distribution and Sharing Platforms:** The operation of sites that distribute content produced and edited by users, such as social networking sites and wiki sites, where the operator does not exercise direct editorial control (60.39).
*   **Online Media and Software Provision:** The operation of independent online gaming and video game sites, the provision of e-books (via streaming or download services, when distinct from publishing), and the online distribution of software not associated with its original publishing (60.39).
*   **Blogging and Digital Distribution:** Content distribution activities conducted via blogs and other similar web-based interfaces (60.39).

This group excludes:

*   Broadcasting and audio/video streaming services that hold distribution rights (60.10, 60.20), as well as music and gambling-specific platforms (60.10, 92.00).
*   Technical infrastructure, data hosting, and computing services, such as data processing or web search portals (63.10, 63.91).
*   Independent creative professional services, including those of journalists, photojournalists, actors, and performing artists (74.20, 90.11, 90.20).
*   The activities of libraries and archives (91.1).
*   Intermediation services for transport or accommodation (52.32, 55.40).

description: TELECOMMUNICATION, COMPUTER PROGRAMMING, CONSULTING, COMPUTING INFRASTRUCTURE AND OTHER INFORMATION SERVICE ACTIVITIES

details.includes: This section includes telecommunication and related service activities, in other words, transmitting voice, data, text, sound and video (division 61), computer programming, consultancy and related activities (division 62), and the provision of computing infrastructure, data processing, hosting and other information service activities (division 63).
details.excludes:
This section excludes:
- publishing, broadcasting and content production, including software publishing, post-production services to convert audio and video content into streaming formats and independent third-party provision of on-demand audio and video streaming or download distribution services, see section J

- activities of gambling sites, see 92.00

detailled_description:
This division encompasses the provision of telecommunication and related service activities, specifically the transmission of voice, data, text, sound, and video. It covers activities centered on the transmission of content using wired, wireless, or satellite technologies, without involvement in the creation or alteration of the content itself.

This includes, among others:

*   **Infrastructure Operation and Maintenance:** The operation, maintenance, and provision of access to transmission facilities, including wired, wireless, and satellite telecommunication networks. This involves managing switching facilities, cable distribution systems, and point-to-point communication links (611).
*   **Telecommunication Reselling and Intermediation:** The purchasing and reselling of network capacity, as well as the activities of telecommunication brokers, agents, and mobile virtual network operators (MVNOs). It also covers the provision of telephone and internet access in facilities open to the public (612).
*   **Specialized and Value-Added Services:** The provision of niche communication services such as satellite tracking, telemetry, and the operation of radar stations. It further includes the delivery of internet access over third-party networks, transmission of SMS, MMS, and Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP) services provided by entities that do not own the underlying transmission infrastructure (619).
*   **Content Transmission Services:** The transmission of television signals, including bundled and programmed channels (e.g., IPTV), and services for machine-to-machine communication.

This division does not include the production and post-production of motion pictures, audiovisual media, television programmes, or sound recordings, including services to convert content into streaming formats (division 59). Furthermore, it excludes the activities of broadcasting and the provision of audio and video streaming or download distribution services (division 60), as well as the installation of telecommunication wiring in buildings without operating the transmission facilities (43.21).

details.includes:
This division includes: 
- activities of providing telecommunication and related service activities, i.e. transmitting voice, data, text, sound and video. The transmission facilities that carry out these activities may be based on a single technology or a combination of technologies. The commonality of activities classified in this division is the transmission of content, without being involved in its creation or alteration. In the case of transmission of television signals this may include complete bundled and programmed channels (produced in division 60) into programme packages
- provision of services for machine-to-machine communication
- transmission of audio or video data without having acquired the rights to the audio or video content
details.excludes:
This division excludes:
- motion picture, audiovisual, television programme, and sound recording production and post-production activities, including services to convert audio and video content into streaming formats, see division 59
- activities of broadcasting and provision of audio and video streaming or download distribution services, see division 60

description: Wired, wireless, and satellite telecommunication activities
detailled_description:
This category encompasses the operation, maintenance, and provision of access to telecommunication infrastructure used for the transmission of voice, data, text, sound, and video. It covers activities reliant on wired, wireless, or satellite networks, as well as the management of transmission and switching facilities.

This includes, among others:
*   **Wired and Satellite Infrastructure:** The operation and maintenance of point-to-point communication facilities using landlines, microwave links, or satellite systems, as well as the operation of cable distribution systems for data and television signal transmission (6110).
*   **Wireless Networks:** The maintenance and operation of cellular and other wireless telecommunication networks, including paging systems (6110).
*   **Service Provision:** The provision of internet access by infrastructure operators and the delivery of visual, aural, or textual programming—such as via direct-to-home satellite systems or internet protocol television (IPTV)—as well as the provision of Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP) services by the operator of the infrastructure (6110).

This does not include the installation of telecommunication, computer network, or cable television wiring in buildings (e.g., fiber-optic cabling) without operating the transmission facilities (43.21); the publishing of instant messaging or satellite geolocation applications (58.29); telecommunication reselling or intermediation services (61.20); the provision of internet access in public facilities like internet cafés (61.20); or the provision of Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP) services by entities that do not operate their own transmission facilities (61.90).

description: Wired, wireless, and satellite telecommunication activities

details.includes:
This class includes:
- operating, maintaining or providing access to facilities for the transmission of voice, data, text, sound and video using wired, wireless or satellite telecommunication infrastructure, including:
 • operating and maintaining switching and transmission facilities to provide point-to-point communication via landlines, microwave or a combination of landlines and satellite link-ups
 • operating of cable distribution systems (e.g. for distribution of data and television signals) with or without providing customers with third-party video-on-demand services
 • provision of internet access by the operator of the infrastructure
 • maintaining and operating cellular and other wireless telecommunication networks (including paging systems)
 • delivery of visual, aural or textual programming received from cable networks, local television stations or radio networks to consumers via direct-to-home satellite systems or via internet protocol television (the units classified here generally do not produce programming material)
 • voice over internet protocol (VoIP) provision by the operator of the infrastructure

The transmission facilities that carry out these activities, may be based on a single technology or a combination of technologies.
details.excludes:
This class excludes:
- installation of telecommunication, computer network and cable television wiring in buildings, including fibre-optic wiring without operating facilities for the transmission of data, see 43.21
- publishing of instant messaging or satellite geolocation applications, see 58.29
- telecommunication reselling activities and intermediation service activities for telecommunication, see 61.20
- provision of telephone and internet access in facilities open to the public (e.g. internet cafés), see 61.20
- voice over internet protocol (VoIP) provision, without operating facilities for the transmission of data, see 61.90

description: Telecommunication reselling activities and intermediation service activities for telecommunication
detailled_description:
This category encompasses the reselling of telecommunication capacity and the provision of intermediation services for telecommunication networks. It covers entities that do not operate their own infrastructure but facilitate access to wired, wireless, and satellite telecommunication services.

This category includes, among others:
*   **Reselling Activities:** The purchasing and subsequent reselling of network capacity, as well as the distribution of prepaid calling cards and related services (6120).
*   **Intermediation and Agency Services:** Activities performed by telecommunication brokers and agents acting on behalf of telecommunication carriers or mobile virtual network operators (MVNOs). This includes the sale of mobile telephone service plans and other telecommunication subscriptions (6120).
*   **Public Access Provision:** The provision of telephone and internet access in facilities open to the public (6120).

This does not include the provision of telecommunication services by operators that own or manage telecommunication infrastructure (6110).

- intermediation services for wired, wireless and satellite telecommunication activities, including:

 • selling mobile telephone service plans on an agent basis
 • wireless telephone service plan sales agent activities, selling on behalf of wireless telecommunication carriers

This category encompasses a range of specialized telecommunication activities that do not involve the direct operation of core telecommunications infrastructure. It covers the provision of niche communication services, satellite-based operations, and various internet-based messaging and access services provided over third-party networks.

This includes, among others:

*   **Specialized Telecommunication and Satellite Services:** The provision of specialized applications such as satellite tracking, communication telemetry, and the operation of radar stations. It also includes the operation of satellite terminal stations and facilities that connect to terrestrial communication systems for satellite-based transmission and reception (6190).
*   **Internet and Messaging Services:** The provision of internet access (such as dial-up) over networks not owned or controlled by the service provider, as well as the transmission of text messaging (SMS) and voice over internet protocol (VoIP) services. This also covers advanced data services (SMS+, MMS+) and the provision of SMS push services, such as notification services, banking alerts, and advertising (6190).

This does not include the provision of internet access by operators of telecommunication infrastructure (61.10), or the reselling of telecommunication services and telecommunication intermediation services (61.20).

description: Computer programming, consultancy and related activities
detailled_description:
This division encompasses a comprehensive range of professional activities related to information technology, including the design, development, and maintenance of software, as well as the provision of expert consultancy and operational management for computer systems and infrastructure. description: Financial service activities, except insurance and pension funding
detailled_description:
This division encompasses financial service activities involved in obtaining and redistributing funds, excluding those related to insurance, pension funding, or compulsory social security. It covers a comprehensive spectrum of financial intermediation, ranging from core monetary activities and specialized credit granting to the strategic holding of financial assets and the management of investment vehicles.

This includes, among others:

*   **Monetary Intermediation:** The core functions of the financial system, including central banking operations, the issuance of currency, and the acceptance of deposits and provision of credit by commercial and savings banks, credit unions, and other deposit-taking institutions (Monetary intermediation: 641).
*   **Holding and Financing Activities:** The activities of captive financial entities, such as holding companies that own controlling equity in subsidiaries, and financing conduits established to channel funds within corporate groups (Activities of holding companies and financing conduits: 642).
*   **Trusts, Funds, and Collective Investment Schemes:** Entities organized to pool financial assets—such as securities—on behalf of shareholders or beneficiaries. This cluster includes investment funds, unit trusts, estates, and agency accounts that generate property income without providing management services (Activities of trusts, funds and similar financial entities: 643).
*   **Other Specialized Financial Services:** A wide range of non-depository financial activities, including financial leasing, specialized credit granting (e.g., factoring, trade finance, consumer credit), and own-account investment or hedging activities, such as those performed by venture capital firms and private equity groups (Other financial service activities, except insurance and pension funding: 649).

This division does not include the activities of promotional institutions for economic development that act as the government’s arm for the execution of public policy mandates (84.13), nor does it include insurance and pension funding activities (division 65), the active management of companies (70.10), or fund management activities performed on a fee or contract basis (66.30).

This category encompasses the core activities of monetary intermediation, which involve obtaining funds in the form of transferable deposits or close substitutes—assets fixed in money terms—and the subsequent distribution of these funds through lending or financial clearance. It covers the essential operations of the financial system, ranging from central banking functions to the retail and commercial credit activities of deposit-taking institutions.

This includes, among others:

*   **Central Banking and Monetary Authority:** The management of national currency, including the issuance of banknotes and digital currency; the implementation of monetary policy to control money supply and promote financial stability; the management of international reserves; and acting as the primary fiscal agent for the government (Central banking: 6411).
*   **Deposit-Taking and Lending Activities:** The acceptance of deposits and the provision of credit in various forms, such as loans, mortgages, and consumer credit (Other monetary intermediation: 6419). This category specifically covers the operations of commercial banks, savings banks, credit unions, cooperatives, and postal banking services (Other monetary intermediation: 6419).

This does not include the operation and supervision of financial markets (66.11), financial supervision of insurance and pension funds (66.29), broader financial regulation related to consumer protection or business conduct (84.13), credit-granting activities by non-depository institutions (64.92), credit card transaction processing (66.19), or the activities of international financial organizations (99.00).

description: Activities of holding companies and financing conduits
detailled_description:
This category encompasses the activities of corporate groups' captive financial entities, specifically holding companies and financing conduits established to serve the financial needs of a group. These units act primarily as vehicles for owning subsidiaries or arranging and channeling funds within a corporate structure.

The scope of this category is divided into two main functional areas:

*   **Activities of Holding Companies:** This includes entities whose primary purpose is to hold the assets of one or more subsidiaries by owning controlling levels of equity. These units do not engage in the administration or management of their subsidiaries, nor do they provide other services to the enterprises in which they hold equity (6421).
*   **Activities of Financing Conduits:** This includes entities created by financial or non-financial groups to raise or borrow funds, often on open markets, for the purpose of remitting those funds to a parent or other entities within the same group. This cluster includes captive financial institutions engaged in intragroup lending, as well as "brass plate" companies that primarily manage claims and liabilities toward non-resident units, often characterized by minimal physical presence or employees (6422).

This category does not include:
- Captive factoring and invoicing companies (64.92)
- Own-account investment activities, such as those performed by venture capital companies or private equity firms (64.99)
- Dealing in financial markets on own account (64.99)
- Active management of companies, including strategic planning, decision-making, and administrative services provided by head offices (70.10)
- Activities of shareholding companies that do not own controlling levels of equity (64.32)
- Asset management activities performed on a fee or contract basis (66.30)
- Management services of public funds and public debt (84.11)
- Other specific activities of corporate groups' captive financial entities which are captured under their relevant activity classes.

description: Activities of trusts, funds and similar financial entities
detailled_description:
This category encompasses the activities of legal entities organized to pool securities or other financial assets on behalf of shareholders or beneficiaries without providing management or administrative services. These entities are primarily characterized by the generation of interest, dividends, and other property income, typically maintaining little to no employment and deriving no revenue from the sale of goods or services.

The scope of this category includes the following functional areas:

*   **Collective Investment Schemes:** This covers money market and non-money market investment funds that raise capital by issuing shares or units to the public for investment in financial assets (64.31). This includes open-end investment funds, closed-end investment funds, and various forms of unit and investment trusts.
*   **Trust, Estate, and Agency Accounts:** This includes entities that, while not acting as collective investment schemes, are organized to pool securities, estates, or other financial assets under trust agreements, wills, or agency agreements (64.32). Furthermore, it includes shareholding companies that do not possess controlling levels of equity, as well as venture capital companies that rely exclusively on share financing without receiving management fees.

This category does not include:
*   Activities of entities that earn revenue from the sale of goods or services (classified according to their principal activity, such as NACE divisions 66, 68, or 77).
*   The management of funds (see 66.30).
*   Pension funding (see 65.30).
*   Securitization transactions involving the issuance of financial instruments (see 64.92 and 64.99).
*   Holding companies (see 64.21) or venture capital companies that do not meet the specific criteria of 64.32.

description: Other financial service activities, except insurance and pension funding

It focuses on specialized financial intermediation, credit granting, and investment activities conducted on own account.

This includes, among others:

*   **Financial Leasing:** The provision of assets under contracts where the risks and rewards of ownership are transferred to the lessee, including the leasing of durable goods like vehicles (6491).
*   **Credit Granting:** Non-depository financial intermediation primarily concerned with providing various forms of credit. This includes consumer credit, international trade financing, long-term industrial finance, mortgage lending, factoring, supply chain financing, and the activities of pawnbrokers (6492).
*   **Other Financial Services n.e.c.:** Financial activities focused on fund distribution, hedging, and proprietary trading. This covers the writing of swaps, options, and hedging arrangements; investment activities by venture capital companies and investment clubs; the clearing and settlement of transactions; and own-account trading in financial markets, commodities, receivables, and crypto-assets that involve a corresponding liability (6499).

*   Insurance and pension funding activities (division 65).

*   Operating leasing, which is classified according to the type of goods leased (division 77).
*   Brokerage services, including the trading of securities, commodity contracts, or currency on behalf of others (66.12).
*   Management of investment funds (66.30).

description: Insurance, reinsurance and pension funding, except compulsory social security
detailled_description:
This division encompasses the underwriting of insurance policies, the provision of reinsurance, and the operation of pension funding schemes, excluding mandatory social security. It involves the professional management of financial assets and risk pooling to ensure that claims or future retirement obligations can be met through the investment of collected premiums and contributions.

This includes, among others, the following areas:

*   **Insurance (651):** The underwriting and provision of all forms of life and non-life insurance, including captive insurance activities. This covers life insurance policies and annuities (6511), as well as non-life indemnity products such as accident, health, property, liability, and motor insurance (6512). It involves insurance providers operating on their own account to pool and assume risks.
*   **Reinsurance (652):** Specialized activities involving the transfer and distribution of risk between insurance entities. This includes the assumption of liabilities originally underwritten by primary insurers (6520), including structured or finite reinsurance arrangements designed to manage capital and volatility.
*   **Pension Funding (653):** The administration of financial vehicles designed to secure retirement income, including both defined benefit and defined contribution pension plans (6530). This covers funds established for the employees or members of sponsoring organizations to provide future pension obligations.

This division does not include the provision of insurance-related services on a fee or contract basis, such as the activities of insurance agents, brokers, or claims adjusters (Division 66). It also excludes the management of pension funds on a contract basis (66.30) and the administration of compulsory social security schemes (84.30).

This includes, among others:

*   **Life Insurance (6511):** This covers the underwriting of annuities and life insurance policies, including term and permanent life insurance, as well as policies covering disability income, funeral expenses, and accidental death or dismemberment. It also includes supplementary insurance underwritten in conjunction with life policies—such as insurance against personal injury, incapacity for employment, or disability resulting from accident or sickness—as well as non-cancellable permanent health insurance.
*   **Non-Life Insurance (6512):** This covers a wide range of indemnity and liability products, including accident, medical, health, travel, and legal expenses insurance. It also includes property and casualty coverage (fire and natural forces, motor vehicles, railway rolling stock, aircraft, and maritime transport), freight insurance, financial loss and liability insurance, credit insurance, and workers’ compensation.

description: Activities auxiliary to financial services and insurance activities
detailled_description:
This division encompasses the provision of professional services that support and facilitate financial transactions, insurance operations, and the management of investment funds. These services are provided on a fee or contract basis for third parties, without the service provider taking ownership of the financial assets or liabilities involved in the transactions.

The scope of this division is clustered into the following key areas:

*   **Financial Market Services:** This includes the administration and operation of financial markets, such as stock and commodity exchanges, as well as brokerage and intermediation services. This encompasses securities and investment fund brokerage, currency exchange, mortgage and loan brokerage, and the facilitation of crowdfunding platforms (661).
*   **Insurance and Pension Auxiliary Services:** This covers the intermediation, administration, and technical support necessary for the functioning of insurance and pension systems. It includes the activities of insurance agents and brokers, risk and claims assessment, insurance adjusting, actuarial services, and administrative support for pension and insurance funds (662).
*   **Fund Management Activities:** This includes the professional management of financial portfolios and investment funds on a fee or contract basis. It covers the strategic decision-making and administrative oversight of mutual funds, pension funds, and other pooled investment vehicles, alongside trust and fiduciary services (663).

This division does not include: the actual underwriting of insurance and pension risks (division 65); financial activities conducted on one's own account (division 64); energy exchanges for utility distribution (division 35); the management of real estate (division 68); debt collection and non-performing loan servicing (82.91); appraisal services not related to insurance (74.99); or the management of public funds and public debt (84.11). Additionally, it excludes the publishing of financial market analysis (58.19), private investigation activities (80.01), and the provision of regulatory oversight by central banks or governmental entities (division 84).

It includes the operation of financial markets, the facilitation of securities and commodity trading, and various specialized services such as transaction processing, advisory, and asset management support.

The scope of this category is clustered into the following key areas:

*   **Administration of Financial Markets:** This includes the operation and supervision of physical or electronic marketplaces for financial instruments. This encompasses the administration of securities and stock exchanges, commodity and futures contracts exchanges, and crypto-asset exchanges, as well as the provision of non-central bank financial supervisory services (6611).
*   **Brokerage and Intermediation:** This includes dealing in financial markets on behalf of others, such as stockbroking, securities and investment fund brokerage, and the brokerage of standardised commodity contracts. It also includes currency exchange services, mortgage and loan brokerage, consumer credit intermediation, and the facilitation of equity and debt-based crowdfunding platforms (6612).
*   **Financial Auxiliary and Advisory Services:** This encompasses a broad spectrum of support services, including financial transaction processing and settlement (such as electronic payment services), securities custody, and the tokenization of digital assets. It also covers professional advisory services, including investment and robo-advisory, merger and acquisition advisory, and the validation and mining of crypto-assets deemed financial assets (6619).

This category does not include: energy exchanges for utility distribution (see division 35); the publishing of financial market analysis (see 58.19); activities relating to the management of funds (see 66.30); the administration of markets or supervisory activities specifically for insurance and pension funding (see 66.29); real estate project trading (see division 68); debt collection and non-performing loan servicing (see 82.91); donation-based fundraising (see 82.99); or the trading/brokerage of crypto-assets that do not carry liabilities (see 82.99). Additionally, it excludes financial and market regulation concerning consumer protection or conduct of business (see 84.13), as well as activities performed on one’s own account rather than as a service to others (see division 64).

description: Rental and operating of own or leased real estate

*   **Residential Properties:** The rental and operation of apartment buildings, dwellings, and homes, including the provision of furnished or unfurnished flats for long-term use (annual basis or longer) and the operation of residential mobile home sites for primary residences (6820).
*   **Non-Residential and Industrial Buildings:** The rental and management of office buildings, industrial facilities, warehouses, data centres, hotels (as real estate assets), exhibition halls, retail stores, shopping centres, and various leisure buildings (6820).
*   **Land and Specialized Facilities:** The rental of land, including agricultural and forestry land, as well as the provision of space specifically for animal boarding and the letting of roofs for infrastructure installations, such as solar power systems (6820).

description: Real estate activities on a fee or contract basis
detailled_description:

It encompasses both the intermediation between buyers, sellers, and renters, as well as the administrative and operational management, valuation, and advisory services required for real estate assets.

The scope of this category includes the following areas:

*   **Real Estate Intermediation:** This covers the facilitation of buying, selling, and leasing transactions, whether conducted through traditional channels or digital platforms. *   **Property Management and Operational Support:** This involves the management of real estate properties, including dwellings held in joint ownership, as well as rent-collecting services (68.32).

This division encompasses the provision of professional architectural and engineering services, along with specialized technical testing, analysis, and certification activities.
