This category includes, among others:

*   **Architectural and Engineering Services:** The design and planning of buildings, infrastructure, and industrial systems. This includes architectural consultancy, town and city planning, landscape architecture, and heritage conservation (7111). It also encompasses multidisciplinary engineering design—such as civil, mechanical, electrical, and environmental engineering—as well as project management, technical supervision, and building inspection services (7112).
*   **Surveying and Mapping:** Specialized technical activities including geophysical, seismic, and geodetic surveying, bathymetry, photogrammetry, and the development and revision of cartographic and spatial information (7112).
*   **Technical Testing and Analysis:** The execution of physical, chemical, and analytical testing on diverse materials and products, including strength, durability, and radiographic testing (7120). This cluster also covers the performance testing of machinery and complete systems (e.g., motor vehicles, electronic equipment, and aircraft models), as well as environmental monitoring of air and water quality (7120).
*   **Certification and Inspection Services:** Official product certification, regular roadworthiness testing for motor vehicles, and technical inspections of utility systems like air ducts and pipelines when performed independently of installation or repair services (7120). It also includes forensic laboratory services and food hygiene testing (7120).

This does not include: physical construction, renovation, or retrofitting of structures (Section F); goods handling and weighing (52.25); IT consultancy, software development, or cybersecurity services (Division 62); specialized management consultancy (70.20); research and development in engineering or biological sciences (Division 72); interior decorating and specialized design (Division 74); testing of animal specimens not related to food production (75.00); or clinical medical and dental diagnostic services (Division 86).

This division encompasses systematic creative work, including basic research, applied research, and experimental development, undertaken to increase the stock of knowledge and to devise new applications. It covers a broad spectrum of scientific and scholarly inquiry across all fields of knowledge, including the development and production of prototypes for further improvement.

This includes, among others:

*   **Natural Sciences and Engineering:** Systematic research and development activities focused on scientific inquiry, technological advancement, and interdisciplinary innovation within technical, physical, biological, medical, health, and agricultural sciences (721).
*   **Social Sciences and Humanities:** Scholarly investigations and creative work aimed at acquiring new knowledge within economics, psychology, sociology, law, political science, history, linguistics, philosophy, and the arts (722).
*   **Experimental Development:** Systematic work, drawing on existing knowledge, directed to producing new materials, products, and devices, or improving existing systems and services (721, 722).

This does not include market research and public opinion polling (73.20) or diagnostic DNA sequencing for medical purposes (86.91).

details.includes:
This division includes the activities of three types of research and development:
(1) basic research: experimental or theoretical work undertaken primarily to acquire new knowledge of the underlying foundations of phenomena and observable facts, without particular application or use in view;
(2) applied research: original investigation undertaken in order to acquire new knowledge, directed primarily towards a specific practical aim or objective; and
(3) experimental development: systematic work, drawing on existing knowledge gained from research and/or practical experience, directed to producing new materials, products and devices, to installing new processes, systems and services, and to improving substantially those already produced or installed.

Research and experimental development activities in this division are not to be regarded as ancillary activities. They are subdivided into the two following categories: natural sciences and engineering; social sciences and the humanities.

description: Research and experimental development on social sciences and humanities
detailled_description:
This category encompasses systematic creative work and investigations directed at the acquisition of new knowledge and the development of applications within the realms of social sciences, humanities, and the arts. It covers a broad spectrum of scholarly inquiry, including both disciplinary and interdisciplinary research projects that contribute to the theoretical and practical understanding of human society and culture.

This class includes research and development (R&D) activities focused on social sciences, such as economics, business administration, psychology, cognitive sciences, education, sociology, law, political science, and media and communication (7220). Furthermore, it includes R&D in the fields of humanities and the arts, specifically covering history, archaeology, literature, linguistics, and philosophy (7220). The category also encompasses interdisciplinary research projects predominantly situated within the social sciences and humanities, as well as specialized studies concerning socio-economic relations (7220).

This category does not include market research and public opinion polling, which are classified under class 73.20.

description: Activities of advertising, market research and public relations
detailled_description:
This division encompasses a comprehensive range of professional services focused on the creation, management, and strategic dissemination of commercial messages, as well as the systematic analysis of market data and the management of organizational reputation. It integrates the operational lifecycle of advertising, the analytical processes of market and public opinion research, and the strategic advisory functions inherent in public relations and corporate communication.

This includes, among others:
*   **Advertising Services:** The full-cycle planning, creation, and execution of marketing and advertising campaigns, including the design of outdoor display structures, showrooms, and window dressings; the distribution of promotional materials; and the mediation of advertising space and time through professional media representation (731).
*   **Market and Opinion Research:** The systematic collection, processing, and analytical interpretation of data regarding consumer behaviors, product preferences, market trends, and public attitudes toward social, economic, or political issues, utilizing a variety of qualitative and quantitative methodologies (732).
*   **Public Relations and Communication:** The provision of expert consulting and operational support to businesses and organizations to manage public perception, stakeholder relationships, and strategic communication, including formal lobbying activities and promotional representation (733).

This does not include activities where advertising income is generated as a byproduct of a primary operation (e.g., the publishing of newspapers or periodicals); the direct sale of advertising time or space by media owners; the production of commercial content for film, television, or radio; specialized advertising photography; the manufacturing of physical advertising materials; or the provision of call center services focused solely on the technical execution of telephone interviews.

details.includes:
This division includes the creation of advertising campaigns and placement of such advertising in periodicals, newspapers, radio, television, over the internet or other media, as well as the design of display structures and sites.

These advertising activities are often provided via advertising agencies and media representatives.

This division also includes market and opinion research (for example on the attitudes, values and behaviour of the population and of various socio-demographic and socio-economic groups with regard to economic, social and political issues). It also includes public relations and communication activities.

description: Market research and public opinion polling
detailled_description:
This category encompasses activities related to the systematic collection and analysis of information regarding market trends and public opinion. It focuses on assessing consumer awareness, product development, advertising impact, and sociological research concerning social and political participation.

This class includes, among others, the conducting of market research studies regarding the evaluation and use of goods and services, as well as product development and pricing strategies (7320). Furthermore, it covers studies on media usage and the effectiveness of advertising (7320), alongside opinion research focusing on quality of life, lifestyles, social participation, and political voting behavior (7320). These research activities utilize both qualitative and quantitative methodological orientations, employing diverse survey procedures such as questioning, observation, measurement, and counting through various channels including face-to-face, postal, telephone, and online interviews (7320).

This does not include advertising activities (73.1); public relations and communication services (73.30); or the operation of call centers specifically undertaking telephone interviews on a contract or fee basis (82.20).

description: Other professional, scientific and technical activities
detailled_description:
This division encompasses a wide range of specialized professional, scientific, and technical services that require high levels of expertise but do not fall under traditional domains such as legal, accounting, engineering, research and development, or advertising activities. It covers a diverse array of services, from creative design and linguistic mediation to specialized technical consulting and the management of intellectual property.

This includes, among others:
*   **Specialized Design Activities:** The creative and technical development of products, fashion, graphics, and interior spaces, which integrate functional, aesthetic, and market-driven requirements (741).
*   **Photographic Activities:** A comprehensive range of commercial and consumer photography, videography, film processing, restoration, and digital imaging services, including document microfilming and 3D object scanning (742).
*   **Translation and Interpretation Activities:** Professional linguistic services provided in written, spoken, or signed formats to facilitate communication across different languages (743).
*   **Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services n.e.c.:** A broad residual category that includes the management and brokering of patents, trademarks, and copyrights (7491), as well as specialized consulting in fields like agronomy, environmental impact, and occupational safety. It also encompasses business brokerage (excluding real estate), appraisal of personal property, and the activities of professional agents representing individuals in the arts, sports, and entertainment (749).

This does not include legal and accounting activities (division 69); management consultancy (division 70); architectural and engineering activities, technical testing, and analysis (division 71); scientific research and development (division 72); advertising and market research (division 73); the printing of photographs (18.12); the operation of coin-operated photo machines (96.99); the development or publishing of translation software (58.29, 62.10); the leasing of intellectual property (77.40); real estate brokerage (68.31); or health-related consultation services (86.2).

* **Clinical and Surgical Care:** Direct animal health care, control activities, and medical treatments performed in consulting rooms, surgery rooms, or mobile locations (750: Veterinary activities).
* **Support and Diagnostic Services:** Professional medical evaluation and assistance provided through clinico-pathological and other diagnostic procedures (750: Diagnostic activities; Veterinary assistants and auxiliary personnel).

Furthermore, it excludes the testing and control of animals before slaughter for food safety (see 71.20), scientific research related to animal genetics (see 72.10), and general pet boarding services that do not provide veterinary health care (see 96.99).

Division 77 encompasses the rental and leasing of a wide array of tangible goods and non-financial intangible assets, alongside intermediation services that facilitate these transactions. The division focuses on operating leases where the lessor maintains the economic risk, providing customers with access to assets in exchange for periodic rental or lease payments without transferring ownership.

This division includes, among others:

*   **Motor Vehicles:** The rental and operating leasing of light motor vehicles (passenger cars, motorcycles, motorhomes) and heavy-duty vehicles (trucks, utility trailers) without a driver (771).
*   **Personal and Household Goods:** The rental of recreational and sports equipment (boats, bicycles, ski equipment) as well as various domestic and personal items such as furniture, clothing, jewellery, electronic appliances, and media (772).
*   **Other Machinery, Equipment, and Tangible Goods:** The rental and leasing of specialized industrial and capital assets, including agricultural and construction machinery (tractors, scaffolds), office and computing equipment, transport equipment (airplanes, ships, railway vehicles), and specialized professional instruments (773).
*   **Intellectual Property:** The commercial licensing of intangible assets such as patents, trademarks, brand names, franchise rights, and scientific research results, excluding copyrighted works (774).
*   **Intermediation Services:** Professional services that facilitate the rental and leasing of the aforementioned tangible and non-financial intangible assets, including automotive rental intermediation and general digital or traditional booking platforms that connect users with providers (775).

This division does not include the rental of equipment with an operator (classified under the specific industry sector, such as construction or transport), financial leasing (64.91), the rental of real estate (section M), the streaming of copyrighted content (division 58), or audiobook streaming not associated with publishing (60.10).

details.includes: This division includes the rental and leasing of tangible and non-financial intangible assets and intermediation service activities thereof. For leasing activities, only the provision of operating leases is included in this division. The renter or lessor has the economic risk for the tangible goods and non-financial intangible assets provided, whereas the intermediator has no economic risk for the tangible goods and non-financial intangible assets that are intermediated. In this division, a wide array of tangible goods is concerned (for example, automobiles, computers, consumer goods, industrial machinery and equipment), provided to customers in return for a periodic rental or lease payment.

description: Rental and leasing of personal and household goods
detailled_description:
This category encompasses the rental and leasing of a wide array of personal and household goods intended for use by households or industries. The activities covered typically involve the short-term provision of such goods, though some items may be leased for longer durations.

The scope of this category is divided into two primary areas:

*   **Recreational and Sports Equipment:** This includes the rental of equipment for leisure and athletic activities, such as pleasure boats, yachts, canoes, and sailing boats (provided they are supplied without an operator), as well as bicycles (including those with electrical assistance) and ski equipment (77.21).
*   **Other Personal and Household Goods:** This includes the rental of a broad range of domestic and personal items, such as textiles, clothing, footwear, furniture, pottery, kitchenware, and electrical appliances. It also covers the rental of jewellery, musical instruments, books, journals, plants, flowers, and tools for amateur home repairs. Additionally, this cluster includes the rental of electronic equipment for household use, video games, videotapes, discs, and records, as well as the provision of gazebos and tensile structures when offered without additional services (77.22).

This category does not include the rental of motor vehicles or recreational vehicles (77.1), the rental of office furniture (77.33), or the rental of machinery and equipment related to specific industries or commercial transport (77.34, 77.39). It also excludes the provision of accommodation (55.20, 55.30), the rental of leisure equipment as an integral part of recreational facility operations (93.29), and the operation or publishing of online gaming services (58.21, 60.39).

description: Rental and leasing of other machinery, equipment and tangible goods
detailled_description:
This category comprises the rental and operating leasing of a wide variety of tangible goods, machinery, and equipment, provided that these items are leased without an operator or driver. It covers assets typically used as capital goods by industries, as well as specialized equipment for office, commercial, or event-based applications.

This includes, among others:
*   **Agricultural and Construction Machinery:** The rental of agricultural and forestry machinery and equipment, such as tractors (7731), and construction and civil engineering equipment, including crane lorries, scaffolds, and work platforms without erection or dismantling (7732).
*   **Office and Computing Equipment:** The rental of office furniture, duplicating machines, typewriters, cash registers, electronic calculators, as well as computers and their peripheral equipment (7733).
*   **Transport Equipment:** The rental of air transport equipment, such as airplanes, helicopters, and hot-air balloons (7735); water transport equipment, including commercial ships, boats, and hovercraft (7734); and land transport equipment excluding motor vehicles, such as railway vehicles and caravans (7739).
*   **Industrial, Commercial, and Specialized Goods:** Other capital goods such as engines, turbines, machine tools, mining and oilfield equipment, professional communication and motion picture production equipment, measuring and scientific instruments, medical and hospital equipment, and slot machines (7739). 
*   **Logistics and Event Equipment:** The rental of furniture, power, light, and sound equipment for events, fairs, and exhibitions, as well as the rental of shipping containers, accommodation or office containers, pallets, tires, and animals (7739).

This does not include:
*   Rental of machinery and equipment with an operator (classified under the relevant service industry, e.g., 01.61, 02.40, division 43, 50, or 51).

description: Leasing of intellectual property and similar products, except copyrighted works
detailled_description:
This category encompasses the activities of allowing others to use intellectual property and similar assets in exchange for royalty payments or licensing fees, excluding the leasing of copyrighted works. It covers the commercial exploitation of intangible assets where the owner, who may or may not be the original creator, grants permission for the use, reproduction, or implementation of these assets in business processes, products, or franchises.

This category includes the receipt of royalties or licensing fees for the following:
*   **Industrial and Commercial Rights:** This includes patented entities, trademarks, service marks, and brand names (7740).
*   **Operational and Franchise Rights:** This includes franchise agreements and the use of internet domains (7740).
*   **Exploration and Development Rights:** This includes rights related to mineral exploration and evaluation, as well as rights for designed or developed board games (7740).
*   **Research Assets:** This includes the results of scientific research (7740).

This category does not include the acquisition of rights for the purpose of publishing; the production, reproduction, or distribution of copyrighted works (such as books, software, or films); or the streaming of such content (divisions 58, 59). Furthermore, it excludes audiobook streaming activities not associated with publishing (60.10), the leasing of real estate (68.20), and the leasing of tangible assets (groups 77.1, 77.2, and 77.3).

description: Intermediation service activities for rental and leasing of tangible goods and non-financial intangible assets
detailled_description:
This parent category encompasses professional intermediation services that facilitate the rental and leasing of various tangible goods and non-financial intangible assets by connecting clients with service providers for a fee or commission. These activities are performed by third-party intermediaries who do not themselves provide the rental or leasing services, operating through both digital platforms and traditional non-digital channels.

This category includes, among others:

*   **Automotive Intermediation:** Services involving the mediation of rental and leasing agreements for passenger cars, motorhomes, motorcycles, and trailers (7751). This includes general intermediation, the operation of booking platforms, and specific reservation services for these vehicles.
*   **General Tangible and Intangible Goods Intermediation:** The facilitation of rental agreements for various other tangible assets, including household equipment such as lawn mowers, ladders, and bicycles, as well as non-financial intangible assets (7752). These activities support peer-to-peer or professional-to-consumer exchanges, and revenue may be derived from service fees, commissions, or supplementary income streams such as the sale of advertising space.

This category does not include the direct rental or leasing of these assets, which are classified under their respective rental and leasing codes (e.g., rental of light motor vehicles under 77.11; rental of heavy motor vehicles under 77.12; rental of caravans under 77.39; or rental and leasing of personal and household goods under 77.2). It also excludes units that maintain ownership of machinery, equipment, and other goods that are ultimately rented or leased, which are classified under divisions 77.3 and 77.40.

These intermediation activities can be carried out on digital platforms or through non-digital channels (including face-to-face, door-to-door, telephone, mail, and so on). The fee or commission can be received from either the client or the provider of the rental and leasing service. Revenue for the intermediation activities can include other sources of income (for example, revenues from the sale of advertising space).

description: Temporary employment agency activities and other human resource provisions
detailled_description:
This category encompasses the provision of human resources and the supply of workers to client businesses for specific periods of time to temporarily replace or supplement the client's existing workforce. It covers the administrative and legal responsibilities associated with managing these personnel as the employer of record.

This includes, among others, temporary employment agency activities and various human resource provisions (7820). In these arrangements, the temporary employment agency acts as the employer for the purposes of payroll, taxes, and other fiscal or human resource matters, while the client maintains responsibility for the direct supervision and management of the provided personnel.

In such an employment arrangement, the temporary employment agency or provider of human resources is the employer of the individual workers provided. However, the client is responsible for the supervision of the temporary personnel.

These activities are providing human resources for clients’ businesses. The units classified here represent the employer of record for the temporary employees on matters relating to payroll, taxes, and other fiscal and human resource issues, but they are not responsible for the management and supervision of employees. description: Travel agency, tour operator and other reservation service and related activities

This division encompasses the activities of agencies and operators primarily engaged in the assembly, marketing, and sale of travel packages, alongside specialized reservation and tourism-related support services for the general public and commercial clients. This division encompasses a comprehensive range of professional investigation and security services provided by private operators to businesses, legal entities, and individuals. These activities focus on the protection of people, property, and assets through physical security measures, electronic monitoring, and specialized investigative services.

The scope of this division includes the following functional areas:

*   **Investigation and Physical Security:** This comprises investigative services for private, commercial, corporate, insurance, and criminal matters for the exercise of legal rights. It also covers physical guard and patrol services for premises, as well as the provision of security personnel for the prevention and safety of people at public events and premises open to the public (800).
*   **Asset and Transit Security:** This includes specialized armored car services for the secure pickup and delivery of money, receipts, and other valuable items, as well as passenger and luggage inspection at transit hubs and secure document/data destruction services (800).
*   **Electronic Security and Monitoring:** This covers the operation of electronic security alarm systems (e.g., burglar and fire alarms) and remote monitoring of video surveillance systems. Where the primary activity focuses on monitoring, this also includes the sale, installation, repair, and maintenance of electronic security systems, mechanical or electronic locks, safes, and vaults (800).
*   **Consulting and Emergency Support:** This includes professional security consulting services and the activities of emergency call centers (800).

This division does not include public order and safety activities (policing), information technology security activities (division 62), the installation of security systems without subsequent monitoring, or the retail sale of security equipment without associated security services.

*   **Asset and Transit Security:** This includes specialized services for cash-in-transit, such as armored car services and support for cash collection and deposit, as well as passenger and luggage inspection at airports, railway stations, and similar transit hubs (8001). It also covers secure document shredding and data destruction services (8001).
*   **Electronic Security and Monitoring:** This covers security system services provided via alarm receiving centers (ARC) or security service centers, including remote monitoring and video surveillance of electronic systems (e.g., burglar, fire, and surveillance alarms) and locking devices (8009). When provided in conjunction with monitoring services, this also includes the installation, repair, modification, and maintenance of electronic security systems, mechanical or electronic locks, safes, and vaults (8009).
*   **Consulting and Emergency Support:** This includes the provision of security advice and consulting services, as well as the activities of emergency call and service centers (8009).

This category does not include the installation of security systems without subsequent monitoring (43.21), the retail sale of security equipment without installation or monitoring (47.52), or cybersecurity consulting activities (62.20). Furthermore, it excludes general concierge, reception, or doorman safety services (81.10, 82.10), public order and safety activities (policing) (84.24), specialized security training services (85.59), and standalone key duplication services (95.29).

description: Services to buildings and landscape activities
detailled_description:
This division encompasses a comprehensive range of professional support services dedicated to the operational maintenance, sanitation, and aesthetic management of buildings, industrial sites, transport equipment, and outdoor landscapes. These services provide essential facility upkeep to ensure functional, hygienic, and well-maintained environments for private, commercial, and public clients.

This division includes, among others, the following clusters of activities:

*   **Combined Facilities Support:** The provision of integrated support services within a client’s premises, including general facility maintenance, reception, security-related administrative tasks, and waste disposal (811).
*   **Cleaning Services:** A broad spectrum of professional cleaning activities categorized by technique rather than the type of client served. This includes the general interior and exterior cleaning of buildings (e.g., offices, residential units, factories), specialized technical cleaning of industrial machinery and ventilation ducts, post-construction cleaning, and the maintenance of transport equipment such as trains, buses, and tankers (812). It also covers public and industrial sanitation, including street sweeping, snow and ice removal, bottle cleaning, and professional disinfecting and extermination services (812).
*   **Landscape Service Activities:** The design, planting, maintenance, and ecological restoration of green spaces. This includes the care of parks, gardens, and grounds for public, private, and commercial facilities; the maintenance of vegetation for transport and recreational infrastructure (e.g., sports fields, playgrounds); and environmental protection activities, such as erosion control and the renaturation of ecosystems (813).

This division does not include agricultural pest control (01.61), the maintenance of agricultural land (01.61), or the operation of marine ecosystems (03.30). It also excludes professional landscape architecture and design services (71.11), specialized security guard activities (80.01), administrative conservation of national parks (91.42), the washing of motor vehicles (45.20), or specific laundry services such as carpet, rug, and drapery cleaning (96.10). Furthermore, it excludes the operational management of specific industry-related facilities like hotels, restaurants, or hospitals, which are classified under their respective industry sectors.

details.includes:

This category covers professional activities related to the design, planting, care, and maintenance of managed landscapes, as well as the restoration and protection of natural environments. It encompasses the comprehensive management of green spaces across various private, public, commercial, and industrial sectors, alongside specialized ecological engineering and environmental preservation services.

This includes, among others:
*   **Maintenance of Parks, Gardens, and Grounds:** The planting, care, and maintenance of green spaces for private and public housing, institutional buildings (schools, hospitals, administrative, and religious sites), municipal grounds (parks, green areas, and cemeteries), and industrial or commercial facilities (8130).
*   **Infrastructure and Specialized Greenery:** Management of vegetation for transport infrastructure (highways, railways, waterways, and ports), as well as structural greenery such as roof gardens, facade plantings, and indoor gardens (8130).
*   **Recreational and Water-Based Landscapes:** Development and maintenance of sports grounds (football fields, golf courses), playgrounds, recreational areas, and aquatic landscaping, including basins, ponds, watercourses, and bio-engineered plant sewage systems (8130).
*   **Ecological Preservation and Restoration:** Activities focused on the protection and restoration of landscapes, including noise, wind, and erosion protection. This extends to environmental management, such as the renaturation of ecosystems, creation of species habitats, control of invasive species, and maintenance of sensitive areas like dunes, moors, and wetlands (8130).

description: Office administrative, office support and other business support activities
detailled_description:
This division encompasses the provision of a comprehensive range of day-to-day office administrative services, routine business support functions, and specialized support activities delivered to other organizations on a contract or fee basis. It serves as a broad umbrella for operational and logistical services that assist businesses in maintaining their core activities, managing customer communications, and organizing professional events.

The scope of this division includes the following clusters:

*   **Office Administration and Support:** This includes the performance of day-to-day office functions, such as general office management, receptionist services, financial planning, record-keeping, personnel administration, and secretarial support. It also covers document preparation tasks, including typing, word processing, transcription, proofreading, and letter writing, as well as mailing and postal support services (821).
*   **Customer Communication and Call Centres:** This involves managing business-to-customer communications via inbound and outbound channels, including telephone-based support, web-based contact centres, telemarketing, and market/opinion research interviews (822).
*   **Event Management and Organization:** This comprises the professional planning, promotion, and management of business events, including conventions, trade shows, exhibitions, conferences, seminars, workshops, and various public markets or fairs (823).
*   **Business Support and Intermediation:** This includes specialized intermediation services that facilitate connections between clients and service providers on a fee or commission basis, such as ticket reservation services (824). It also covers a diverse array of specialized support services, including bill and debt collection, credit reporting, packaging and product preparation (bottling, labelling, stamping), fundraising services, court reporting, and various niche administrative logistical tasks (829).

This division does not include services that are better classified as primary business activities or those managed by specialized sectors. Specifically, it excludes:
*   Printing, pre-press, and document storage/archiving services (18.12, 18.13, 52.10, 63.10).
*   Strategic management and consulting, including activities of head offices or shared service centres (70.10, 70.20).
*   Rental of real estate or equipment (68.20, 77.39).
*   Specialized intermediation for sectors such as finance, insurance, telecommunications, energy, travel, or medical and educational services (Section L, 35.40, 61.20, 79.11, 85.61, 86.97).
*   Logistical services incidental to transport (52.26) and courier services (53.20).
*   Organization of cultural, sporting, or personal events (90.39, 93.19, 96.99).
*   Marketing and advertising campaign development (73.11).

This category encompasses the provision of a comprehensive range of day-to-day office administrative and routine business support functions performed for other organizations on a contract or fee basis. It includes activities traditionally carried out by businesses for themselves, such as general office management, document preparation, and specialized support services.

The scope of this category covers the following areas:

*   **General Office Administrative Services:** This includes the provision of combined administrative functions such as reception services, financial planning, billing and record-keeping, personnel administration, and general secretarial support (82.10).
*   **Document and Clerical Support:** This includes document preparation tasks, including editing, proofreading, typing, word processing, transcription, and letter or résumé writing (82.10). It also encompasses the digitalisation of files without further data processing, the formatting of e-books, and the operation of self-service photocopying machines (82.10).
*   **Postal and Mailing Services:** This includes the provision of mailbox rental services and general mailing support such as pre-sorting and addressing (82.10).

description: Organisation of conventions and trade shows
detailled_description:
This category encompasses the professional organisation, promotion, and management of business-oriented and commercial events, including trade exhibitions and professional gatherings. It further includes the management and provision of staff for the facilities hosting these events, provided these services are directly associated with the organisation or management of the events themselves.

This class includes the following types of events:
*   **Business and Commercial Events:** The organisation and promotion of business and trade shows, as well as general or specialised exhibitions (8230).
*   **Professional and Corporate Gatherings:** The coordination of company events, conferences, conventions, seminars, symposiums, and workshops (8230).

This category does not include the erection of exhibition stands or booths (classified in division 43); the organisation of cultural events, such as film or dance festivals (90.39); the organisation of sporting events (93.19); or the organisation of personal ceremonies or celebrations, such as weddings and birthday parties (96.99). This category encompasses a broad range of specialized support services predominantly provided to businesses and organizations on a fee or contract basis. It includes activities related to financial administration, product preparation, and various operational support services not classified elsewhere.

This category includes the following functional areas:

*   **Financial and Credit Support Services:** This encompasses the collection of payments for claims (bill or debt collection), the compilation of information regarding creditworthiness or employment history, rating agency activities, and repossession services (8291).
*   **Packaging and Product Preparation Services:** This includes packaging on a contract or fee basis, such as the bottling of liquids or gases, blister or foil packaging of solids, security packaging of pharmaceuticals, product sterilization, and ancillary services like labelling, stamping, imprinting, parcel packing, and gift wrapping (8292).

description: PUBLIC ADMINISTRATION AND DEFENCE; COMPULSORY SOCIAL SECURITY

details.includes:
This section includes activities of a governmental nature, normally carried out by the public
administration. This includes the enactment and judicial interpretation of laws and their pursuant regulation, as well as the administration of programmes based on them, legislative activities, taxation, national defence, public order and safety, immigration services, foreign affairs and the administration of government programmes.

The legal or institutional status is not, in itself, the determining factor for an activity to belong in this section, rather than the activity being of a nature specified in the previous paragraph. This means that activities classified elsewhere in NACE do not fall under this section, even if carried out by public entities (for example, the administration of the school system – in other words, regulations, checks, curricula – falls under this section, but teaching itself does not (see section Q), while a prison or military hospital is classified to health (see section R)). Similarly, some activities described in this section may be carried out by non-government units.
details.alsoIcludes: This section also includes compulsory social security activities.

description: Public administration and defence; compulsory social security
detailled_description:
This category encompasses the overarching administrative, executive, and legislative functions of government, the provision of essential services to the community as a whole, and the management of compulsory social security schemes. It covers the strategic management of public resources, the maintenance of national security and public order, and the administration of social protection programmes mandated by law.

This includes, among others:

*   **General Public Administration and Policy:** The executive and legislative activities of government bodies at all levels, including fiscal affairs, budget implementation, and the administration of national statistical and planning services. It also covers the regulation of social, economic, and environmental policies, including the support of sectors such as agriculture, energy, infrastructure, and the administration of programmes for health, education, and social services (841).
*   **Provision of Community Services:** The maintenance of societal order and national sovereignty, including foreign affairs, diplomacy, and international aid (8421). It encompasses the administration and operation of national defence forces (8422), as well as the justice system, public safety, policing, and prison administration (8423, 8424). Additionally, it includes the provision of emergency services, such as fire prevention, rescue operations, and civil protection (8425).
*   **Compulsory Social Security:** The funding and administration of government-mandated social protection schemes, including sickness, work-accident, and unemployment insurance, as well as the management of retirement pension funds and income replacement benefits for parental leave or disability (8430).

This does not include central banking activities (64.11); the operation of government-owned buildings (68.20, 68.3); financial services such as private insurance or pension funding (65, 66); legal advice and representation (69.10); research and experimental development (Division 72); or the direct provision of education (Section P), health services (Section Q), or social work services (Division 87, 88). Furthermore, it excludes the activities of libraries, museums, and archives (Division 91), as well as activities of extraterritorial organizations (99.00).

description: Administration of the State and the economic, social and environmental policies of the community
detailled_description:
This category encompasses the overarching administrative, executive, and legislative functions of government at all levels, as well as the regulation and supervision of community policies across social, economic, and environmental domains. It covers the strategic management of public resources, the facilitation of public services, and the promotion of efficient business and social operations through targeted policy implementation.

This includes, among others:

*   **General Public Administration:** The executive and legislative activities of central, regional, and local government bodies, including the operation of ministries, fiscal affairs management (taxation, customs, and duty collection), budget implementation, management of public funds and debt, and the administration of national statistical and planning services (8411).
*   **Social and Community Services Regulation:** The public administration and sponsorship of programmes aimed at enhancing personal well-being, such as health, education, culture, sport, recreation, housing, and social services. This also includes the administration of environmental protection, potable water supply, and waste management programmes, alongside the management of associated research and development (R&D) funds (8412).
*   **Economic Regulation and Business Support:** The regulation and support of economic sectors including agriculture, energy, mining, infrastructure, transport, communication, and tourism. It encompasses the administration of labour affairs, implementation of regional development policies to reduce unemployment, cybersecurity agency activities, and financial regulation for consumer protection and business conduct, as well as R&D policies aimed at improving economic performance (8413).

This does not include central banking activities (64.11), the operation of government-owned or occupied buildings (68.20, 68.3), financial supervisory activities related to insurance and pension funding (66.29) or other financial services (66.11), research and experimental development activities (72), education services (Section Q), human health activities (86), sewerage, refuse disposal and remediation activities (divisions 37, 38, 39), compulsory social security activities (84.30), or the operation of libraries, museums, and archives (division 91).

description: Provision of services to the community as a whole
detailled_description:
This category encompasses the provision of essential public services to the community as a whole, focusing on national security, the administration of justice, public safety, and foreign relations. It covers the institutional framework and operational activities required to maintain societal order, defend the state, and manage international engagement.

This includes, among others:

*   **Foreign Affairs and International Aid:** The administration of diplomatic and consular missions, management of international trade and financial affairs, and the provision of technical or military aid to foreign countries (Foreign affairs, 8421).
*   **Defence and Civil Protection:** The administration and operation of land, sea, air, and space military forces, including logistics, health support for personnel, and the management of civil defence and contingency planning (Defence activities, 8422).
*   **Justice and Public Order:** The operation of courts, judicial systems, and military tribunals, the activities of public prosecutors, and prison administration. It also includes the operation of police forces, border and coast guards, traffic law enforcement, and the provision of emergency supplies for domestic peacetime disasters (Justice and judicial activities, 8423; Public order and safety activities, 8424).
*   **Fire and Rescue Services:** The administration and operation of fire brigades for fire prevention and rescue operations, as well as specialized lifeguard and mountain/water rescue services (Fire service activities, 8425).

This does not include international refugee services (88.99); the activities of extraterritorial organizations (99.00); research and experimental development (Division 72); legal advice and representation (69.10); education (Division 85) or hospital services (86.10) provided by specialized institutions; security activities for private events (80.10); police laboratory operations (71.20); or specialized firefighting services for forestry (02.40), oil and gas fields (09.10), or airports (52.23).

This section includes education at any level or for any profession. The instructions may be oral or written and may be provided by radio, television, the internet or via correspondence.

Education activities are those having an educational programme, a time frame and some evaluation of the knowledge achieved.

This section includes formal initial education at its various levels provided by institutions in the regular school system designed for students as a continuous educational pathway before their first entrance into the labour market, as well as formal education outside the regular school system with programme content and qualifications that are equivalent to those of such initial education (adult education, literacy programmes, and so on).

Also included are activities provided at their respective levels by military schools and academies, prison schools, and so on.

This section includes compulsory and non-compulsory schooling, as well as public and private education.

For each level of education, special education for physically or mentally disabled persons is included.

Groups 85.1 to 85.4 take into account the formal education activities provided under the international classification of educational programmes (ISCED-P 2011 classification). The breakdown of the categories in this section is based on the level of education offered as defined by the levels of ISCED-P 2011*. The activities of educational institutions providing courses at ISCED-P 2011 Level 0 are classified in class 85.10, at ISCED-P 2011 Level 1 in class 85.20, at ISCED-P 2011 Level 2 category 24 and Level 3 category 34 in class 85.31, at ISCED-P 2011 2011 Level 2 category 25 and Level 3 category 35 in class 85.32, at ISCED-P 2011 Level 4 in class 85.33 and at ISCED-P 2011 Levels 5 to 8 in group 85.4.

Educational institutions classified in groups 85.2 to 85.4 are authorised to certify successful completion of an educational programme, usually in the form of a document officially recognised by the relevant national education authorities.

This category encompasses the provision of education at all levels, spanning from initial pre-primary instruction to advanced tertiary academic and vocational degrees, as well as non-formal education and supporting administrative or advisory services. It covers the entirety of the formal educational system, structured lifelong learning pathways, and specialized supplementary training intended for personal, hobby, or professional development.

This includes, among others:
*   **Formal Education Systems:** The provision of structured instruction across all stages, including pre-primary schooling (851), primary education (852), secondary and post-secondary non-tertiary education (853), and tertiary academic or vocational education leading to recognized degrees and qualifications (854). This includes both standard curriculum-based instruction and equivalent programmes for adults or individuals reintegrating into the education system (852, 853, 854).
*   **Non-Formal and Specialized Education:** Intentional, planned learning activities that fall outside the formal school system, including sports and recreational instruction (8551), artistic and cultural training (8552), driving and transport-related training (8553), and other specialized tutoring, language, or skill-based courses (8559).
*   **Educational Support Services:** Professional services that facilitate the educational process, including intermediation between educators and learners (8561), as well as educational consulting, career guidance, curriculum development, and standardized testing or evaluation services (8569).

This does not include child day-care activities (88.91); non-formal education or training provided as part of specific commercial, sports-club, or social work activities (e.g., 85.5, 93.12, 93.13, 88.10, 88.99); or research and experimental development on social sciences and humanities (72.20).

It covers both standard elementary instruction within the school system and equivalent educational programmes designed for adults or individuals who have missed the opportunity for conventional primary schooling.

This includes, among others:
*   **Fundamental Academic Instruction:** The delivery of coursework aimed at developing core literacy and numeracy skills, alongside an elementary understanding of subjects such as history, geography, natural science, social science, art, and music (8520).
*   **Equivalent Educational Programmes:** The provision of programmes for students past the typical age for primary schooling, including adult literacy, second-chance education, and academic reintegration programmes (8520).

This does not include:
*   Non-formal education and training, irrespective of the age of the student or the subject matter (85.5).

This category encompasses the provision of secondary and post-secondary non-tertiary education, bridging the gap between compulsory schooling and higher education. It covers both general and specialized academic programs, as well as vocational training designed to prepare individuals for employment or further study.

This group includes:

*   **General Secondary Education (8531):** Programs that provide a foundation for lifelong learning, covering both lower and upper secondary levels. This includes curriculum-based instruction by specialized teachers, designed to prepare students for entrance to higher education or technical/vocational paths.
*   **Vocational Secondary Education (8532):** Programs emphasizing subject-matter specialization through both theoretical and practical instruction for present or prospective employment. This includes vocational schools for specific trades (e.g., tourism, culinary arts, cosmetology, computer repair) and specialized occupational training, such as instruction for professional drivers (trucks, buses, coaches), forklift operators, and pilots (including drone pilots).
*   **Post-Secondary Non-Tertiary Education (8533):** Programs that, while occurring after secondary education, do not meet the criteria for tertiary or higher education. This includes supplementary programs that bridge the gap for students transitioning to tertiary education or pursuing specific post-secondary vocational qualifications.
*   **Adult and Reintegration Programs:** Educational offerings provided within or outside the formal school system that are equivalent in content to secondary education but are targeted at individuals past the traditional school age. This includes adult literacy programs and second-chance or reintegration education.

This does not include non-formal education and training (85.5); performing arts instruction for recreation, hobby, or self-development purposes (85.52); driving schools not intended for occupational drivers (85.53); technical and vocational higher education (85.40); or job training provided as part of social work activities without accommodation (88.10, 88.99).

Tertiary education encompasses formal academic, professional, and vocational instruction provided at post-secondary levels, leading to the attainment of recognized degrees and professional qualifications. This category covers the range of academic pathways from short-cycle practical programs to advanced doctoral research and specialized postgraduate studies.

This class includes, among others:

*   **Academic and Professional Degree Programs:** Provision of education at various levels, including short-cycle studies (ISCED-P 2011 Level 5), first-cycle/bachelor’s degree programs, second-cycle/master’s degree programs, comprehensive master’s degree courses, and third-cycle doctoral studies (Tertiary education 8540).
*   **Specialized and Vocational Higher Education:** Higher vocational and professional training programs, including those leading to master craftsman qualifications, as well as education activities conducted by performing arts schools providing tertiary-level qualifications (Tertiary education 8540).
*   **Continuing and Flexible Learning:** Adult and continuing education programs that are equivalent in complexity and content to the tertiary-level education described, as well as studies conducted on a full-time or part-time basis (Tertiary education 8540).

This does not include non-formal education and training (see 85.5).

details.includes:
This class includes the furnishing of tertiary academic, professional and vocational courses and the granting of degrees at short-cycle, bachelor’s or equivalent level, master’s or equivalent level, and doctoral level.

This class includes education in public and private universities provided at the level of:
- short-cycle studies, usually based on practical learning appropriate to the performance of a given profession and preparing students for entry into the labour market or other higher education programmes
- first-cycle studies open to applicants with a secondary school leaving certificate and leading to a first-degree qualification
- second-cycle studies open to applicants holding at least a first-cycle qualification and leading to a second-cycle qualification
- comprehensive master’s degree courses open to applicants holding a secondary school leaving certificate and leading to a second-cycle qualification
- postgraduate studies open to applicants who have completed at least first-cycle studies and leading to a postgraduate qualification
- third-cycle studies (training for doctoral students) open to applicants holding at least second-cycle studies and leading to a third-cycle qualification

Education may be conducted as full-time or part-time studies.
details.alsoIcludes:
This class also includes:

detailled_description:
This category encompasses non-formal education and specialized training that falls outside the formal school and tertiary education systems. It focuses on intentional, planned learning activities for personal development, hobby enhancement, or professional improvement, typically provided through short courses, workshops, or seminars that do not lead to formal academic qualifications.

This scope includes several distinct clusters of instruction:
*   **Sports and Recreational Education:** The provision of athletic instruction, including gymnastics, swimming, martial arts, riding, yoga, Pilates, and board/e-sports training (8551).
*   **Cultural and Artistic Education:** Instruction in the arts, such as music, dance, drama, fine arts, and photography, primarily for hobby or self-development purposes (8552).
*   **Driving and Specialized Transport Training:** Education activities provided by driving schools, as well as flying, sailing, and shipping schools that do not issue commercial certificates or professional licenses (8553).
*   **Other Specialized Education (n.e.c.):** A wide range of diverse educational services including academic tutoring, remedial courses, professional examination preparation, language instruction, computer and programming training, as well as various lifestyle and specialized skill courses such as sewing, oenology, meditation, and survival training (8559).

These activities are provided by various entities, including schools, camps, studios, and independent professional instructors or tutors.

This group excludes formal educational activities, such as pre-primary, primary, secondary, and tertiary education (groups 85.1 to 85.4). It also excludes specialized sports training provided by sports clubs (93.12), fitness instruction offered by commercial fitness centers (93.13), and vocational training that leads to professional commercial certificates or permits (85.32). Additionally, it does not include formal adult literacy programmes or entertainment-focused activities in care facilities.

details.includes:
This group includes education (including non-formal) which is neither part of initial education in the regular school system, nor equivalent in programme content and qualifications to those programmes. It includes training for any professional, hobby or self-development purposes for both children and adults, including non-formal continuing vocational education and training. Non-formal education is defined by ISCED-P 2011 as institutionalised, intentional and planned by an education provider, as an addition, alternative and/or complement to formal education within the process of an individual’s lifelong learning. It targets people of all ages but does not necessarily apply a continuous pathway/structure; it may be short in duration and/or low-intensity, and it is typically provided in the form of short courses, workshops or seminars.

This group includes the provision of athletic instruction to groups or individuals, foreign language instruction, instruction in the arts, drama or music, as well as other instruction or specialised training provided by camps and schools, not comparable to the education in groups 85.1 to 85.4.
details.alsoIcludes: This group also includes education activities run by self-employed / own account / individual / independent lecturers (tutors, academics, instructors).
details.excludes: This group excludes formal educational activities as outlined in groups 85.1 to 85.4, in other words, pre-primary education, primary education, secondary education, post-secondary non-tertiary education or tertiary education.

details.includes:

This category encompasses a range of professional and administrative services that support educational processes, systems, and the facilitation of learning-related transactions. It covers both the intermediation between educators and learners and the provision of non-instructional, specialized advisory and evaluative services.

This category includes the following functional areas:

*   **Intermediation Services:** This includes services dedicated to bringing clients and educational service providers together for a fee or commission, whether through digital platforms or traditional, non-digital channels (8561).
*   **Educational Support and Consulting:** This includes the provision of non-instructional activities aimed at supporting educational systems, such as educational and career-related counselling, guidance counselling, and educational consulting (8569).
*   **Evaluation, Testing, and Curricular Development:** This includes activities related to the development of curricula, the organization of student exchange programmes, as well as educational testing and evaluation services, including the examination of regulated professions (e.g., pilots) and expert assessment of learning abilities (8569).

This category does not include research and experimental development on social sciences and humanities (72.20).

description: HUMAN HEALTH AND SOCIAL WORK ACTIVITIES

details.includes: This section includes the provision of a wide range of health and social work activities. These activities can be exercised by private or public service providers.

detailled_description:
This division encompasses the provision of comprehensive human health care services, ranging from acute inpatient hospital treatment to specialized outpatient medical, dental, and paramedical practices. It covers a broad spectrum of diagnostic, curative, rehabilitative, and preventive activities aimed at maintaining or improving the health of individuals.

This division includes, among others:

*   **Inpatient and Hospital Care:** The activities of general and specialized hospitals (including mental health, university, and prison hospitals) that provide diagnostic and medical treatment requiring accommodation, alongside support facilities such as laboratories, operating rooms, and pharmacy services (86.1).
*   **Medical and Dental Practice:** Professional medical consultation and treatment provided by general practitioners and medical specialists, as well as general and specialized dental practices, including orthodontics and oral pathology, conducted in various settings such as private offices, outpatient clinics, or at the patient's home (86.2).
*   **Paramedical and Specialized Health Services:** The activities of health professionals other than hospitals or doctors, including nursing and midwifery services, physiotherapy, occupational therapy, and psychological services (86.9).
*   **Diagnostic and Supportive Health Activities:** Independent medical laboratory services (e.g., blood analysis, imaging), emergency patient transport services, and the management of biobanks (blood, sperm, transplant organs), as well as services for traditional, complementary, and alternative medicine (86.9).

This division does not include veterinary activities (75.00), the manufacturing of medical or dental prosthetics (32.50), residential nursing care facilities (87.10), homecare services (88.10), or non-medical cosmetic and beauty treatments (96.22, 96.23).

details.includes:
This division includes activities of short- or long-term inpatient health care. It covers general and specialty medical/surgical care offered by hospitals, preventoria, medical nursing homes, mental hospital institutions, rehabilitation centres and other human health institutions which have accommodation facilities and which engage in providing diagnostic and medical treatment to primarily inpatients, with a wide range of medical conditions.

This division also includes medical consultation and treatment in the field of general and specialised medicine, by general practitioners and medical specialists and surgeons. It includes dental practice activities of a general or specialised nature, as well as orthodontic activities.

Additionally, this division includes medical, curative, rehabilitative or prevention activities by paramedical practitioners and health professionals other than hospitals or practicing medical doctors.
details.alsoIcludes: This division also includes other human health activities (for example, activities of medical laboratories, blood banks, sperm banks, transplant organ banks, and so on, including collecting, processing, storing and shipping).
details.excludes:
This division excludes:
- veterinary activities, see 75.00

detailled_description:
This category encompasses medical and diagnostic hospital activities performed by legally recognized institutions for human health. It covers a broad spectrum of services provided to inpatients, including medical care, specialized accommodation, and the support facilities necessary for hospital operations.

This category includes, among others:
*   **Inpatient Medical and Treatment Services:** The provision of short- or long-term medical, nursing, and health services by general and specialized hospitals, including community, regional, university, military, and prison hospitals (86.10).
*   **Specialized Hospital Facilities:** Activities of mental health and psychiatric hospitals providing diagnosis and medical treatment (86.10).
*   **Clinical and Supportive Hospital Operations:** Services carried out under the supervision of medical doctors, such as the activities of medical and paramedical staff, laboratory and technical facilities (including radiologic and anaesthesiologic services), emergency room operations, operating room services, pharmacy services, and food/hospital support services (86.10).
*   **Specialized Health Centers:** Activities of family planning centers that provide medical treatments requiring accommodation, such as sterilization or termination of pregnancy (86.10).

This does not include:
*   Laboratory testing and inspection of materials and products (other than medical laboratory testing) (71.20) or veterinary activities (75.00).
*   Health activities for military personnel in the field (84.22).
*   Private medical or dental consulting services provided by professionals outside of the hospital framework (86.2, 86.23).
*   Independent diagnostic imaging services and medical laboratories that are not integrated into hospital activities (86.91).
*   Independent patient transport services by ambulance (86.92).

The activities are chiefly directed to inpatients, are carried out under the direct supervision of medical doctors and include:
- activities of medical and paramedical staff
- activities of laboratory and technical facilities, including radiologic and anaesthesiologic activities
- emergency room activities
- provision of operating room services, pharmacy services, food and other hospital services

This category encompasses medical and dental consultation and treatment services provided by legally recognized practitioners, ranging from general medicine to specialized medical and dental care. These activities may be conducted in various settings, including private or group practices, hospital outpatient clinics, businesses, schools, residential care facilities, or through home visits.

The scope of this category includes:

*   **General Medical Practice:** Medical consultation and treatment provided by general practitioners (8621).
*   **Specialized Medical Services:** Consultations and treatments in fields of specialized medicine and surgery, including psychiatric services, cosmetic surgery, and family planning clinics (8622). This cluster also covers specialized outpatient and day-clinic treatments such as dialysis, chemotherapy, radiation therapy, and respiratory treatments, as well as the interpretation of diagnostic medical imaging and the operation of vaccination and thrombosis centers (8622).
*   **Dental Practice Activities:** General and specialized dental care, including orthodontics, endodontics, pediatric dentistry, and oral pathology, as well as dental procedures performed in operating rooms (8623).

This category does not include inpatient hospital activities (86.10), nursing and midwifery activities (86.94), physiotherapy activities (86.95), or the practice of traditional, complementary, and alternative medicine (86.96). Furthermore, it excludes the manufacturing of dental prosthetics by laboratories (32.50), the professional activities of dental paramedical personnel (86.99), and cosmetic beauty treatments provided by non-medical personnel (96.22).

details.includes:

These activities can be carried out in private practice, group practices, hospital outpatient clinics and in clinics attached to businesses, schools, homes for older persons, labour organisations and fraternal organisations, as well as in patients’ homes.

detailled_description:
This category encompasses a broad range of human health services provided by paramedical practitioners and other health professionals, excluding services provided by hospitals or practicing medical doctors. It covers a diverse array of medical, curative, rehabilitative, and preventive activities that do not involve the provision of accommodation services.

This category includes the following functional areas:
*   **Diagnostic and Laboratory Services:** Medical laboratory activities, including blood analysis, genetic testing, and diagnostic imaging services such as X-ray centers and doping control (8691).
*   **Emergency and Specialized Patient Transport:** Ambulance services for patient transport that involve the presence of paramedical staff and lifesaving equipment (8692).
*   **Mental Health and Therapeutic Services:** Consultation and treatment provided by psychologists, psychotherapists, and music therapists (8693), as well as physical therapies including physiotherapy, occupational therapy, and medical massage (8695).
*   **Nursing and Midwifery:** Nursing and midwifery services provided by independent practitioners in consulting rooms or at the patient's home, including palliative care (8694).
*   **Traditional and Alternative Medicine:** Health services based on traditional, complementary, or alternative practices, such as acupuncture, homeopathy, chiropractic treatments, osteopathy, naturopathy, and the activities of healers (8696).
*   **Intermediation Services:** Services that connect patients with health providers through digital or non-digital platforms, including appointment booking for medical and dental care (8697).
*   **Other Specialized Health Activities:** A residual category for health-related services, including speech therapy, podiatry, orthoptics, dietetics, and the operation of biobanks (blood, tissue, sperm, and organ banks). It also covers specific bodywork techniques such as shiatsu and Thai massage, as well as art, dance, and animal-assisted therapies (8699).

This does not include: non-medical laboratory testing (71.20); hospital activities (86.10); medical and dental practice activities (86.2); residential nursing care facilities (87.10); homecare services (88.10); the production of artificial teeth or prosthetics (32.50); or non-medical massage salons (96.23).

This division encompasses the provision of residential care services combined with nursing, supervisory, or other forms of assistance required by residents. It involves a integration of health and social services, typically provided in facilities specially built or adapted for specific target groups, where residents may stay on a permanent or temporary basis.

This includes, among others, the following clusters of activities:

*   **Residential Nursing and Medical Care:** The provision of inpatient nursing, medical diagnostics, rehabilitation, and palliative care in facilities with a permanent core staff of healthcare professionals (871).
*   **Specialized Residential Care for Mental Health and Substance Abuse:** Protective supervision, counseling, and rehabilitation services for individuals diagnosed with mental illness, intellectual disabilities, or substance abuse issues in non-hospital settings (872).
*   **Residential Care for Older Persons and Persons with Physical Disabilities:** Provision of room, board, and personal support services, including assisted living and residential care for those who require daily living assistance but do not necessitate intensive, continuous nursing care (873).
*   **Other Residential Social Assistance:** The operation of residential facilities providing 24-hour social support for groups such as orphans, children in boarding homes, homeless persons, refugees, and individuals in correctional or family support settings, as well as intermediation services for residential care placements (879).

This division does not include non-residential nursing activities (86.94) or non-residential social care and support activities (division 88).

This category encompasses the provision of residential care services that integrate medical, nursing, and rehabilitation treatments within a stable environment. These establishments are characterized by a permanent core staff of registered or licensed practical nurses who deliver ongoing health-related support alongside personal care services.

This includes, among others:
*   **Residential Nursing Facilities:** The provision of nursing care, medical diagnostics, medication administration, and wound dressing (Nursing care facilities, Nursing homes/hospices).
*   **Specialized Residential Care:** Facilities providing long-term health monitoring and recuperative services (Homes for older persons with nursing care, Convalescent homes, Rest homes with nursing care).
*   **Palliative and End-of-Life Care:** Dedicated inpatient hospice services focused on palliative care (Inpatient care hospices for palliative care).

This does not include:

description: Libraries, archives, museums and other cultural activities

This division encompasses the professional activities related to the identification, collection, inventory, management, and conservation of cultural, historical, and natural heritage. It includes the operation of institutions that preserve and provide access to informational, archival, and museum collections, as well as the maintenance of significant cultural sites and the protection of natural environments.

This includes, among others:

*   **Library and Archive Activities:** The professional management, cataloguing, and provision of access to informational, cultural, and historical collections, including the operation of reading, listening, and viewing rooms, as well as the acquisition, preservation, and classification of public and private digital and physical archival records (911).
*   **Museum and Heritage Site Operations:** The care, exhibition, and public interpretation of diverse collections, including art, history, science, and ethnography, alongside the management of historical buildings, gardens, landscapes, and archaeological sites (912).
*   **Conservation and Restoration Services:** Specialized technical activities dedicated to the physical preservation and restoration of historical and archaeological assets, including expert advisory services and the digitization of heritage for virtual documentation (913).
*   **Botanical, Zoological, and Nature Preservation:** The operation and management of botanical gardens, zoological gardens, aquariums, and wildlife parks, as well as the ongoing maintenance and conservation of nature reserves and protected wilderness areas (914).

This division does not include: the manufacture or repair of non-historical musical instruments (32.20, 95.29); the renovation, reconstruction, or retrofitting of historical and archaeological buildings (43.99); the retail sale of paintings, sculptures, or second-hand goods (47.69, 47.79); transport and storage activities (division 52); insurance activities (division 66); architectural services for heritage conservation (71.11); scientific research and development, including archaeological excavation and conservation sciences (division 72); activities of tourist guides and lecturers (79.90); or sports, amusement, and recreation activities, such as bathing beaches and recreation parks (division 93).

description: Museum, collection, historical site and monument activities
detailled_description:
This category encompasses the operation, management, and preservation of cultural heritage, covering a broad spectrum of both movable collections and fixed heritage sites. It focuses on the care, exhibition, and public interpretation of cultural, historical, and natural assets, whether managed by public institutions or private entities.

This group includes, among others, the following activities:

*   **Museum and Collection Management:** The operation, care, and exhibition of diverse museum collections, including art, applied arts, crafts, and design (e.g., jewelry, costumes, ceramics). It also encompasses natural history, science and technology, and historical (including military) museums, as well as open-air, ecomuseums, and digital or virtual museums. This extends to the management of collections within historic houses, national galleries, and ethnographic or folk art interpretation centers, as well as the activities of art galleries that exhibit works without engaging in commercial sales (9121).
*   **Historical and Archaeological Preservation:** The operation and maintenance of cultural heritage places resulting from human intervention, including historical buildings, gardens, landscapes, and archaeological sites that are open to public visitation (9122).

This group does not include:
*   Renovation, renewal, reconstruction, or retrofitting of historical and archaeological sites and buildings (43.99).
*   Architectural activities specifically focused on the conservation and restoration of cultural heritage properties (71.11).
*   Archaeological excavation activities (72.20).
*   Library and archive activities (91.11, 91.12).
*   Direct conservation and restoration works performed on cultural heritage items (91.30).
*   Commercial retail sale of paintings and sculptures (47.69) or the repair of non-historical furniture (95.24).

description: Botanical and zoological garden and nature reserve activities

This category encompasses the operation and maintenance of facilities dedicated to the preservation, display, and study of flora and fauna, as well as the management of protected natural areas. It covers both managed gardens and large-scale conservation zones aimed at wildlife protection and environmental maintenance.

This includes, among others:

*   **Botanical and Zoological Gardens (9141):** The operation of botanical gardens, zoological gardens, children’s zoos, and aquariums.

This does not include landscape and gardening activities (81.30), the operation of sport fishing and hunting preserves (93.19), or protection and restoration activities related specifically to agricultural land (Division 01) or forestry land (Division 02).

description: Sports activities and amusement and recreation activities
